chapters.title: Chapter 5530: Existence!
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
The last thread of the Curse tore free of Hvitrmarr's existence, and in the exact instant it left…Noah stretched that instant into infinity.
Everything froze.

The expelled obsidian hung motionless in its pillar far above. The endless blue paused mid-flood through nine reborn Organs! The falling snow beyond the White Steed's frame stopped in the sky like scattered stars, and within the vaulted stillness of a frozen moment, THE True Human Emperor simply floated there, and sensed his existence.
He did not count. He did not calculate! For once, he only felt.
And in that frozen moment, two presences moved.

They were the only things in all the stillness permitted to move, for they were fused into the very self doing the stretching, and Ruination and THE Infiniverse came to him simultaneously, without a single word, and hugged him.

Ruination's illusory form wrapped around him from one side, her strings folding over his shoulders like a mantle! THE Infiniverse pressed in from the other, her arms tight around the new body she had guarded the seeds of, her face buried against him, and neither of them said anything at all, because there was nothing to say that their grip was not already saying! He had died. They had watched, from inside his splitting halves, shielded by his ending, and no protocol and no composure in either of them had survived the memory of that silence!
Noah smiled softly.
He raised his new hands, and patted both of their heads.
"I am sorry." His voice was quiet in the frozen vault. "I will try everything humanly possible…to not have something like that happen again."

He did not promise it would never happen. They would have known the lie! He promised the trying, which was the only thing a Human could honestly promise, and the two of them heard the honesty inside it and hugged him tighter while nodding against him, crown and existence holding their Emperor in a moment stretched wide enough to hold all three!
And Noah smiled, and turned his senses inward, into the body that held them.
His new body!

Regrown from the Root with so much Primeval weaving that it hardly remembered what it had replaced, every bone and channel and sea woven from Primeval Osmontian Cells, and everything felt so unfathomably light! His will moved through himself without a single seam of resistance, thought arriving as action, intention arriving as fact!
And his Causes…
His Causes felt unfathomably grander!

All nine of them turned through his existence with a depth they had never carried, and he could feel WHY, for they were no longer only his! Each one was mixed now, married through nine reborn Organs to nine First Causes seated by the hands of Those Who Remain, and through those marriages, something was flowing back!

His Prime Cause of Existence carried a new note of sworn permanence from its union with Fealty! Adversity hummed with Valor's charge-drawn breath! Tyranny had learned something from Mercy's gentled claws, and Apocalypse from Temperance's discipline, and all nine of them were visibly, actively undergoing a change, an evolution in slow glorious progress, growing grander with every moment they mingled with the First weavings of a Steed!
And when he looked at the whole of his existence together, he was shocked, as the prompts began.
|For enduring tremendous adversity, for dying within it and returning through it, and for completing what you began at the cost of everything: +25,000,000 Osmontian Biomass has been gained.|
Twenty-five MILLION!

|All facets of your existence have been automatically upgraded to Rank B Ngetal. Osmontian Source Infinity aside, your Volume, your Output, your Trueness, and your Foundations now stand at the rank of reach and pervasion as their floor.|

|And above the floor, Master: your Second Foundation, THE Tide That Owes Nothing, your Intent, THE Ananke Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian, and your Osmontian Source Infinity have elevated to Rank A Idho. Near-permanence. Authority over endings. The rank your fused peak could only pretend toward, now standing as your base.|

|Your True Appendages have also been reborn alongside your body, and further elevated. THE Estuary Eye: Rank A Idho. THE Pinion Vigil: Rank A Idho. THE Hepatarch of the Undying Root: Rank A Idho, exhausted but grander for its work. THE Primeval Osmontian Marrow: Rank A Idho. THE Amaranthine Heart, THE Circlet, THE Quintessential Pantheon of THE Infiniverse: Rank A Idho. All of them stand at the rank of Yew, Master. Every instrument you carry is now an authority over endings.|

|For reference, as you will ask: elevation to Rank S Ebad is priced at 100,000,000 Osmontian Biomass per facet. The trembling shield-tree does not come cheaply. Reserves currently stand above 25,500,000.|
Prompts of majesty and wonder pulsed!
Noah floated in the stretched stillness with his crown and his Observable Existence in his arms, and took all of it in, and for a long moment of the infinite moment, he simply…reflected.

He had died. He had stood in a sea of his own dead and been asked the question that every ruler owes and almost none ever answer, and he had answered it honestly. He had felt fear, and it had not broken him. He had felt doubt, and climbed through it!
The Root that saved him was spent. The door behind him was closed, and death, for the first time in his existence, was again a thing with consequences.

And somehow, that made all of it heavier, and all of it brighter at once! To climb without a net was simply…to be Human again. He had asked, once, on a golden island, whether immortality violated being human.
Existence, apparently, had heard the question.
And it was amidst this reflection that the prompts returned, and their tone had changed.
|Master. THE Tide That Owes Nothing has been triggered at Rank A Idho for the first time.|

|The Tide has weighed what you have done. You have undertaken a tremendous act of giving: you have cleansed the Curse of a Steed whose lineage stems from Those Who Remain, at the price of your own death. You gave existence itself back to a dying Steed of the First Clutch of makers, and the Tide does not permit such giving to flow one way.|
|An Unfathomable wonder of unknown origins will be paid through this act of giving.|
The moment the prompts finished…
CRACK!
Noah's stretched moment of infinity shattered.

Time slammed back into motion around him, snow falling, blue flooding, the pillar climbing, and in the same heartbeat he felt something squeeze into existence directly above his palms, fold itself out of nothing with a small, dense, impossibly quiet weight, and drop into his hands.
It was…a simple white egg.
Noah stared at it.

There were no flashy lights! There were no terrifying bursts of power, no detonating skies, no light-years of split heavens announcing a boon's arrival! The grandest Foundation he possessed, at the rank of authority over endings, triggered by an act of giving priced at his own death, had produced…a smooth, palm-sized, perfectly white egg, sitting in his hands.
|You have gained ?????.|

Even Ruination's prompt had nothing else to offer! Five question marks, from the existence that had catalogued Curses of Those Who Remain and Character Sheets of Steeds, and the egg simply sat there, white and warm and silent, explaining absolutely nothing!
Noah's eyes became heavy as he looked at it.

An unfathomable wonder of unknown origins. Unknown even to the Regard, unknown even to her! He turned it once in his fingers, felt nothing but smooth warmth and a faint, patient density, like something very large practicing being very small…and he put it away, deep into his stores, beside the Primeval limb and the Marrowbane Fruit and every other loaded thing he owned.
Because they were still within the body of Hvitrmarr.
And in front of them, the vaulted white-flame dark was gathering itself into a shape.
Light condensed! White flame drew inward from the reborn vaults, folding and slimming and settling, and a humanoid manifestation of Hvitrmarr formed before them!

She stood tall and straight-backed, robed in layered white that fell like fresh snowfall given tailoring, and her terrifying, regal beauty struck the vault silent. Hair of white flame poured down her back, still faintly burning without fuel or end! Twin slender curves of translucent ivory swept back from her temples, the ghost-echo of her horns, and her face was ageless and cold and heartbreakingly fine, the face of a queen carved by makers who had never once intended for it to know suffering! And her eyes, gold, ring within ring within ring, rested upon Noah and upon THE Infiniverse.
She was trying to show them nothing.

And Noah saw everything she was hiding! The happiness, three thousand years overdue, trembling at the very edges of that composed cold face. The hope, no longer punished, no longer priced, burning quietly in the rings of her eyes for the first time without agony answering it. The relief, vast as her true body, held back behind regal stillness because a queen of the First lineage did not weep in front of guests, and every nanosecond of her not-weeping was visibly, gloriously costing her!
She looked at them both for a long moment.
Then Hvitrmarr, First of her lineage in three thousand years to stand uncursed, gave them a light bow.
"I owe you…existence."

chapters.title: Chapter 5531: Fledgling!
paragraphs: "I indeed owe you Everything."
Hvitrmarr's manifestation straightened from her bow, and her ring-in-ring eyes had already hardened back into a queen's.
"Which is why we have to go. Right now. So that I can ensure your safety, because…Jarl Skallagrim, a Cursed Descendant, is here, and even I cannot stand against him."
They were already here?
"I could not leave this Dimension before. The Curse chained every Steed to THE Krazhor-Nul, a fence around the livestock, and running only ever meant running in circles inside it."
"But with the Curse gone…I am free to do so. I will be taking us away from THE Krazhor-Nul Dimension itself."
Away from the Dimension! Out past its walls, beyond the reach of Jarls and hosts and dying colossi, through the dark between Dimensions.
And Noah's gaze became heavy.
"Not yet."
The word landed in the vault with the full weight of his immensity, an Emperor's refusal spoken to a Steed offering salvation, and he continued before it could be argued!
"Make sure to take THE Creature and Anaximander outside…as well as Ryaenara!" His hands were already moving, waving through the white-flame dark as his newly risen Intent poured outward.
"This is her, and what I can emulate of her weavings of existence. Can you locate her before leaving?"
Light bloomed between his palms.

An image of Ryaenara unfurled across the vault, vibrant and loose-grinned and profane even in still light, and around the image, Noah emulated everything he held of her! The texture of her Antiquity, older than the Scales! The signature of her weavings as his Estuary and every record of every shared battlefield reconstructed her presense thread by thread, an existence sketched from memory by an authority over endings.
He had made a choice, and the choice was simple.
He was not leaving Ryaenara behind.
Not in a Dimension with Cursed Descendants and other monstrosities!

Hvitrmarr looked at the image for a long moment, somber, and the Causes inside her pulsed. Nine reborn suns turning faster, Fealty's new heart drumming through the vault, and when she spoke, there was something old and careful in it.

"To locate one thread across a Dimension this vast, while outrunning what hunts us…I will need to express my full power." Her golden eyes rose to his. "And to express my full power, I will need…someone to ride me."
What?
Noah blinked once.
Right! She was a Steed.

A living Observable Existence built, at the level of her deepest architecture, around carrying! Nine Organs that tilted towards virtue, Fealty and Obedience and Devotion, an entire anatomy of virtues that all pointed at a saddle, and for three thousand cursed years, that architecture had been chained to thrones and whips, and never once completed by a willing seat!
Noah looked at her with shining eyes, and spoke grandly.
"I will ride you. Let's go."
The manifestation of Hvitrmarr nodded once, and everything moved.

The vault folded. Noah saw THE Creature and Anaximander pulled into this space in streaks of obsidian and white, the golden island he had left outside drawn in whole alongside them, sands and forges and all, swallowed into the sovereign interior of the White Steed for safekeeping. And his own body was pulled the opposite way, drawn up across the inner vaults of her chest, past the drumming new Heart of Fealty, up through parting scales as he found himself pulled toward the back of this grand Steed.
Ivory plates unsealed above him. Cold sweet air poured in.
And Noah emerged into the open sky of the ancient ice.

The snowy landscape stretched below in every direction, glacial plains glowing faintly blue with the residue of the war just won, snow still falling in slow silver veils, and his body rose through it all in her grip of white light before settling, gently, deliberately, upon the back of The White Steed.
The moment he did…
HUUUM!
The entire Dimension seemed to bear witness.

The ambient storms of THE Krazhor-Nul stilled across the horizon. The falling snow hung! The strings of Infinity and Primordial Source and even THE Lingering Word itself all seemed to turn, in one vast attending hush, toward the ancient ice where, for the first time since the makers walked, a Steed of the First lineage was mounted by a willing, chosen, uncursed rider, and even Noah, crowned and reborn, was astonished.
For the instant he settled upon her scales, he felt it!
An immense, unfathomable strengthening of his existence!

|You are the first non-Descendant of Nhaglfarr-Ythok, THE Sleepless Fiend of Those Who Remain, to ride one of the Steeds born of his ingenuity. The Steeds were his design. His craft and his cruelty both. Their saddles were cut for his bloodline alone, and for ages beyond counting, only Cursed Descendants have ever sat where you are sitting. The architecture of the First lineage has weighed you, and it has chosen to recognize your seat as sworn, not stolen.|

|Designation gained: THE Fledgling Liege of the First Lineage. This is the beginner's distinction of a rider of these Steeds. The word Fledgling is doing heavy work in that title. What sits above it returns only ?????.|
|Starter boons of THE Fledgling Liege, cataloged:|

|THE Bond of Seat and Sworn. A permanent channel now runs between rider and Steed. Thought passes without words across any distance. Senses may be borrowed: her sight that reads weavings within weavings, her sovereignty-sense that tastes Dimensional law. And the reservoirs of both existences now stand open to one another: you may draw upon the power of her eighteen Causes, and she upon your seas. Two existences, one account.|

|THE Anchored Seat. Nothing unseats you. No velocity, no force, no authority tears you from her back while the bond stands: your position is now a fact of existence rather than a matter of grip. Her element cannot harm you, her white flame recognizing you as its own, and within the reach of her sovereignty, hostile environments, void, pressure, and essence are refused on your behalf.|

|THE Regal Mantle. You passively radiate the presence of the First lineage while seated. Lesser existences will find that their instincts developed opinions about you before their minds were consulted.|

|THE Boundless Crossing. The First Steeds were built for one purpose above all others: to carry riders across the dark between Dimensions. It is what her ancestor did with the maker whose weight bent the crossing. It is what her blood has remembered through every cursed generation. While you ride her, Dimensional Traversal is no longer an ordeal. Walls between Dimensions become doors. Doors become a stride. The roads between many Dimensions are mapped in her inherited memories, Master…and you now hold the map.|
|Deeper functions of the bond remain sealed behind the Fledgling distinction. They return ?????, and they are many.|
Prompts of majesty upon majesty bloomed.
But the prompts were only words, and what Noah FELT beneath them was beyond any cataloging!
For the bond was open, and existence was flowing both ways.

His Osmontian Source Infinity poured down through his seat into her, oceans of newly-risen A-Rank sea rolling through her vast frame, and he felt her drink it the way parched roots drink rain, felt his Infinity spread through eighteen Causes and set every one of them blazing brighter! His Intent flowed with it, THE Ananke Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian sinking into her weavings, and her whole colossal existence answered his identity, aligning to it, the way a blade aligns to the hand it was forged for!
And back up through the bond…she flowed into him.

Her Causes came first, eighteen of them, First and Prime, their mingled truths washing up through his seat and into his own nine, feeding the slow grand evolution already underway! He felt Fealty's permanence and Valor's drawn breath, Endurance's tirelessness and Devotion's lift, virtues older than the Scales pouring through a Human body.
And then her Intent arrived.
And Noah's existence pulsed.
For her Intent, the Intent seated in her First-lineage architecture by the living hands of Those Who Remain, flowed into him, and it did not taste of Ananke.
It sat above Ananke!
Autarkis!

Above inevitability! Above "I must be obeyed"! A third texture, vast and quiet and prior, the very thing he had felt once as a door beyond a door when his own Intent crowned itself, and here it was, flowing through his seat in living rivers, and through the bond he felt her feel his shock, and felt something almost like an ancient, tired smile move through the mountain beneath him!
'Later,' her thought came, the first words ever spoken through their bond. 'Ride now. Learn later.'
And Hvitrmarr stretched her wings.

The great white sails of Devotion-and-Harvest spread across the snowing sky, wider than horizons, and as they reached their full glorious span, a pillar of white and blue light shot up all around them.

Sovereignty and Infinity braided into a single rising column, rider and Steed announced together to nearby corners of an ancient Dimension, and the frozen plains below turned to a sea of glittering light!
And at this time…
In the far distance, a throne stopped dead in the sky.
Jarl Skallagrim and his eight Steeds stared ahead at the rising pillar with utter incredulity, and their bodies trembled!

Every one of them! The eight dying colossi in their harness shook in their chains, ancient eyes stretched wide, terminal frames quaking, because their senses were all reporting the same impossible absence! From the white queen at the heart of that distant light, there was no sign of the Curse!
None! Not a thread! Not a whisper of the gnawing that had defined every Steed's every nanosecond since the sentence was first spoken.
She found a solution.
She actually found a SOLUTION!

Three thousand years of watching, a millennium of Skallagrim's patient study, ages of an entire Dimension's certainty, all of it detonated in a single sensing, and then, slowly, terribly, eight pairs of dying eyes and one pair of lucid rotting ones moved from the queen…
To the man atop her.
To the rider!

And all their eyes blazed with immense greed! The eight Steeds' hope-rejuvenated gazes locked onto the small crowned figure seated upon the uncursed Steed with the ravenous focus of the drowning sighting shore, and Jarl Skallagrim's terribly sane eyes fixed upon Noah with the weavings of a man with a few years left staring at the being who dispensed more.
The possibility-weavings in his palm churned into a blur.
And Jarl Skallagrim bellowed out madly, lucidity and desperation fused into one Dimension-shaking roar, as for countless gigaparsecs in every direction…
All skies turned black!

Ivory plates unsealed above him.
Cold sweet air poured in.
And Noah emerged into the open sky of the ancient ice.

The snowy landscape stretched below in every direction, glacial plains glowing faintly blue with the residue of the war just won, snow still falling in slow silver veils, and his body rose through it all in her grip of white light before settling, gently, deliberately, upon the back of The White Steed.
The moment he did…
HUUUM!
The entire Dimension seemed to bear witness.
The ambient storms of THE Krazhor-Nul stilled across the horizon.
The falling snow hung!

The strings of Infinity and Primordial Source and even THE Lingering Word itself all seemed to turn, in one vast attending hush, toward the ancient ice where, for the first time since the makers walked, a Steed of the First lineage was mounted by a willing, chosen, uncursed rider, and even Noah, crowned and reborn, was astonished.
For the instant he settled upon her scales, he felt it!
An immense, unfathomable strengthening of his existence!
|You are the first non-Descendant of Nhaglfarr-Ythok, THE Sleepless Fiend of Those Who Remain, to ride one of the Steeds born of his ingenuity.
The Steeds were his design.
His craft and his cruelty both.
Their saddles were cut for his bloodline alone, and for ages beyond counting, only Cursed Descendants have ever sat where you are sitting.
The architecture of the First lineage has weighed you, and it has chosen to recognize your seat as sworn, not stolen.|
|Designation gained: THE Fledgling Liege of the First Lineage.
This is the beginner's distinction of a rider of these Steeds.
The word Fledgling is doing heavy work in that title.
What sits above it returns only ?????.|
|Starter boons of THE Fledgling Liege, cataloged:|
|THE Bond of Seat and Sworn.
A permanent channel now runs between rider and Steed.
Thought passes without words across any distance.
Senses may be borrowed: her sight that reads weavings within weavings, her sovereignty-sense that tastes Dimensional law.
And the reservoirs of both existences now stand open to one another: you may draw upon the power of her eighteen Causes, and she upon your seas.
Two existences, one account.|
|THE Anchored Seat.
Nothing unseats you.
No velocity, no force, no authority tears you from her back while the bond stands: your position is now a fact of existence rather than a matter of grip.
Her element cannot harm you, her white flame recognizing you as its own, and within the reach of her sovereignty, hostile environments, void, pressure, and essence are refused on your behalf.|
|THE Regal Mantle.
You passively radiate the presence of the First lineage while seated.
Lesser existences will find that their instincts developed opinions about you before their minds were consulted.|
|THE Boundless Crossing.
The First Steeds were built for one purpose above all others: to carry riders across the dark between Dimensions.
It is what her ancestor did with the maker whose weight bent the crossing.
It is what her blood has remembered through every cursed generation.
While you ride her, Dimensional Traversal is no longer an ordeal.
Walls between Dimensions become doors.
Doors become a stride.
The roads between many Dimensions are mapped in her inherited memories, Master…and you now hold the map.|
|Deeper functions of the bond remain sealed behind the Fledgling distinction.
They return ?????, and they are many.|
Prompts of majesty upon majesty bloomed.
But the prompts were only words, and what Noah FELT beneath them was beyond any cataloging!
For the bond was open, and existence was flowing both ways.

His Osmontian Source Infinity poured down through his seat into her, oceans of newly-risen A-Rank sea rolling through her vast frame, and he felt her drink it the way parched roots drink rain, felt his Infinity spread through eighteen Causes and set every one of them blazing brighter!

His Intent flowed with it, THE Ananke Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian sinking into her weavings, and her whole colossal existence answered his identity, aligning to it, the way a blade aligns to the hand it was forged for!
And back up through the bond…she flowed into him.
Her Causes came first, eighteen of them, First and Prime, their mingled truths washing up through his seat and into his own nine, feeding the slow grand evolution already underway!
He felt Fealty's permanence and Valor's drawn breath, Endurance's tirelessness and Devotion's lift, virtues older than the Scales pouring through a Human body.
And then her Intent arrived.
And Noah's existence pulsed.
For her Intent, the Intent seated in her First-lineage architecture by the living hands of Those Who Remain, flowed into him, and it did not taste of Ananke.
It sat above Ananke!
Autarkis!
Above inevitability!
Above "I must be obeyed"!

A third texture, vast and quiet and prior, the very thing he had felt once as a door beyond a door when his own Intent crowned itself, and here it was, flowing through his seat in living rivers, and through the bond he felt her feel his shock, and felt something almost like an ancient, tired smile move through the mountain beneath him!
'Later,' her thought came, the first words ever spoken through their bond. 'Ride now.
Learn later.'
And Hvitrmarr stretched her wings.

The great white sails of Devotion-and-Harvest spread across the snowing sky, wider than horizons, and as they reached their full glorious span, a pillar of white and blue light shot up all around them.

Sovereignty and Infinity braided into a single rising column, rider and Steed announced together to nearby corners of an ancient Dimension, and the frozen plains below turned to a sea of glittering light!
And at this time…
In the far distance, a throne stopped dead in the sky.
Jarl Skallagrim and his eight Steeds stared ahead at the rising pillar with utter incredulity, and their bodies trembled!
Every one of them!
The eight dying colossi in their harness shook in their chains, ancient eyes stretched wide, terminal frames quaking, because their senses were all reporting the same impossible absence!
From the white queen at the heart of that distant light, there was no sign of the Curse!
None!
Not a thread!
Not a whisper of the gnawing that had defined every Steed's every nanosecond since the sentence was first spoken.
She found a solution.
She actually found a SOLUTION!

Three thousand years of watching, a millennium of Skallagrim's patient study, ages of an entire Dimension's certainty, all of it detonated in a single sensing, and then, slowly, terribly, eight pairs of dying eyes and one pair of lucid rotting ones moved from the queen…
To the man atop her.
To the rider!
And all their eyes blazed with immense greed!

The eight Steeds' hope-rejuvenated gazes locked onto the small crowned figure seated upon the uncursed Steed with the ravenous focus of the drowning sighting shore, and Jarl Skallagrim's terribly sane eyes fixed upon Noah with the weavings of a man with a few years left staring at the being who dispensed more.
The possibility-weavings in his palm churned into a blur.
And Jarl Skallagrim bellowed out madly, lucidity and desperation fused into one Dimension-shaking roar, as for countless gigaparsecs in every direction…
All skies turned black!

chapters.title: Chapter 5532: Dimensionlapse!
paragraphs: Riding was a sensation Noah had to adapt to.

Not the seat. The seat was effortless, anchored by boons into a fact of existence! What required adapting was everything flowing through the seat, the drumming of a Fealty-heart the size of a realm beneath him, the tidal rhythm of Valor's lungs, eighteen mixing Causes turning under his palms like an engine of virtues, and his own seas pouring down into all of it while her ancient rivers poured back up.
Two existences breathing in each other's rhythm, and every breath of it settling deeper! It felt far, far too intimate than he expected.

And with his reformed body, reborn light and sharp from the Root, in addition to this ridiculous empowerment that came from mounting Hvitrmarr…Noah was able to very clearly sense the power that made this Steed want to run away.
His gaze rose across the blackened gigaparsecs.
And he looked upon the maddened figure of the Cursed Descendant.

Jarl Skallagrim burned against his own darkened skies, titanic and rotting and terribly awake, carried forward on his throne by eight dying Steeds whose eyes were all fixed on Noah, and from that distant lucid figure rolled a power that pressed against Noah's newly-risen senses with a texture he had never once encountered.
It was terrifying enough to give a sense of hopelessness.

Even now! Even at A-Rank Idho, even seated on a First-lineage Steed, even twenty-five million strong, the presense of the thing on that throne registered in his weavings as something his frameworks simply could not hold! It did not belong to the Fifth Scale. It did not belong to the Sixth! It did not belong to ANY Scale, and Noah realized, with the cold clarity of a man updating his maps mid-journey, that he would need to find entirely new rankings of power outside of Vakochev's Scales altogether, because…damn.
If Hvitrmarr, uncursed and eighteen-Caused and sovereign, still chose to run away from this monstrous thing…
Then they ran.
"Go."

Noah whispered it calmly while clasping the scale of Hvitrmarr below him, and in the next second, he and the massive White Steed beneath him turned their gazes across the dark, glared coldly at Jarl Skallagrim, rider and mount delivering one shared look of unhurried, imperial promise…
And disappeared!
The white-blue pillar collapsed inward on the empty ice, and where a queen and her Liege had stood, there was only falling snow!
And Jarl Skallagrim glared forth madly!

His rotting face twisted around its terrible lucidity as he rose from his throne, and he WHIPPED the reins of cursed lightning, and eight rejuvenated Steeds screamed against their harness and tore forward through the blackened sky, an entire hateful cluster hurling itself after the vanished point of its salvation as the chase began in earnest!
In this snowy area, upon the emptied ice where two impossible things had just departed, a golden cloud drifted down through the falling silence, and upon it stood a shocked old woman.
THE Recorder of Wilds stared at the point where Noah and Hvitrmarr had just been, and her ancient eyes were shining.
"Who is he to actually dare to reverse an action of one of Those Who Remain? Does he even know what he just did?" Her voice was hushed, and for once, it was not narrating.
"And more than that…a Cure for the Curse of this Cursed Dimension! This…how does this affect things…"
She had been speaking to herself when, in the next moment, the ice shook.
She turned.
And behind her, descending through the storm on legs like dying mountain ranges, was the Steed of Oblivion!

Ghrimhest's colossal gray frame filled the snowing sky, chains screaming, its guttering eyes stretched wide and fixed on the horizon where the pillar had stood, and shockingly, atop the burden-bearer's vast back, small against its enormity and burning with desperate power…
Was Jarl Erling.

The dying titan himself as he had seen the failure of his party through Ghrimhest's senses, and he had used whatever unique power his Steed possessed to cross the Dimension himself! Now that he knew another Jarl was involved, there was no need for secrecy! The race was naked, and the prize was fleeing, and his titanic bronze face was filled with such regret and such pain that it had cracked new fissures beside the crimson ones.
He may have even missed out! The cure had been here,  and Jarl Erling roared with everything his remaining years could carry!
"GO! GO GO! CATCH UP TO THEM!"

The Steed of Oblivion bellowed, and the mountain-frame surged forward through the storm, keeper and burden-bearer tearing off after the same vanished point as the Jarl before them, and THE Recorder of Wilds stood upon her cloud and watched them go, and slowly shook her head.
A Steed that was no longer cursed. So long as the fleeing ones were not stupid, they should not be caught.

They would be far from this Dimension soon. And the pursuit? It was impossible for the Cursed Steeds to leave this Dimension, fenced by the sentence itself. And for the Cursed Descendants, leaving was merely…hard. Not impossible, just very hard!
And more than hard, it was priced.

For she knew what few remaining beings knew. One of the promises made to the Descendants for their sin was this: if they left this Dimension, they would have no chance of Salvation from their curse. The fence around the bloodline was not a wall. It was a wager! Stay, and hope. Leave, and be certain! And so for ages, dying generation after dying generation had stayed, orbiting the faint promise like moths deciding the lamp was a dawn.

"Mm. And now the dawn has run off," the old woman murmured. "Words should be handled with the same care as eggs, but I will say this much. Among all the Descendants of all of Those Who Remain, the ones seeded under THE Sleepless Fiend have always hated their ancestor the most..."
But as the Recorder was thinking all this, in the next moment…she was surprised.
For off to the side, another aura arrived.

It did not creep, and it did not announce! It was simply there, seated into the storm as if it had always been part of the weather, and it looked straight at her, through every fold of unsensability she wore, and the old woman felt the rare, almost nostalgic pleasure of being seen…
And she smiled.
Out of the billowing snow walked a titan.

He was massive, a gorilla-like humanoid whose shoulders moved like hills deciding to travel, his whole vast body draped in fur of pure obsidian that drank the storm-light and gave back none of it! Waves of majesty rolled off of him with every unhurried step, the pressure of something earlier than frameworks, and in one enormous hand he carried a black bow taller than True Lifeforms, its limbs burning along their length with a low, patient fire, and any being with the senses to read that flame would have understood instantly that it could scorch and melt Ananke Intent effortlessly, the way morning melts frost!
A Primeval One.
The titan's deep-set eyes swept once across the emptied ice, across the residue of the pillar, and settled on the old woman upon her cloud, and he nodded.
"Recorder." His voice was the sound of a mountain being courteous. "I have been waiting for you. Though I did not expect to find you at the scene of an incident."
His gaze moved to the horizon where two hunts had vanished. "Did you see what happened here?"
The Recorder smiled at this.

"I saw. But that is the second thing I will talk about, as the first thing, the one that brought many of us to this Dimension, has to be discussed before it." She settled her sleeves, ancient eyes twinkling. "Haha, where are the other Primevals? O, Doku?"
Doku, the obsidian archer, rolled his vast shoulders.
"The others are meeting with the Jarls. The ones who still have many years left to live, and thus still have manners left to spend." His deep voice carried a plain, unhidden distaste.

"But I do not really agree with our approach here. Just because Cursed Descendants are easier to deal with…does not mean we have to work with them. There are countless possibilities out there. We are reaching for the nearest branch and calling it the best fruit."
The Recorder smiled wider.

"And yet we are here." She poured herself tea without hurry, the storm bending politely around the ritual. "Because someone, and we still have not figured out the culprit, mind you, someone is causing Dimensionlapses across many nearby Dimensions. Pitting different forces into war as separate Dimensions begin fusing into each other! The many Dimensions we hold are being threatened. So here we are, in a cursed backwater older than the Scales, seeking any point of knowledge and cooperation we can find."
Her wrinkled eyes gleamed over the rim of her cup. "Haha, and what do I find in this place? Someone curing a Curse of THE Sleepless Fiend!"
Doku heard this, and his deep-set eyes shone!
The black bow's fire flared along its limbs as the obsidian titan leaned toward her, majesty rippling off him in eager waves.
"What? We can use that for our own aims!" His voice dropped into the register of strategy. "Who? Which Descendant figured out the cure? Or was it one of us?"
The Recorder blinked.

For perhaps the first time in several eras, the old woman who had a narration for everything did not quite know how to answer, and her teacup hovered, and her expression folded into something genuinely conflicted.
"Well…" she said slowly. "They are neither Primevals nor Descendants…"
Doku straightened to his full titanic height, the storm parting around his shoulders, genuine surprise moving through his ancient face.
"Then who could they possibly be?"
At this question, The Recorder only smiled, and looked out to where a certain Steed had disappeared.

The snow in this region had turned into a billowing storm, white veils folding over the emptied ice in slow colossal waves. And through all of it, if one only looked closely, the snowflakes themselves were pulsing. Each falling flake carried a silent blue-white light, faint and patient and new, the light of Causes mixing together for the first time in existence…
Still prevalent.

chapters.title: Chapter 5533: Breathe!
paragraphs: They found Ryaenara in a sea of poison.

The chase had torn across the Dimension in folds of white-blue light, Hvitrmarr's inherited might swallowing gigaparsecs between wingbeats, and through the bond, Noah felt the moment her borrowed senses and his emulated weavings finally triangulated on a single vibrant thread, burning loose and profane and utterly alive at the heart of a region drowned in verdant miasma.
Ryaenara!

The poisoned expanse opened below them, an ocean of green-gold murk where toxin had replaced weather, and at its center, the Antiquity was fighting! Her radiant figure wove through collapsing structures of venom as her opponent filled the horizon behind her, a Cenozoic True Lifeform in the shape of a massive verdant frog, mountainous and glistening, its throat-sac swelling with lakes of miasma, its bulbous eyes tracking her with the patient hunger of a creature that had dissolved everything it had ever met.
And Hvitrmarr did not slow.
She descended upon the region like a verdict, and her Intent ERUPTED!
THE Autarkis Intent!

It poured off her body in a sovereignty that sat above inevitability itself, the third order, the texture past the door, and as it flooded the poisoned sky, Hvitrmarr's claw extended! The Claws of Mercy-and-Tyranny reached down and out, talons of white flame stretching until they seemingly covered light years, five curved horizons of burning ivory descending over the frog's entire existence, and before the Cenozoic True Lifeform could so much as swell its throat…
The claw crashed onto it.

There was no battle! There was not even an exchange! The verdant titan's Ananke-grade Intent collapsed instantly beneath the touch of an order it could not argue with, its Trueness caving inward alongside it, the seamless "I am" of a Cenozoic apex crumpling like wet parchment under a mountain, and the massive frog was driven down into its own miasma, unmade of everything that had made it mighty, in a single descending motion!
And in the same motion, light wrapped around Ryaenara.

The Antiquity froze inside the gentle white cocoon, and her wide eyes found the colossal White Steed above her, and then the small crowned figure seated upon its back, and the look on her face was pure, spectacular incredulity. Osmont. Riding a monstrosity of wonder!
"Come!" Noah called down grandly.
And Ryaenara disappeared into Hvitrmarr's chest!
And in this fraction of an instant, in the sliver of time it took to do this one action…behind them, all of existence changed.
Noah felt it through every Cause he owned, and turned.
The Dimension itself was transforming.
For gigaparsecs behind them, everything, the storms, the strings of Infinity and Primordial Source, the drowned green horizon, the very dark between all of it, was becoming a hand.

Not covered by a hand. BECOMING one! An obsidian hand of Jarl Skallagrim, assembled out of existence itself, storm-fronts folding into finger-joints, light-years of sky hardening into obsidian knuckles, the ambient essence of an entire region converted wholesale into palm and grasp, and from its closing curl came a suction force so terrifying that the poisoned ocean below rose whole off the land and streamed toward it, that distance itself leaned backward into the grip, a horrific phenomenon that rewrote the simple concept of "behind them" into a single word.
Caught.
"OOOOH!"

Noah bellowed out as he grasped onto Hvitrmarr's scales tightly, his A-Rank seas slamming down through the bond, and he and Hvitrmarr both roared as one! Her nine Organs churned! Fealty's heart hammered into a war-drum, Valor's lungs drew a breath the size of the sky, and his Nine Prime Causes spun into her 9 like engines coupling at full burn, two existences igniting every joined Cause they shared against the pull of a grasping Dimension!
And gloriously, the truth revealed itself.

Hvitrmarr had already begun slipping across Dimensions the moment she acted to bring Ryaenara in! The catch and the crossing had been one maneuver, started before the hand ever formed, her First-lineage blood threading them into the gaps between the Dimension's weavings even as her claw was still descending, and they were only completing the action now.
This...was the only reason they were not caught.
The obsidian fingers closed.
And in the next instant, rider and Steed turned into pure white-blue light!

The radiance pulled away from the obsidian hand like a thread drawn out of a closing fist, phasing into the gaps of this Dimension, between its strings, beneath its laws, and OUT of it entirely, and against a suction that had swallowed a poisoned sea, the light of Noah and Hvitrmarr...
Disappeared!
The obsidian hand closed on nothing.

Jarl Skallagrim had risen from his throne to arrive here first.

He had outrun his own harness. He had spent power that his two remaining years could not afford, converted a region of an ancient Dimension into his own grasp, and he floated now in the miasma-tainted silence, staring at the point where his salvation had phased out of existence, and his rotting face was very, very calm.
Behind him, the Steeds arrived.
The eight of them tore into the region dragging his empty throne, and the moment their senses swept the emptiness, they began to howl.

Long, cracking, terminal howls of pain, for the uncursed one was gone, the proof was gone, the first new hope in years had left the Dimension they could never leave, and their dying Causes screamed the loss through every chained channel!
Jarl Skallagrim floated coldly amid the howling.
Then he reached out, and grasped one of the eight.
His obsidian hand, the small one, the merely titanic one, closed around the nearest Steed's neck-ridge, and he began to calmly and brutally tear it apart.
SQUELCH!
There was no fury in the motion.

He worked with the unhurried thoroughness of a man taking down a tent, peeling the dying colossus open along its chained weavings as it screamed, its terminal Causes guttering out one by one in his grip, and the other seven Steeds watched in absolute frozen fear, howls strangled into silence, an entire harness learning in real time what their keeper's calm was worth!

He looked at the seven remaining, and they did not meet his eyes.

Her great head turned slightly, one gold eye finding him across her own horizon.

And Noah smiled.

Hvitrmarr's Organs pulsed beneath him.

Noah nodded.

"All that is Human, wherever it stands, whenever it stands."
HUUM!
Hvitrmarr did not flinch from the size of it! Her wings spread wider across the frothing dark, and her vow came back level and absolute.
"Then I will take you to every Dimension you need. Many are mapped in my lineage, and they are yours now. You need only say where." Her voice settled into something older than the formality.
"I will repay the debt of my curse however I can, for however long the repaying takes."
Noah's eyes shined brightly at this, and he nodded!
And in the next moment, he sent his thoughts down through the bond, and an instant later…
WAP!

A white platform formed below the three of them the moment they arrived, a disc of pale sovereign light holding them just above her scales, for they were not considered to be riding Hvitrmarr, and by every law of the saddle and the lineage, they shouldn't be able to!
Shouldn't.
But who knew what monsters like Anaximander were capable of? The scholar was already looking down at the white platform beneath his feet with the mild, curious expression.
Ryaenara's gaze swept from the naked strings of the dark, to the colossal uncursed queen beneath her, to the crowned figure seated at the head of it all.
And Noah looked at all of them as he wanted to hear their input!

chapters.title: Chapter 5534: Trials! I
paragraphs: <THE Creature>
Upon a white platform on the back of a Steed, in the dark between all Dimensions, Existence itself watched a Human, and marveled in silence.

THE Creature's obsidian flames burned low and even as his gaze rested on THE Youngest. On the crowned figure seated at the head of a grand lifeform, speaking easily with his companions. On the being who had, in the span of one Dimension, undergone tremendous change.
The Youngest had pulled far ahead. At this moment, seated on that Steed, he should be…a bit more powerful than him.
THE Creature looked down at his own hands.

Obsidian fingers, threaded now with white-gold from the Primeval tail at his back. Hands that had carried eras. Hands that had never once, in all the long bearing, felt like they were holding less than they should.
And yet.

What was this, sitting in him now? This sense of falling behind? Of being…slow? He turned the feeling over carefully, because it was unfamiliar. He had never been one who felt weaker. He had never felt inadequate! He had not known such emotions even existed within him, and he would have said, if asked, that they did not, for he had made a practice across his existence of giving away many of his Everythings and regenerating them afterward, his Everything of Fear, his Everything of Longing, given and regrown, given and regrown…just to see if he could.
He had treated his own depths like a demonstration.
And here was a depth he had never demonstrated, arriving unasked. Was this what the Youngest felt on all those climbs?
"The Jarls will hunt me now."
Noah's voice moved easily through the dark, unhurried, addressed to all of them.
"I'm currently a target of the Cursed Descendants of THE Krazhor-Nul Dimension." He shrugged slightly.
"It's not anything crazy. I should be able to continue moving without problems. I'll be following my own path regardless, and I know all of you have your own plans."
His gaze passed across them.
"THE Sealed One is an enemy to take down in time. Others will fall in line after. But before any of that…what do you all wish to do?"
The question hung in the frothing dark.
And THE Creature reflected.

He looked at the feeling in his hands, this new weight called falling-behind, and he looked at the road that had put it there. The Youngest had not pulled ahead by waiting. He had pulled ahead by rushing in, and doing it rapidly at that!
If he wanted to truly follow his path…he had to rush in without anything holding him back.
The decision settled into him completely, and without ceremony.
"I will have to go," THE Creature spoke up, his flat voice carrying across the platform, "and seek the power I need to truly begin my path of a Great Ruler."
The conversation stilled.
"It is a path I must walk alone. For now…this should be my goodbye." His obsidian gaze was level. "I thank you because the power gained from THE Krazhor-Nul Dimension will be of big help."
And as he said it, he looked at his tail.
THE Blank Caudal of the Unwritten Primeval swayed slowly behind him, white-haired and patient, threading its light through his flames.
He looked up at The Youngest and Anaximander.
The two of them stared at him silently. No protest. No negotiation as after a moment, they simply nodded.
And THE Creature…showed a rare smile.
It moved across his features unfamiliar and unhurried, and when he spoke, his grand voice had the cadence of utter glory.

"I used to believe Existence was a weight that things carried. That every being staggered beneath the fact of itself, and the strongest were merely the ones who staggered least." His flames burned low.

"I was wrong. I have watched all of you, and I was wrong. Existence is not the weight. Existence is the carrying. It is not the stone, it is the back that bends and does not break, it is the hand that lifts what it did not drop"

His gaze passed slowly across all of them. "What is borne, and who bears it, and how they rise beneath it. That is all Existence has ever been. And a Ruler of Existence…must simply be the one who carries the largest share, the longest, for the most."
The dark between Dimensions held very still around the words.
Then THE Creature closed his eyes.

He turned his attention inward and backward, into the deep architecture of his own existence, to the presence that sat folded there, inherited and his, the seated colossus of worn gray stone. He regarded it for a long moment, this Paradox he had disliked and carried anyway, and he addressed it directly for the first time.
"I am ready to go all in." His voice was quiet. "Let the trials of existence begin."
And within him, and behind him, and somehow also very far away…
HUUM!
The statue opened its eyes.
Two points of light kindled in the faceless gray stone, ancient past all framing, and an ancient voice boomed out, not loud, but vast, a voice that seemed to arrive from the direction time came from.
"THE FIRST TRIAL…IS TO BATHE IN THE BLOOD OF A THOUSAND TRUE LIFEFORMS THAT HAVE SIGNIFICANTLY HARMED EXISTENCE."
A thousand True Lifeforms! Harvested not at random, but judged, each one weighed and found guilty of harming Existence itself, and their blood the bath!
THE Creature did not hesitate.
He gave a simple nod and opened his eyes, and began to float up off the back of Hvitrmarr as waves of schorcing flames billowed around him!
At the platform's edge, he paused, and looked at Anaximander.
"My friend. I will try not to call you for help again too quickly. But if I do…forgive me."
And Anaximander smiled, tousled and plain amid the naked strings of the dark.

"Whenever you need me, call." The scholar's eyes were warm. "Distance is a superstition, and so is 'too quickly.' Existence can be very miserable alone, and we can make the conditions ourselves not to be miserable."
With these words held, THE Creature turned last to Noah.
And his eyes flashed with a competitive light!
"Youngest. I am curious how far your human road will stretch. I am waiting to see which of us will become a Great Ruler." The rare smile returned, one degree sharper.
"We may be back together before you know it, soon. As…I will see if I can possibly pull ahead of you by then."
THE Youngest smiled calmly at this, and nodded.
THE Creature gave one last nod to Ryaenara.
The Mirthful Antiquity nodded back, uncharacteristically wordless, her vibrant eyes holding him a moment longer than a nod required.
And then he fully floated away from Hvitrmarr.

He did not ask for a road. He did not ask for a door! He moved out into the frothing dark between all Dimensions as if he already knew exactly where he wanted to go, and did not need anybody to take him there, because he did not. His Pantheon had no shape. His Pantheon became its surroundings.
Existence was his Pantheon.
And even out here, between all membranes and beneath all frameworks…was existence.
His obsidian flames spread into the dark, and the dark received them, and at this moment, wholly and without reservation, THE Creature went all in to everything that existence entailed!

sentences.text: <THE Creature>
Upon a white platform on the back of a Steed, in the dark between all Dimensions, Existence itself watched a Human, and marveled in silence.
THE Creature's obsidian flames burned low and even as his gaze rested on THE Youngest.
On the crowned figure seated at the head of a grand lifeform, speaking easily with his companions.
On the being who had, in the span of one Dimension, undergone tremendous change.
The Youngest had pulled far ahead.
At this moment, seated on that Steed, he should be…a bit more powerful than him.
THE Creature looked down at his own hands.
Obsidian fingers, threaded now with white-gold from the Primeval tail at his back.
Hands that had carried eras.
Hands that had never once, in all the long bearing, felt like they were holding less than they should.
And yet.
What was this, sitting in him now?
This sense of falling behind?
Of being…slow?
He turned the feeling over carefully, because it was unfamiliar.
He had never been one who felt weaker.
He had never felt inadequate!

He had not known such emotions even existed within him, and he would have said, if asked, that they did not, for he had made a practice across his existence of giving away many of his Everythings and regenerating them afterward, his Everything of Fear, his Everything of Longing, given and regrown, given and regrown…just to see if he could.
He had treated his own depths like a demonstration.
And here was a depth he had never demonstrated, arriving unasked.
Was this what the Youngest felt on all those climbs?
"The Jarls will hunt me now."
Noah's voice moved easily through the dark, unhurried, addressed to all of them.
"I'm currently a target of the Cursed Descendants of THE Krazhor-Nul Dimension." He shrugged slightly.
"It's not anything crazy.
I should be able to continue moving without problems.
I'll be following my own path regardless, and I know all of you have your own plans."
His gaze passed across them.
"THE Sealed One is an enemy to take down in time.
Others will fall in line after.
But before any of that…what do you all wish to do?"
The question hung in the frothing dark.
And THE Creature reflected.
He looked at the feeling in his hands, this new weight called falling-behind, and he looked at the road that had put it there.
The Youngest had not pulled ahead by waiting.
He had pulled ahead by rushing in, and doing it rapidly at that!
If he wanted to truly follow his path…he had to rush in without anything holding him back.
The decision settled into him completely, and without ceremony.
"I will have to go," THE Creature spoke up, his flat voice carrying across the platform, "and seek the power I need to truly begin my path of a Great Ruler."
The conversation stilled.
"It is a path I must walk alone.
For now…this should be my goodbye." His obsidian gaze was level.
"I thank you because the power gained from THE Krazhor-Nul Dimension will be of big help."
And as he said it, he looked at his tail.
THE Blank Caudal of the Unwritten Primeval swayed slowly behind him, white-haired and patient, threading its light through his flames.
He looked up at The Youngest and Anaximander.
The two of them stared at him silently.
No protest.
No negotiation as after a moment, they simply nodded.
And THE Creature…showed a rare smile.
It moved across his features unfamiliar and unhurried, and when he spoke, his grand voice had the cadence of utter glory.
"I used to believe Existence was a weight that things carried.
That every being staggered beneath the fact of itself, and the strongest were merely the ones who staggered least." His flames burned low.
"I was wrong.
I have watched all of you, and I was wrong.
Existence is not the weight.
Existence is the carrying.
It is not the stone, it is the back that bends and does not break, it is the hand that lifts what it did not drop"
His gaze passed slowly across all of them.
"What is borne, and who bears it, and how they rise beneath it.
That is all Existence has ever been.
And a Ruler of Existence…must simply be the one who carries the largest share, the longest, for the most."
The dark between Dimensions held very still around the words.
Then THE Creature closed his eyes.
He turned his attention inward and backward, into the deep architecture of his own existence, to the presence that sat folded there, inherited and his, the seated colossus of worn gray stone.
He regarded it for a long moment, this Paradox he had disliked and carried anyway, and he addressed it directly for the first time.

"Let the trials of existence begin."

HUUM!

"THE FIRST TRIAL…IS TO BATHE IN THE BLOOD OF A THOUSAND TRUE LIFEFORMS THAT HAVE SIGNIFICANTLY HARMED EXISTENCE."
A thousand True Lifeforms!
Harvested not at random, but judged, each one weighed and found guilty of harming Existence itself, and their blood the bath!

chapters.title: Chapter 5535: Trials! II
paragraphs: He floated across boundless darkness for an indeterminate amount of time.

Time did not press its claims out here, and THE Creature did not press his! He drifted through the frothing black with his body folded in upon itself, knees drawn up, obsidian flames banked low around his body, curled the way a thing is curled when it is newly born, and in a manner of speaking…he was.
For around his folded form, roiling waves of a deep Ananke Intent burned!

The digestion had finished somewhere in the drifting dark. Two Gilded True Lifeforms had rendered down to their last weavings within his depths, and their essense had carried him across the threshold he had approached for so long, and the second order of Intent now turned around him in slow tidal revolutions, inevitability wearing obsidian, and beneath it, his weight felt even more immense. As if everything he had ever carried had settled at last.
He did not open his eyes for any of it.
He only opened his eyes, and unfurled, when he felt himself slipping across the folds of a Dimension.
The dark parted. Membrane-weavings slid across his flames like curtains of another existence's law, and as he passed through them, the statue spoke.
Its voice came calm this time. Not the booming verdict of the trial's declaration, but something quieter and older.
"You stand within THE Ghor-Vazhal." The ancient voice moved through him without hurry. "Its masters call it the Fields. Everything else that has ever learned its name calls it the Cultivation Farms."
"Here, Source True Lifeforms practice an external art of existence. You bear your adversity. They have decided bearing is inefficient." The calm of the voice made the words worse.

"They cultivate Gu Lifeforms, bred hungers, refined across generations, and they strengthen these Gu through the sacrifice of cognizant lifeforms. Trillions of them. Across countless worlds and realms and domains of this Dimension, lifeforms moving through existence carrying their own adversity are plucked from their lives, refined for flavor, sacrifised, and eaten, and the Gu digest what those lives carried, and the masters harvest the Gu, and progress arrives for them rapidly, externally, at no cost their own existence ever feels."
The membrane-folds thinned ahead. Light the color of old blood bled through.

"Trillions of lives are wiped out daily. It has been so for ages. Boundless suffering stretches across worlds and domains that appear in no records except as acreage." A pause, and the calm voice set down its last stone. "Here, many True Lifeforms who have significantly harmed Existence can be found. That is why the first trial begins in this place. Begin whenever you wish."
And rage coursed through THE Creature.
It ROSE, the way floodwater rises, patient and total, filling every channel of a newly-Ananke existence from the floor upward!

Existence is the carrying! It is the back that bends and does not break! And here was an entire Dimension built by beings who had heard that same truth somewhere in their long climbing, and had answered it with a ledger and a farm! Beings who did not carry. Beings who billed to to others!
Who had turned the bearing of trillions into feed, and called the weaving an art!
The folds opened, and he slipped fully in, and saw where he had appeared.
The skies were painted red.

Butcher red! A vast crimson firmament stretched from horizon to horizon, stained by ages of what rose into it, and below, across a scorched land that had been walked flat by chained feet…rose the pyramids.

They climbed in their dozens toward the red sky, colossal stepped mountains of black stone, each tier worn smooth and dark with use, and at the very top of every one of them, roiling, sat the Gu Lifeforms! Grotesque bred hungers the size of hills, no two alike, one a mass of mouths arranged in a wheel, one a bloated segmented thing whose shell wept, one a beautiful shimmering moth whose wings were made entirely of grasping hands, each of them squatting upon its pyramid's peak like an idol of appetite!
And up the steps of every pyramid, in procession…climbed the chained.

Millions of them! Humanoid lifeforms and beasts both, shackled throat to throat in lines that stretched back across the scorched land beyond sight, dragged upward tier by tier by weavings that gave them no floor to fall to and no strength to resist, and at the top of each climbing line, at each peak, the processions ended in the mouths of the Gu! Steadily. Rhythmically! An intake as constant and unremarkable, to this place, as breathing, the carrying of trillions rendered down into feed while the red sky drank the noise!
And at a central point among the pyramids, upon a floating terrace of veined gold…multiple Source True Lifeforms were gathered together, laughing, and talking.

Lounging! Robed existences of the threshold, dense and patient and ancient, sharing refreshment above the machinery of their art, one of them gesturing lazily toward a distant pyramid as if comparing yields, another laughing at the remark, the sound of it drifting bright and easy across a landscape eating millions!
THE Creature looked at this scene.

He looked at the wheel of mouths taking its procession. He looked at the chains, and the climbing lines without end, and the laughter on the golden terrace, and somewhere behind his ribs, a statue's ancient eyes burned, and the floodwater reached the top of him!
And THE Creature roared out with maddened grandeur!
OOOOH!

The sound tore across this tiny region of THE Ghor-Vazhal like the birth-cry of a verdict, Ananke Intent detonating off his frame in obsidian tides, and every chained head across a million tiers turned, and every Gu's appetite stuttered, and upon the golden terrace, the laughter died mid-note as ancient heads snapped upward toward a fold in their sky that had opinions!
And THE Creature raised his fists, and SMASHED them down toward the gathered True Lifeforms!
And the skies answered!

The red firmament itself convulsed as, across the whole visible heaven, the stained clouds and the bloodlight and the upper airs gathered and folded, forming into colossal illusory fists, ten of them, a hundred, the sky becoming knuckles from horizon to horizon, and they came down with his own fists, all of them, together, as if existence itself was attacking!

chapters.title: Chapter 5536: Trials! III
paragraphs: The fists came down.

A hundred of them, folded out of a sky that had been drinking screams for ages, huge knuckles of stained cloud and bloodlight dropping together with the two obsidian ones at their center, and the floating terrace of veined gold, that lounging place where an art was talked over with food and drink, stopped being a place at all.
BOOM!
The impact flattened the region.

Gold burned away. The terrace's foundations, weavings anchored into the Dimension's own strings by beings who had held them for ages, tore free with a sound like a continent being unstitched, and the shockwave rolled outward across the scorched land in a ring of obsidian fire that walked over three pyramids and left them leaning, and every chained line across a million tiers went down flat as the ground bucked beneath them!
And out of the flattening, the Source True Lifeforms rose.

They rose fighting. THE Creature would grant them that much and nothing else. Nine of them came up out of their own ruin with their density intact, robed existences of the threshold, ancient and patient and very hard to unravel, and their Intent came off them in slow heavy pressures that made the air itself refuse to move, and one of them looked at him with such deep, insulted disbelief that it was almost worth something.
"Who the fuck is this dumb motherfucker?!"
HUUM!
Their Intent converged.

Nine Ananke-grade weights, laid one atop another, one joined pressure built to press a trespasser flat into the very land they farmed, and it fell upon THE Creature with all the piled authority of ages of undisturbed harvest!
And THE Creature simply spread his arms.
HUUM!
THE MAW opened somewhere that was not his body.

It opened in the ground beneath their feet, and in the red sky above their heads, and in the space between their converging weights, because THE Pantheon of All Existence has no shape and never needed one, and the nine masters of the Cultivation Farms suddenly understood, all at once, that they were no longer standing in their Dimension.
They were standing INSIDE him.

The red sky was him. The scorched land was him. The leaning pyramids and the chains and the whole flat butchered horizon was him, and their nine converging Intents poured into a throat that had been swallowing adversity since before the Scales were drawn, and vanished, and did not come back!
Their weights guttered and their pressure broke.
And the one who had spoken first took one step backward.
That step was the only warning any of them received.
WAA!
THE Creature moved!
His obsidian flames tore across the emptied sky in a single black stroke, and behind him, unfurling long and white and patient, came the tail.
THE Blank Caudal of the Unwritten Primeval!

White hair threaded with the gold of a thing older than every framework these beings had ever climbed, it whipped out across gigaparsecs of ruined farmland and took the nearest master around the throat, and the Source True Lifeform's dense and patient existence, that thing so famously hard to unravel, was hauled off its feet and driven down through nine tiers of its own pyramid at a speed that turned black stone into black powder!
CRASH!

And it kept going. It went down through the pyramid's root, and through the crust beneath, and the tail did not release, it constricted, white coils tightening in the dark under the world while the master's Trueness bled out of it in sheets of wasted light!
At the peak of that same pyramid, the Gu began to react.

The wheel of mouths, hill-sized and grotesque, shook itself off its perch as ages of training told it that something had entered the land, and it turned all of its mouths toward THE Creature at once and screamed a scream made of every intake it had ever performed!
THE Creature looked at it.

He looked at the bred hunger, the trained appetite, the generations of careful breeding that had produced a thing whose entire purpose was to receive what other beings had carried and hand the profit upward, and his rage found a new floor to flood!
He reached out with his hand.
And the tail came up out of the ground behind the Gu.
SHIING!

It punched through the wheel from beneath and burst out of the top of it, and then it opened, white coils splaying like a hand inside a fist, and THE Creature closed his fingers, and his tail tore the Gu apart from the inside out!
The hill-sized thing came apart in the red air.
And what spilled out of it was not guts.
It was the corpses.

Ages of it, uncounted, the piled weight of every life that had climbed those steps and been sacrifised into that wheel, released all at once into a sky that had no idea what to do with it, and for one moment the whole region was full of the weight of trillions, their labors, their endurances, their small stubborn bearings, hanging in the butcher-red light with nowhere left to go!
And across a million tiers, the chained looked up and saw it!
THE Creature's flames burned white-gold at their edges, and he went to work.

What followed was not a battle! It had the shape of one for a while, because the masters of the Fields were mighty, and they fought with all the art of ages, and two of them managed to wound him. One split his shoulder open with a lance of packed sacrificial essense and THE Creature did not so much as look at the wound. One anchored a weaving into his flames that should have cut him off from his own Pantheon, which was a genuinely excellent idea, and would have worked on almost anything else in existence, and did nothing at all to a being whose Pantheon was the ground the weaving was anchored in.
He took that one in his hands and laid THE Burden of Existence upon it.
HOONG!
The appendage settled onto the master's back, and it gave that ancient patient thing exactly what it had spent its ages avoiding.
The bearing.

Every era THE Creature had carried, every weight, every adversity borne without complaint since before many Dimensions had a name, moved whole onto a being who had built an entire civilization on the idea that bearing was a waste, and the Source True Lifeform's knees hit the black stone, and then its hands, and then its face, and it stayed down there making a sound that had no dignity in it whatsoever while its own weavings buckled under a debt it had never once paid a copper toward!
And then he crushed its skull with his heel.
SQUELCH!
Across the region, the pyramids were coming down.

He walked through the Fields and unmade them. The tail whipped and coiled and strangled, taking Gu and master alike, smashing bred hungers into those that had fed them, and where his flames touched the black stone the stone forgot it had ever been stacked. The moth with wings of grasping hands tried to rise off its peak and got half a wingbeat before white coils took it around the thorax and folded it in half the wrong way.

The bloated segmented thing burst and rained ages of stolen carrying across three continents of scorched land. Six pyramids. Nine. Fourteen! An entire district of the Cultivation Farms turned into rubble and rising weight while the red sky churned overhead, and behind his ribs, an ancient Creature kept a calm and terrible tally!
And the last of the nine True Lifeforms, the one who had spoken first, finally stopped retreating and turned to face him with its Trueness burning down to its final reserves.
It roared at him.
"Do you know what you are doing?! What force we belong to?! We stem from-"
The tail was already moving.

It came across the red sky wearing the full weight of a newly-seated Ananke Intent, white and gold and utterly without hurry, and it cleaved the master's skull apart mid-sentance, and the great and ancient existence that had been about to call on its lineage came apart in two clean falling halves.
"I don't give a damn."
Silence took the Fields.

The last of the ruin settled. The rubble stopped moving. Across a landscape that had been eating millions daily since before the Scales were laid out, nothing was eating anything at all, and the only sound left in the whole butchered region was the wind pulling at loose chain.
THE Creature floated up into the red sky.
He rose slowly, obsidian flames burning low and even around his frame, until he hung high above the broken pyramids, and from up there he could see all of them.
The chained.

Millions of them, still shackled throat to throat in lines that stretched past the horizon, humanoid lifeforms and beasts both, lying where the shockwaves had thrown them and staring upward at the thing in their sky. He looked down into their faces.
He saw what was in them.

There was no gratitude. Not yet, and maybe not ever, because gratitude needs a future and these beings had been raised in a place that issued none. What he saw was rage. Old rage, buried so deep beneath the climbing and the chains that most of them had probably forgotten they were carrying it, surfacing now in ten million upturned faces at once.
Good.
"I will take your rage and your pain and your suffering," THE Creature said, and his flat voice carried across every area and every chain and every scorched acre of the Fields.
"And I will make them all answer for it."
"Don't let go of that rage. Do not let it go!"
HUUM!

And then he turned in the red sky and shot out toward another direction, obsidian fire tearing a line across the sky, because this had been one district, one region, one flat butchered corner of a Dimension that stretched much further than that, and out there across THE Ghor-Vazhal the other pyramids were still standing and the other Gu were still swallowing and the chained lines had not stopped climbing for so much as a heartbeat.
Decillions.

The number moved through him and would not settle. Countless Decillions of thinking beings across the Fields, born into farmland, raised as flavor, whose entire fate from first breath to last was to be used and devoured so that beings on golden terraces could climb without the excitment of ever having to carry anything, and every one of them had borne something, and not one of them had ever been asked!
And rising underneath all these thoughts, older, unhealed, the thing he never spoke of.
His other half.
Brutalized in front of him. This was what he continued to be reminded of when he looked at all their faces!
His rage rose higher as his first Trial barely began.
A thousand? He would kill fucking millions if he needed to!
