HUUM!
Their Intent converged.

Nine Ananke-grade weights, laid one atop another, one joined pressure built to press a trespasser flat into the very land they farmed, and it fell upon THE Creature with all the piled authority of ages of undisturbed harvest!
And THE Creature simply spread his arms.
HUUM!
THE MAW opened somewhere that was not his body.

It opened in the ground beneath their feet, and in the red sky above their heads, and in the space between their converging weights, because THE Pantheon of All Existence has no shape and never needed one, and the nine masters of the Cultivation Farms suddenly understood, all at once, that they were no longer standing in their Dimension.
They were standing INSIDE him.
The red sky was him.
The scorched land was him.

The leaning pyramids and the chains and the whole flat butchered horizon was him, and their nine converging Intents poured into a throat that had been swallowing adversity since before the Scales were drawn, and vanished, and did not come back!
Their weights guttered and their pressure broke.
And the one who had spoken first took one step backward.
That step was the only warning any of them received.
WAA!
THE Creature moved!
His obsidian flames tore across the emptied sky in a single black stroke, and behind him, unfurling long and white and patient, came the tail.
THE Blank Caudal of the Unwritten Primeval!

White hair threaded with the gold of a thing older than every framework these beings had ever climbed, it whipped out across gigaparsecs of ruined farmland and took the nearest master around the throat, and the Source True Lifeform's dense and patient existence, that thing so famously hard to unravel, was hauled off its feet and driven down through nine tiers of its own pyramid at a speed that turned black stone into black powder!
CRASH!
And it kept going.

It went down through the pyramid's root, and through the crust beneath, and the tail did not release, it constricted, white coils tightening in the dark under the world while the master's Trueness bled out of it in sheets of wasted light!
At the peak of that same pyramid, the Gu began to react.

The wheel of mouths, hill-sized and grotesque, shook itself off its perch as ages of training told it that something had entered the land, and it turned all of its mouths toward THE Creature at once and screamed a scream made of every intake it had ever performed!
THE Creature looked at it.

He looked at the bred hunger, the trained appetite, the generations of careful breeding that had produced a thing whose entire purpose was to receive what other beings had carried and hand the profit upward, and his rage found a new floor to flood!
He reached out with his hand.
And the tail came up out of the ground behind the Gu.
SHIING!

It punched through the wheel from beneath and burst out of the top of it, and then it opened, white coils splaying like a hand inside a fist, and THE Creature closed his fingers, and his tail tore the Gu apart from the inside out!
The hill-sized thing came apart in the red air.
And what spilled out of it was not guts.
It was the corpses.

Ages of it, uncounted, the piled weight of every life that had climbed those steps and been sacrifised into that wheel, released all at once into a sky that had no idea what to do with it, and for one moment the whole region was full of the weight of trillions, their labors, their endurances, their small stubborn bearings, hanging in the butcher-red light with nowhere left to go!
And across a million tiers, the chained looked up and saw it!
THE Creature's flames burned white-gold at their edges, and he went to work.
What followed was not a battle!
It had the shape of one for a while, because the masters of the Fields were mighty, and they fought with all the art of ages, and two of them managed to wound him.
One split his shoulder open with a lance of packed sacrificial essense and THE Creature did not so much as look at the wound.

One anchored a weaving into his flames that should have cut him off from his own Pantheon, which was a genuinely excellent idea, and would have worked on almost anything else in existence, and did nothing at all to a being whose Pantheon was the ground the weaving was anchored in.
He took that one in his hands and laid THE Burden of Existence upon it.
HOONG!
The appendage settled onto the master's back, and it gave that ancient patient thing exactly what it had spent its ages avoiding.
The bearing.

Every era THE Creature had carried, every weight, every adversity borne without complaint since before many Dimensions had a name, moved whole onto a being who had built an entire civilization on the idea that bearing was a waste, and the Source True Lifeform's knees hit the black stone, and then its hands, and then its face, and it stayed down there making a sound that had no dignity in it whatsoever while its own weavings buckled under a debt it had never once paid a copper toward!
And then he crushed its skull with his heel.
SQUELCH!
Across the region, the pyramids were coming down.
He walked through the Fields and unmade them.

The tail whipped and coiled and strangled, taking Gu and master alike, smashing bred hungers into those that had fed them, and where his flames touched the black stone the stone forgot it had ever been stacked.
The moth with wings of grasping hands tried to rise off its peak and got half a wingbeat before white coils took it around the thorax and folded it in half the wrong way.
The bloated segmented thing burst and rained ages of stolen carrying across three continents of scorched land.
Six pyramids.
Nine.
Fourteen!
An entire district of the Cultivation Farms turned into rubble and rising weight while the red sky churned overhead, and behind his ribs, an ancient Creature kept a calm and terrible tally!
And the last of the nine True Lifeforms, the one who had spoken first, finally stopped retreating and turned to face him with its Trueness burning down to its final reserves.
It roared at him.
"Do you know what you are doing?!
What force we belong to?!
We stem from-"
The tail was already moving.

It came across the red sky wearing the full weight of a newly-seated Ananke Intent, white and gold and utterly without hurry, and it cleaved the master's skull apart mid-sentance, and the great and ancient existence that had been about to call on its lineage came apart in two clean falling halves.
"I don't give a damn."
Silence took the Fields.
The last of the ruin settled.
The rubble stopped moving.

Across a landscape that had been eating millions daily since before the Scales were laid out, nothing was eating anything at all, and the only sound left in the whole butchered region was the wind pulling at loose chain.
THE Creature floated up into the red sky.
He rose slowly, obsidian flames burning low and even around his frame, until he hung high above the broken pyramids, and from up there he could see all of them.
The chained.

Millions of them, still shackled throat to throat in lines that stretched past the horizon, humanoid lifeforms and beasts both, lying where the shockwaves had thrown them and staring upward at the thing in their sky.
He looked down into their faces.
He saw what was in them.
There was no gratitude.
Not yet, and maybe not ever, because gratitude needs a future and these beings had been raised in a place that issued none.
What he saw was rage.
Old rage, buried so deep beneath the climbing and the chains that most of them had probably forgotten they were carrying it, surfacing now in ten million upturned faces at once.
Good.
"I will take your rage and your pain and your suffering," THE Creature said, and his flat voice carried across every area and every chain and every scorched acre of the Fields.
"And I will make them all answer for it."
"Don't let go of that rage.
Do not let it go!"
HUUM!

And then he turned in the red sky and shot out toward another direction, obsidian fire tearing a line across the sky, because this had been one district, one region, one flat butchered corner of a Dimension that stretched much further than that, and out there across THE Ghor-Vazhal the other pyramids were still standing and the other Gu were still swallowing and the chained lines had not stopped climbing for so much as a heartbeat.
Decillions.
The number moved through him and would not settle.

Countless Decillions of thinking beings across the Fields, born into farmland, raised as flavor, whose entire fate from first breath to last was to be used and devoured so that beings on golden terraces could climb without the excitment of ever having to carry anything, and every one of them had borne something, and not one of them had ever been asked!
And rising underneath all these thoughts, older, unhealed, the thing he never spoke of.
His other half.
Brutalized in front of him.
This was what he continued to be reminded of when he looked at all their faces!
His rage rose higher as his first Trial barely began.
A thousand?
He would kill fucking millions if he needed to!

chapters.title: Chapter 5537: Ordinary! I
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
Noah turned his gaze to Ryaenara after THE Creature completely disappeared.

She had been quiet since he pulled her out of that poisoned sea, which was not like her at all, for the Mirthful Antiquity did not do quiet, she did loud, and profane, and right now she was standing on a disc of white light above a Steed's scales with her arms folded, looking at him with something working behind her eyes!
She had many things on her mind.
And then she asked her question.
"It seems you were able to cure a Cursed Steed." Her voice came level.

"A curse passed down across its whole lineage, stemming from Those Who Remain themselves." Her vibrant eyes did not leave his face. "Can you do the same for my brother? Do you already have the capability to cure him too?"
The dark between Dimensions flowed past as the strings hummed their long notes, and Noah did not answer quickly.
He thought about it properly first.
"No," he said. "Not yet."
Ryaenara said nothing as she waited.
"Hvitrmarr's curse was rooted in her Causes." Noah rested a hand flat on the ivory beneath him.

"Her First Causes were failing, one by one, on a schedule somebody else wrote for her, and everything else about her was just a thing standing on top of that failure. So I didn't cure her, not the way a healer would. I went in and I replaced her Causes. I took what was terminal and I collapsed it, and I gave the space it left a new meaning, and I seated my own Causes into her Organs where the dying ones had been."
His eyes stayed on Ryaenara's.
"That is what the cure was."

"Your brother is different." He said it plainly. "Ulf's curse is sitting on top of his existence. It isn't a failing organ I can cut out and replace with a better one. It's woven into the same weavings that make him Ulf."

"Which means to cure him the way I cured her, I wouldn't be replacing Causes. I would have to replace an entire existence. Collapse the one he currently has, all of it, and give it new meaning on the other side." He shook his head once.
"I do not have that capability, not with what I know now, not with anything I currently hold. If I tried it today I would not cure your brother. I would end him."
WAA!
Ryaenara looked at him for a long moment.
And then she nodded silently.
"Then I remain with you," she said, "and give what I can to ensure your growth as we head towards IT."
And she was not finished.

"There is something else." Ryaenara's tone changed, going lighter in a way that meant the opposite of light. "After we left THE Krazhor-Nul, messages from THE Sealed One reached out across my existence. Asking for updates on you."
The name moved through the little gathering on Hvitrmarr's back!
Anaximander's head came up slightly, and Noah felt a slow cold interest settle in his chest.
Ryaenara held his gaze without apology.
"What shall I tell him?"
Noah thought about it.
He thought about the shape of the answer, because say too little and the thing gets suspicious, and say too much and you have handed a monster a weapon.
Say something true, but small, and slightly boring.
"Tell him I've begun skipping across Dimensions," Noah said thoughtfully. "That I'm trying to establish myself. Nothing more specific than that."
He smiled slightly. "And tell him you're getting close to me, but keeping your distance."
Ryaenara's mouth curved as she nodded calmly.
Noah then turned his gaze to Anaximander.
The scholar had been standing there through all of it in his white robes with his tousled hair, saying nothing, and he was extremely thoughtful at this moment.
Then he looked up.
"Could you," Anaximander said, "actually come with me?"
Noah raised an eyebrow.

"To that Dimension I mentioned. The one I have to go back to." The scholar's plain voice picked up a little warmth. "You have talked about Humans. About being a Human Emperor, about gathering everything Human wherever it stands. And these beings, these Superpowered Lifeforms, are some of the more human beings you are going to meet anywhere."

"They are like me, and also not like me, and I have never quite been able to explain the difference to myself, which is one of several reasons I have not stopped thinking about them." A small self-aware smile.
"I think you would benefit from meeting them. And from seeing what they have built."
He paused.
"And when I left, an incursion was about to happen as they were defending against Infinite Lifeforms."
"What do you think?"
Noah considered it.

He genuinely did not have a preference, because THE Krazhor-Nul had been chosen for him by his own Anchor, and THE Krazhor-Nul had been far too heavy! Cursed Descendants who converted gigaparsecs into a fist! Steeds whose ambient presence stopped his Pantheon from unfurling! He had walked out of it alive and crowned and riding a steed, and he had walked out of it knowing exactly how close the whole thing was, and he had even died in there!
So. Would this place be more his speed?
Beings without authority, whose identity made existence conform, a whole society of them, defending their own borders against many enemies.
And there was the other thing.

Anaximander had mentioned a Panacea. A cluster of Observable Existences producing something that Source and Infinite True Lifeforms would wage war to take, that they had been waging war to take, for long enough that the defense had become a civilization!
A Panacea!
Noah, who currently had a Dimension full of dying tyrants preparing to hunt him for exactly that kind of thing, felt his interest sharpen.
"Okay!"
His eyes shined as he looked at the scholar.
"What is this place called?"
And Anaximander smiled.

"THE Ymnaros," he said. "It is an old word, older than the beings living there now, and as far as I have been able to trace it, it means something close to Ordinary. They named it that themselves. I have never worked out whether it was a joke."
Noah smiled lightly.
He turned toward the great white head at the front of it all.
"Hvitrmarr."
"I have this Dimension within my internal map," she answered before he finished asking, her ancient voice warm through the bond and through the dark both. "I will take you there."
And her wings began to beat.
WUU!
The long strokes shortened and quickened and gathered as Hvitrmarr banked across the naked strings of the deep, turning them onto a new heading, and Noah felt her capability wake beneath him!
It was the same one that had saved them from a closing obsidian hand.

He felt it come up through her scales into his seat, the First-lineage blood in her threading them into the gaps between things, laws and membranes and distances all agreeing to step aside for a lineage that had been crossing this dark since Those Who Remain designed it, and the frothing black stretched and folded and...
HUUM!
In a matter of seconds, they arrived!
They appeared before a shimmering endless boundary! She was that quick. A steed was that grand!
Noah looked at it, and it was unique.

It hung across the whole of his vision and past it, a vast surface of soft shifting light, and it was not a wall and not a door and not a membrane like the ones he had watched drift past out here, it moved like the surface of water seen from underneath, and it had a warmth to it.
|Analysis of the periphery is complete.|
Ruination's voice came clean and immediate.

|The outer boundary of this Dimension carries an active drawing authority. Its function is not to repel. Its function is to route. Any foreign existence that crosses the boundary is caught by this authority and pulled, regardless of its intended point of entry, into one of many centralized domains maintained across the interior. These are designated THE Muster Halls.|

|Purpose: everything foreign that arrives is delivered into a prepared place, and is treated on arrival as an enemy until proven otherwise. Defenders are stationed. The routing is automatic and constant. The overwhelming majority of incursions are stopped in the Halls and never reach the interior at all.|
|Assessment: this is a Dimension that has been invaded so many times it has built its front door out of the invasions.|

|Some beings are simply too powerful for the drawing authority to hold, and bypass the routing entirely. Those beings arrive wherever they wish. It is reasonable to assume the Halls exist because of how much damage the ones who bypass them have historically done.|
Noah's eyes twinkled!

An entire Dimension that had turned being attacked into an architecture! That had accepted, as a permanent condition of its existence, that things would keep coming for what it held, and had answered by building a system that greeted every single arrival as a hostile act and processed it accordingly!
He liked them already.
'Would you be pulled to one of those?' he asked through the bond. 'If we cross here.'
Hvitrmarr's answer came calm and entirely without arrogance.

'No. I am a Dimension Steed. Routing authorities are for things that must use a Dimension's doors.' Her great head turned as one gold eye found him. 'I can enter directly into any point of this Dimension I choose.'
Noah nodded slowly.
"Let's go then!"
WUU!

Her wings spread wide across the shimmering endless light, and rider and Steed and scholar and Antiquity moved as one toward THE Ymnaros, and the boundary opened its soft shifting folds around them, vibrant and warm and utterly unlike the cold rind of the Dimension they had left, and they disappeared into it!

chapters.title: Chapter 5538: Ordinary! II
paragraphs: <THE Ymnaros>

The gardens had been green and gold for longer than most Dimensions had been standing, running in long terraces across a land that had no edges anyone had ever found, the green shading into the gold and back again as wide slow rivers cut through all of it carrying light instead of silt, and small things had lived there and none of them had ever been important, and that had always been the entire point of the place!
Now the terraces were burning.

The rivers had been broken open along their whole length as their light bled out into the soil in long spreading stains, and the gold had gone black in rings around a hundred impact sites, and where the gardens had climbed they now sagged, and where they had run they now simply stopped.
And above the ruin stood the armies.

They filled the sky in ranks that went back past seeing, existences of Infinity in their tens of thousands, their power built out of escalation and quiet compounding as they hung in their formations with their weight pressing the ruined land flat beneath them, and the weakest thing in that entire gathered host read at THE Triassic Scale!
The weakest!

The Fourth Scale of Existence, the tier where a single being could stand upon an Observable Existence and be the largest fact inside it, and here that was the floor, here that was the rank and file, the bodies you counted in blocks rather than by name!

And scattered up through those blocks, spaced apart the way real threats are always spaced apart, there stood over a hundred figures who carried the unmistakable weight of THE Mesozoic Scale, the Fifth, each one of them a thing that ordinary Dimensions built their entire histories around, and there were over a hundred of them in one sky on one afternoon for one garden.
And rising out of the armies like statues that had been given breath, several massive Infinite True Lifeforms towered above everything!

They were vast past the ranks around them, vast past any comparison with the ranks around them, their bodies reading less as bodies than as landscapes that had agreed to hold a shape for a while, and their existences were seamless in the way that only a True Lifeform's ever is, the claim of "I am" running through them without a single gap for anything to take hold of, and that seamlessness set them above THE Mesozoic entirely.
Cenozoic!
And the difference between the Fifth and the Sixth, in the end, was time.

Beings at the Mesozoic Scale built their Pantheons and made them grander and grander, and it was work enough to eat ages of a life, but a being who crossed into THE Cenozoic Scale kept doing all of that and then began adding something else into their Pantheonic Dimension, something that almost nothing in existence could hold, and what they added were weavings of time!
And most of them could not use it.

That was the honest truth of the Sixth Scale and the reason so many beings who reached it looked, from the outside, like nothing more than very large Mesozoics, because the technique was simply too hard to grasp, and entities in the early stretches of THE Cenozoic Scale carried those weavings inside their Pantheons the way a person carries a language they cannot yet speak, aware of it, unable to use it, fighting with weight and grandeur alone while the real capability sat unopened inside them for ages.
The power at Cenozoic was known as THE Epochal Sovereign Weave!

More plainly, and more often, it was called Temporal-Environmental Overwrite, and a True Lifeform who had truly grasped it no longer fought inside a Dimension's current time or under its current physical rules at all, but dragged the space around them backward or forward instead, hauling the surroundings into weavings where their own Pantheon and their own existence ruled absolutely, so that the fight happened there, in their epoch, on ground that had been made to agree with them before the first blow ever landed.
And the results of it were obscene.

An incoming attack could be made to travel years before it ever reached the one it was aimed at, arriving worn down, arriving late, arriving as a thing that had already spent itself on the way, and the defenses of another could be made to weather years while they stood, an opponent's Pantheon forced to age through decades of erosion in the space of a single held breath!

And the terrifying ones, the ones who could set an entirely different epoch into their surroundings rather than merely bending the local one, did something worse than either of those, because inside a forced epoch a power system could be treated by the environment itself as a thing not yet invented, or as a thing long since abandoned, and a being would raise a capability they had spent ages perfecting only to find the surroundings quietly declining to recognize it at all!
Downgraded! Negated! Not defeated, which would at least have been a kind of respect, but ruled out entirely, the way a law rules out a thing that has not happened yet.
There were levels to it.

There were always levels to it, and every being in that sky knew exactly which level it stood upon, and that was precisely why the ranks held their spacing so carefully around the tall silent shapes among them.
Eight True Lifeforms had entered a small corner of the gardens of THE Ymnaros that day.
Six of them were still standing.

At the center of the ruin, where the terraces had once climbed into their finest arrangement, a shrine rose out of the wreckage, a single obelisk taller than mountains with its faces carved in lines that were neither writing nor decoration, and it burned with a steady blue-gold light that had not dimmed by so much as a shade through the entire assault, the light pouring up its faces and off its point and hanging in the smoke above it, patient, unbothered, still doing whatever it had always been doing.
And two of the six True Lifeforms stood at its base and had not moved from it once.

They did not attack it, and they did not attack anything else either, they simply held their places on either side of that obelisk with their whole attention fixed upon it as though waiting for something, and their stillness said more about what that shrine was worth than the entire army above them could have said with a thousand years of screaming.
And the gardens around the shrine were decimated.
For in that destruction lay two corpses.

Infinite True Lifeforms, both of them, split wide open, and there was no other way to describe what had been done to them, their landscape-bodies lying across the ruined terraces in halves, opened from the top down along a line so clean that it looked considered, their Pantheons collapsed inside them and still collapsing even now, and out of those openings ran rivers of Infinity.
Actual rivers of it!

Bright and endless and pouring, escalation with nothing left to escalate through, spilling down the broken terraces and mixing with the light of the murdered gardens, a wealth of power that a Mesozoic being would have wept simply to touch, running out across the dirt because there was no longer any existence attached to it that could hold onto it!
Two True Lifeforms of the Infinite variety, killed, here, in this garden.
And gathered around those enormous corpses, small as scattered seeds against them, there lay the bodies of unique humanoid lifeforms all adorned in white and blue suits.

Dozens of them, built plainly, no larger than any ordinary person, their suits simple things of white with blue running through them and marked at the chest with a sign that had been designed to be recognized at a distance by frightened people, and some of them had died still holding their formation, and some of them had died reaching toward someone else who had also died.
They were... Superpowered Lifeforms.

The gardens had been green and gold for longer than most Dimensions had been standing, running in long terraces across a land that had no edges anyone had ever found, the green shading into the gold and back again as wide slow rivers cut through all of it carrying light instead of silt, and small things had lived there and none of them had ever been important, and that had always been the entire point of the place!
Now the terraces were burning.

The rivers had been broken open along their whole length as their light bled out into the soil in long spreading stains, and the gold had gone black in rings around a hundred impact sites, and where the gardens had climbed they now sagged, and where they had run they now simply stopped.
And above the ruin stood the armies.

The weakest!

And rising out of the armies like statues that had been given breath, several massive Infinite True Lifeforms towered above everything!

They were vast past the ranks around them, vast past any comparison with the ranks around them, their bodies reading less as bodies than as landscapes that had agreed to hold a shape for a while, and their existences were seamless in the way that only a True Lifeform's ever is, the claim of "I am" running through them without a single gap for anything to take hold of, and that seamlessness set them above THE Mesozoic entirely.
Cenozoic!

And most of them could not use it.

That was the honest truth of the Sixth Scale and the reason so many beings who reached it looked, from the outside, like nothing more than very large Mesozoics, because the technique was simply too hard to grasp, and entities in the early stretches of THE Cenozoic Scale carried those weavings inside their Pantheons the way a person carries a language they cannot yet speak, aware of it, unable to use it, fighting with weight and grandeur alone while the real capability sat unopened inside them for ages.
The power at Cenozoic was known as THE Epochal Sovereign Weave!

Negated!

chapters.title: Chapter 5539: Ordinary! III
paragraphs: Dead Superpowered Lifeforms.
And in the middle of all of it, on his knees in the wreck of a garden, one of them was still alive.
A golden-haired man!

He was built like something that had been made on purpose, enormous through the shoulders and the chest, heavy with a muscle that did not look decorative in the slightest, his arms thick enough that the chains upon them had needed to be thick as well, and he wore the same white and blue as the dead around him with the sleeves gone and the chest sign burned half away, his hair gold and short and matted dark down one side, his jaw set, his mouth bleeding.
And he was staring hatefully up at the army.

Not with fear, and not with despair, and not with the shocked emptiness of a being who had watched everyone he came in with die, but with hatred, clean and enormous and moving from face to face across an entire army as it took each one of them in turn and held it a moment and then moved along to the next one!
And he gave off nothing.

Not one wave of authority! Not the smallest ripple of the pressure that even a Triassic Scale existence pushes out of itself simply by being present, and standing in a sky full of beings whose weight bent the land, this man registered upon the surroundings as approximately as much as the dirt he was kneeling in.
And he had killed two of them!

Two Infinite True Lifeforms, opened top to bottom, their Pantheons collapsed and their Infinity running out into the gardens, and this body that gave off nothing at all had done that, and that was why the army had arranged itself exactly like this, all of it, ten thousand Triassics and a hundred Mesozoics and six True Lifeforms, and that was why not one single being among them had come close enough to touch him.
They had chained him instead.

Rivers of blue chain wrapped him from shoulder to wrist to knee, and they were not metal, they were Infinity poured into the shape of a chain and set there burning, and worked through every link of them were Pantheonic Dimensional weavings of time that glowed along their length in slow pulses which ran down toward his body and never came back.
And with every pulse, he was being regressed.

His strength was being walked backward down its own road, hauled back through all the years it had spent growing into what it was and held down at a version of himself he had left behind ages ago and kept there, the chains adjusting constantly, tightening the instant the strength beneath them tried to climb, and he had been fighting them for a long time as his hands shook with the effort and his arms kept trying anyway, and it was not working!
And standing in front of him, at her leisure, was the one who had built them.

She was tall and unhurried, her gown made of layered threads of Infinity, pale and blue, the threads forever unspooling from her hem and spooling back up into her shoulders so that she was constantly rebuilding herself out of herself while she stood there.

Her hair was hanging to the backs of her knees in that same pale blue and drifting in a wind that was not present, and her eyes had no whites in them at all, while her bare hands were stained blue-gold to the wrist.
The Woman of Rivers and Ledgers- Ashkavaal, THE Second Breath!
And she crouched down into the ruined gold to bring her face level with his, and she spoke to him kindly.
"I hate your people so much."
"Your bodies give off no authority. None at all. I could stand beside one of you at a market and never know it." Her head tilted as the numbers turned over in her eyes.

"And yet you are this powerful. For what? Explain it to me, please, because I would truly like to understand the arrangement where a thing that weighs nothing gets to break two of my friends open like fruit." Her smile stayed warm.
"Just die already. Die, and give up what you protect, and every part of this stops today."
The golden-haired man said nothing.
"No. Of course not." Ashkavaal sighed and straightened up and brushed at her gown with those stained fingers. "Then let us talk about the two you killed."
She glanced back over her shoulder at the corpses, at the rivers of Infinity running down the terraces, and something in her face when she looked at them was almost real!

"For that, there has to be a price. And I have sadly already killed every Superpowered Lifeform in this garden, so there is nobody left standing here that I can take away from you." She turned back to him and the patience settled over her features again and her voice went light and pleasant. "So I will simply use what I have."
"I am going to raise them."
Her stained hand opened toward the scattered white and blue bodies!

"All of them! Every one of your people lying in this dirt! I will bring them back up as Gamaidjan Lifeforms, the Mad Infinite Dead, and they will not know you, and they will not know themsleves, and they will do exactly what I tell them to do." The smile widened by nothing at all.
"And what I will tell them to do is defile you. One by one. In front of everything gathered here."

"And after I have grown bored of that," Ashkavaal said, "I will do the very same thing for every single Superpowered Lifeform I meet in this Dimension, every one of them, in every garden, for as long as it takes me!"
She leaned down toward him once more.
"Are you ready?"
And the golden-haired man looked up at her!

His eyes were wet and they were not soft in the slightest, the hatred in them gone somewhere past what a face is built to hold, and he looked past her at the corpses of his people lying in the light of their own broken rivers, at all those dozens of white and blue suits scattered across a garden they had died standing in front of, and he ROARED!
OOOOH!

It tore out of him without a shred of authority behind it, no pressure, no weight, nothing that the sky above him would even register as an event, just a chained man on his knees in a ruined garden howling up at ten thousand existences with everything his body had left in it, and the chains flared and pulsed and hauled him backward through his own years all over again, and he kept roaring anyway!
And the army laughed!

It rolled down out of the sky in waves as ranks of Triassic and Mesozoic existences found the whole thing enormously funny, the noise spreading back through formations that went past seeing, a hundred thousand beings enjoying themselves thoroughly at the excitment of what was about to be done, and Ashkavaal raised her stained hand toward the nearest body as she prepared to begin.
And at such a time....the skies above cracked.
CRACK!

They split from one end of the ruined gardens to the other as a white line opened straight across the top of the domain, and the laughter died in the throats of an entire army as something came through.
HUUM!
A massive white draconic beast!

Huge in a way that made the towering True Lifeforms in that sky look like things standing near a mountain, pure white, twin spiral ivory horns, a mane of white flame, wings spread wide enough to shade whole terraces, and gold eyes with ring inside ring for pupils!
And atop it stood three figures!

They came out of the split sky and drew up, and they looked around at the burning terraces and the leaking rivers and the shrine still shining blue-gold in all that smoke, at ten thousand Triassics and a hundred Mesozoics and six True Lifeforms hanging in their formations.
And then, together, they looked down!
Coldly!

Across that entire gathered army, heads turned upward, formations shifted, the laughter was gone, and down in the ruin on his knees in his chains the golden-haired man raised his bleeding face toward the split in the sky as his mouth opened slightly.
Who... the hell were the new entrants?!

chapters.title: Chapter 5540: THE Mortal Coil! I
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
They came through the shimmering boundary, and THE Ymnaros opened around them.

Noah felt Hvitrmarr rein herself in the moment they crossed, her ambient field folding down close against her scales, the vast sovereign weight of a Dimension Steed drawing inward until she read, to the world around her, as merely large rather than as a Steed that predated the Scales, and Noah approved of it silently, because there was no reason to announce themselves to an entire Dimension before he had even looked at it properly.
'Quietly, for now,' he sent through the bond.
'Quietly,' she agreed, and folded further.
And Ruination went to work.
|Preliminary analysis of THE Ymnaros is underway.|

|Early findings, incomplete: this Dimension is not a smaller or simpler thing than THE Krazhor-Nul. It is a different KIND of complex, and it is at least as vast. Nested Observable Existences in numbers the boundary alone could not fully account for. Ambient laws layered in strata, older frameworks buried beneath newer ones. A drawing authority woven through the entire outer shell that has clearly been rebuilt many times. A central production of some resource that bends the local Causes toward itself the way a great mass bends the space around it.|
|Assessment: you have not stepped down into an easier zone. You have stepped sideways into a different one that is equally deep. Full analysis will take time.|
Noah took that in without surprise.

Of course it was as vast. Anaximander did not call a place the largest and most complex Dimension he had found and mean it lightly. This was going to be another deep place, but not as packed with monsters so far above him...hopefully!
And below him, spread across the ruin, was the war.

He saw the armies first, because they filled the sky, Infinite Lifeforms in their tens of thousands with the weakest of them reading at THE Triassic Scale and the tall silent shapes among them reading far, far past it. He saw the broken gardens and the leaking rivers of light. He saw the two enormous corpses split open top to bottom with Infinity pouring out of them, and the scattered white and blue bodies around a blue-gold obelisk that was still, somehow, shining.
And then he saw the one who did not fit.

A single chained figure on his knees in the wreckage. Golden-haired, built like something made on purpose, and emanating NOTHING. Not one wave of authority, not the faintest pressure, standing in a sky full of beings whose weight bent the land, and yet they had not simply killed him. They had wrapped him in rivers of burning blue chain and pinned him there, which told Noah, before he read a single detail, that the thing giving off nothing was the most dangerous thing in the garden.
They were powerful, all of them.
And as Noah gazed down at them, and as thousands of them began to gaze up at him, he did not feel an ounce of fear!

He had watched a Cursed Descendant fold gigaparsecs of a Dimension into a fist. He had died, once, inside a Steed, and come back. This was an army, and an army was a large thing, but a large thing was still just that.
Beside him, Anaximander had gone quiet in a way Noah had never heard from him.

Noah glanced over, and the scholar's face had changed. The mild, curious, tousled explorer who called distance a superstition and smiled at everything was gone, and what stood in his place was cold. His eyes had settled on the scattered white and blue bodies around the obelisk, on the small plain corpses of people who had given off no power and died anyway, and for the first time since Noah had known him, Anaximander looked truly angry.
He said nothing. He did not need to. The chill coming off a man whose whole nature was to make existence conform was its own sentence.
A heavy silence hung in the air.

And on the ground, the most powerful of all the Infinite True Lifeforms present, the tall unhurried woman of unspooling blue threads who had been speaking her vile words to the chained man, looked up at the three figures on the white beast, and raised her stained hands, and spoke coldly.
"Now now. I didn't know there would be reinforcements." Her counting eyes turned over as she smiled up at them. "Though it doesn't change very much. I will simply do the same for all of you."
Noah looked down at her calmly.
And seeing the armies gathered here, seeing the ruin and the corpses and the vast army filling the lands, reminded him of something.
The paintings.

Ulf's paintings, the prophecy hung in oils, the ones Ryaenara's dying brother had made of things that had not happened yet. Armies. Ruin. He was standing inside a scene that carried the same weight those paintings had carried.

But THE Creature was not here. And he did not have Emotive out either. The future those paintings pointed toward had specific pieces in it, and the pieces were not all present, which meant the paintings had not shown one fixed and settled thing at all. They had shown a possibility.

Perhaps parallel possibilities, perhaps potential realities, each one depending on the choices others had not yet made, futures branching off the decisions of every being who had a decision left to make.
Not set in stone!
And as he thought it, he gazed down at the beings below, and he activated THE Protagonist's Omniscient Regard.
His fifth Letter answered, and the Regard settled over the garden, and the sheets bloomed in his sight.
He looked at the woman first.
|CHARACTER SHEET|
|Designation: Ashkavaal, THE Second Breath. An Infinite True Lifeform.|

|Scale: THE Cenozoic Scale, the Sixth. She has not merely reached the Sixth Scale, she has GRASPED the weavings of time within her Pantheon, where the overwhelming majority who reach this Scale never do. Her chains regress. Her defenses age their attackers. Within a set epoch she can rule a capability out of existence entirely, but she is still learning how to do this.|

|Disposition: cruel by preference, patient by training, bored by the ease of most of her work. Enjoys the ones who resist. Hates the Superpowered Lifeforms specifically, and does not know why the hatred runs as deep as it does.|
|Motivation: to take what THE Ymnaros protects. To deliver it upward. She is not the top of the thing she serves.|

|Notable thread: her Infinity does not read as her own. It runs UPWARD out of her, always, in a thin constant thread, toward somewhere she does not seem aware she is feeding. She draws, and she is drawn from, and she does not know it. She is not the only one here of whom this is true. Across the entire army, the same thread runs, thousands of them, all pulling from a well none of them can see and all leaking back toward it, an army that believes its power is its own and has never once been told whose cup it is actually filling. ????? sits at the other end of every thread. ????? is very patient.|
Noah's eyes narrowed at that.
An entire army of Infinite Lifeforms, drawing their Infinity, without knowing it, from a single hidden source?
He set the thread aside carefully, and moved his gaze to the chained man.
|CHARACTER SHEET|
|Designation: Theron Adranos. An Existence Class Superpowered Lifeform.|
|Distinction: Rank S, Ebad. The trembling shield-tree.|

|Nature: emanates no authority whatsoever. This is not weakness and not concealment. It is the SHAPE of his kind. Their power does not press outward on the world as a claim; it simply IS, held entirely inside the body, invisible until it acts. He killed two Infinite True Lifeforms giving off less pressure than the dirt beneath him.|
|Disposition: protective past reason. Grieving. Currently regressed and held; his true Distinction is not what the chains are letting him show.|
|Desire: to guard the shrine. To guard his people. He has failed at the second and will die before he fails at the first.|
|Fears: not death. Only that there will be no one left to stand here after him.|
|Notable thread: the obelisk is not a monument. He is not guarding a symbol. ?????|
Noah gazed down at Theron Adranos, at the golden-haired man who gave off nothing, and at the dead scattered around the shrine he would not stop guarding.
And he weighed something internally.
Death was such a normal part of being human.

So many humans lived, and so many died, that death itself became ordinary to the ones still living, a thing on the news, a thing in the next town, a number that scrolled past. People grew calloused to it because they had to, because a person could not stop and grieve every single one and still get out of bed, and so death became background, became a normal and unremarkable feature of the human world.
But each death was a human.

Each one had held dreams, and hopes, and ideals, and a family, an entire private universe that had taken a whole life to build, and when the death came the universe went out all at once, and to the people around it nothing was ever ordinary about it at all. Only distance made death ordinary. Up close it was the end of a world every single time!
Even his own death.

He had died in THE Krazhor-Nul, and he had come back, but only because he'd had the capability to come back. What if he hadn't? What if the Hepatarch had not answered, and Noah Osmont had simply ended in the dark inside a Steed's body? Amelia would have a son-shaped hole in her forever. Henry, Seo-yeon, Adelaide, Barbatos, every person inside THE Infiniverse waiting for him, would have a critical pillar missing from the center of their lives, a pillar gone, the whole structure left standing crooked around the gap where he had been.
That was death. That was what it took, every time, from someone!
This was human.
And as he thought it, standing in the sky above a garden full of the human dead, something opened in him.
An epiphany, profound and complete, the kind that did not arrive as information but as a door swinging wide onto a room he had always owned and never entered!

He had five Letters. I AM. OSMONT. QUINTESSENTIAL. HUMAN. PROTAGONIST. And the Tongue's growth from here was not more Letters, it was WORDS, and he had known that for a while and had not yet spoken a single one, because a Word had to mean something true enough to carry, and he had been waiting, without knowing he was waiting, for a truth exactly this size.
The human experience. And death.
That was the Word.

Not a Word for power, or conquest, or dominion. A Word for the thing that made the dead in that garden matter, the thing that made his own near-ending matter, the plain unbearable truth that a human life was a whole world and a human death was the ending of one, and that no amount of authority stacked on top of a person changed the naked human thing underneath it, the small mortal creature that dreamed and hoped and could be ended.

He would speak it. And in speaking it, he would impose it. Not on himself alone but on an entire domain, everyone inside it made to stand as what they truly were underneath the power they wore, all authority stripped away, everyone designated as having none at all, so that in this one place the human experience could finally be exactly and only human!
"The first word shall be…THE MORTAL COIL."
HUUM!
"THE DOMAIN…OF THE MORTAL COIL."
|A WORD of THE Osmontian Tongue is forming.|
|Analysis of the forming Word:|
|THE DOMAIN OF THE MORTAL COIL.|

|Function: within its bounds, ALL authority is nullified. Every Scale, every Intent, every Pantheon, every Cause, every claim of power a being has ever stacked upon itself is designated absent. Inside this domain no one has authority, because inside this domain everyone is only what a human is beneath it all: a life that can dream, and hope, and end.|

|Effect on the wielder: as THE True Human Emperor, you alone hold a single privilege inside the absolute leveling. You are permitted the standing of an F-Rank Hunter. The weakest a striving human begins as. Not nothing, a human's beginning. In a domain where no one has any power at all, the beginning of a human's road is a throne.|

|THE Infiniverse and those within are among exclusions if contained within you. If any lifeforms within come out, they will face the same human experience. The cost of bearing THE Infiniverse is paid by the uttered word itself while in effect. All redundancies and conflicts will be actively corrected by the word itself while active.|
|Cost, duration, and reach scale with the truth you speak it upon. Speak it fully.|
Noah looked at the terrible thing he had just made, and he understood exactly what it would do to the garden below, and he did not hesitate!

He gazed down at the army, at Ashkavaal with her stained hands raised, at the thousands of Infinite Lifeforms who wore their power like a birthright and had never once in their long lives been asked to stand without it.

And he opened his mouth, and THE Aura of THE Protagonist bloomed around him as he did, Osmontian Biomass beginning to pour into his reserves in a rising golden tide, generated off the sheer adversity of an entire army arrayed beneath him, breakthrough-weight gathering as he faced down odds that should have crushed him, the numbers climbing and climbing as he drew the breath!
"THE MORTAL COIL."
HUUM!
He spoke the first Word of THE Osmontian Tongue.
HUUM!

It did not sound like a word. It sounded like a fact the world had always known and been waiting to hear said out loud, and it rolled out from him across the ruined gardens of THE Ymnaros and kept rolling, and where it passed, the domain came down.
And below, the Infinite True Lifeforms ran out of patience at the worst possible moment.
Two of the tall shapes among the army began to rise, done with waiting, lifting off the ruined terraces to come and end the reinforcements themselves.
And moments later, they felt their flight falter.

The vibrant, terrible waves of authority and power they had carried since before their first memory, the pressure that was so much a part of them that they had never once thought about it any more than a person thinks about the weight of their own hand...

It began to fade, and thin, and go out, and the two great existences felt themselves growing lighter in the exact way nothing that mighty should ever grow lighter, and their rising stalled, and their bodies began to fall!
DUN!
Across the whole vast reach of the domain, every being was about to learn what it meant to be human!

sentences.text: <THE True Human Emperor>
They came through the shimmering boundary, and THE Ymnaros opened around them.

Noah felt Hvitrmarr rein herself in the moment they crossed, her ambient field folding down close against her scales, the vast sovereign weight of a Dimension Steed drawing inward until she read, to the world around her, as merely large rather than as a Steed that predated the Scales, and Noah approved of it silently, because there was no reason to announce themselves to an entire Dimension before he had even looked at it properly.
'Quietly, for now,' he sent through the bond.
'Quietly,' she agreed, and folded further.
And Ruination went to work.

|Early findings, incomplete: this Dimension is not a smaller or simpler thing than THE Krazhor-Nul.
It is a different KIND of complex, and it is at least as vast.
Nested Observable Existences in numbers the boundary alone could not fully account for.
Ambient laws layered in strata, older frameworks buried beneath newer ones.
A drawing authority woven through the entire outer shell that has clearly been rebuilt many times.
A central production of some resource that bends the local Causes toward itself the way a great mass bends the space around it.|
|Assessment: you have not stepped down into an easier zone.
You have stepped sideways into a different one that is equally deep.
Full analysis will take time.|
Noah took that in without surprise.
Of course it was as vast.
Anaximander did not call a place the largest and most complex Dimension he had found and mean it lightly.
This was going to be another deep place, but not as packed with monsters so far above him...hopefully!

He saw the broken gardens and the leaking rivers of light.
He saw the two enormous corpses split open top to bottom with Infinity pouring out of them, and the scattered white and blue bodies around a blue-gold obelisk that was still, somehow, shining.
And then he saw the one who did not fit.
A single chained figure on his knees in the wreckage.
Golden-haired, built like something made on purpose, and emanating NOTHING.
Not one wave of authority, not the faintest pressure, standing in a sky full of beings whose weight bent the land, and yet they had not simply killed him.

They had wrapped him in rivers of burning blue chain and pinned him there, which told Noah, before he read a single detail, that the thing giving off nothing was the most dangerous thing in the garden.
They were powerful, all of them.

He had watched a Cursed Descendant fold gigaparsecs of a Dimension into a fist.
He had died, once, inside a Steed, and come back.
This was an army, and an army was a large thing, but a large thing was still just that.
Beside him, Anaximander had gone quiet in a way Noah had never heard from him.
Noah glanced over, and the scholar's face had changed.
The mild, curious, tousled explorer who called distance a superstition and smiled at everything was gone, and what stood in his place was cold.

His eyes had settled on the scattered white and blue bodies around the obelisk, on the small plain corpses of people who had given off no power and died anyway, and for the first time since Noah had known him, Anaximander looked truly angry.
He said nothing.
He did not need to.
The chill coming off a man whose whole nature was to make existence conform was its own sentence.
A heavy silence hung in the air.

And on the ground, the most powerful of all the Infinite True Lifeforms present, the tall unhurried woman of unspooling blue threads who had been speaking her vile words to the chained man, looked up at the three figures on the white beast, and raised her stained hands, and spoke coldly.
"Now now.
I didn't know there would be reinforcements." Her counting eyes turned over as she smiled up at them.
"Though it doesn't change very much.
I will simply do the same for all of you."
Noah looked down at her calmly.
And seeing the armies gathered here, seeing the ruin and the corpses and the vast army filling the lands, reminded him of something.
The paintings.
Ulf's paintings, the prophecy hung in oils, the ones Ryaenara's dying brother had made of things that had not happened yet.
Armies.
Ruin.
He was standing inside a scene that carried the same weight those paintings had carried.
But THE Creature was not here.
And he did not have Emotive out either.
The future those paintings pointed toward had specific pieces in it, and the pieces were not all present, which meant the paintings had not shown one fixed and settled thing at all.
They had shown a possibility.

Perhaps parallel possibilities, perhaps potential realities, each one depending on the choices others had not yet made, futures branching off the decisions of every being who had a decision left to make.
Not set in stone!
And as he thought it, he gazed down at the beings below, and he activated THE Protagonist's Omniscient Regard.
His fifth Letter answered, and the Regard settled over the garden, and the sheets bloomed in his sight.
He looked at the woman first.
|CHARACTER SHEET|
|Designation: Ashkavaal, THE Second Breath.
An Infinite True Lifeform.|
|Scale: THE Cenozoic Scale, the Sixth.

Her chains regress.
Her defenses age their attackers.
Within a set epoch she can rule a capability out of existence entirely, but she is still learning how to do this.|
|Disposition: cruel by preference, patient by training, bored by the ease of most of her work.
Enjoys the ones who resist.
Hates the Superpowered Lifeforms specifically, and does not know why the hatred runs as deep as it does.|
|Motivation: to take what THE Ymnaros protects.
To deliver it upward.
She is not the top of the thing she serves.|
|Notable thread: her Infinity does not read as her own.
It runs UPWARD out of her, always, in a thin constant thread, toward somewhere she does not seem aware she is feeding.
She draws, and she is drawn from, and she does not know it.
She is not the only one here of whom this is true.

Across the entire army, the same thread runs, thousands of them, all pulling from a well none of them can see and all leaking back toward it, an army that believes its power is its own and has never once been told whose cup it is actually filling. ????? sits at the other end of every thread. ????? is very patient.|
Noah's eyes narrowed at that.
An entire army of Infinite Lifeforms, drawing their Infinity, without knowing it, from a single hidden source?
He set the thread aside carefully, and moved his gaze to the chained man.

|Designation: Theron Adranos.
An Existence Class Superpowered Lifeform.|
|Distinction: Rank S, Ebad.
The trembling shield-tree.|
|Nature: emanates no authority whatsoever.
This is not weakness and not concealment.
It is the SHAPE of his kind.
Their power does not press outward on the world as a claim; it simply IS, held entirely inside the body, invisible until it acts.
He killed two Infinite True Lifeforms giving off less pressure than the dirt beneath him.|

Grieving.
Currently regressed and held; his true Distinction is not what the chains are letting him show.|

To guard his people.
He has failed at the second and will die before he fails at the first.|

Only that there will be no one left to stand here after him.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5541: THE Mortal Coil! II
paragraphs: The two rising True Lifeforms fell out of the sky!

They had lifted off the ruined terraces at the very moment THE MORTAL COIL came down as they were done with waiting and coming up to end the reinforcements themselves, and so they were the highest things in the sky when their power went out, and there was nothing beneath them but air and a very... long way down.
They fell.

And they were enormous, mountains given the shape of bodies, and even stripped down to nothing they were still that big, still that heavy, and mass falling from that height did what mass falling from that height does to anything at all, no matter how mighty it had been a breath ago.
BOOM!

The first one hit the scorched land and the ground came up around it in a crater, and Noah heard the sound its body made, and it was not the sound of a titan striking earth, it was the sound of bones.
Snapping. In their dozens!

A giant made human and then dropped, and every part of it that had been holding a mountain's worth of weight came apart under that weight the instant the authority that had carried it so lightly for ages was simply gone, and the second one came down a heartbeat later in its own crater with its own long chorus of breaking, and then the gardens of THE Ymnaros filled with a sound that this Dimension had, in all its ages of war, quite possibly never heard once.
"AHHH!"
"AWOOO!"
Two Infinite True Lifeforms, SCREAMING.

Screaming, high and ragged and utterly without dignity, the raw animal sound of a living thing in more pain than it had ever been built to feel, because pain was a human thing and these two had never in their long existences been human until right now, and it had found them all at once, and they had no idea what to do with it!
They writhed in their craters and they wailed, and they bled.
And Noah gazed out at the rest of the army.
Their faces had gone ashen.

Thousands of them, tens of thousands, the whole vast army that had filled the sky with its weight, and across every single face was the same dawning horror as the Infinity they had felt inside themselves since before their first memory, the constant private river of power that was more theirs than their own names...simply was not there anymore.

They reached for it the way a person reaches for a step that is not where they left it, and found nothing, and the nothing was worse than any blow Noah could have struck, because a blow they would have understood!
Even beside him, it expressed itself.
Ryaenara, the Mirthful Antiquity, made a small startled sound and pressed both hands flat to her own chest, and her eyes went wide, because she did not feel an ounce of power inside herself either!

And the high winds of THE Ymnaros caught at a body that suddenly had nothing anchoring it to anything and nearly took her clean off the platform, until Anaximander's hand closed on her shoulder and held her down.
The scholar himself stood steady, because he was simply built different, but even he had gone quiet with the strangeness of it.

And beneath them all, Hvitrmarr began to descend, slowly, because Noah patted her scales and she brought them down, and she brought them down the ordinary way, wings and weight and air, because Hvitrmarr did not have access to a single shred of authority inside this domain either.
She was, right now, a massive white reptile with wings. A very large animal, gliding down toward a garden!
Everybody was human!
For the briefest instant, as the Word settled, Noah had seen the woman below try to fight it.

Ashkavaal. THE Second Breath. He had watched her stained hands come up and watched weavings of time bloom off her fingers, her one real answer to a thing like this, and for a fraction of a moment those weavings had strained against as she tried to argue that authority-nullification was a law not yet invented where she stood, or already long obsolete, tried to wrap her own time around herself and step out of the human condition Noah had spoken over the world.
She was still learning!

But Noahs word was a TRUTH, and truth did not negotiate with a technique that hadn't finished growing in, and so the domain settled over her weavings with a plain and total finality! Noah watched the vibrant rivers of Infinity and power that had wreathed her entire body dim, and thin, and go dark, until the tall unhurried woman of unspooling blue threads was simply a titanic human standing in a ruined garden with stained hands and nothing behind them.
And across the wreckage, the chains vanished.

The rivers of burning blue chain that had wrapped Theron Adranos shoulder to wrist to knee, Infinity poured into the shape of a shackle and worked through with weavings of time, were made of exactly the authority the domain had just designated absent, and so they simply ceased, all at once, and the golden-haired man dropped the last inch to his knees free.
He rose.
Slowly, clenching his fists, testing a body that no longer had a leash on it, and he looked up toward the descending white beast and the three figures upon it.

His eyes moved across them and locked onto Anaximander, and recognition crossed his bloodied face as if he had seen this scholar before, as if the mild man in the white robes was not a stranger to him at all!
And Noah felt the strangest thing he had felt in a very long time.
His own immensity was gone.

The crown hung loose on his head, but the Causes, the Foundations, the A-Rank seas, the fused authority that could resuscitate a dead Observable Existence, all of it designated absent, all of it stepped back behind a line his own Word had drawn, and what was left standing on Hvitrmarr's descending back was a man. Just a man!

And Noah, THE True Human Emperor, felt himself returned to a sensation he had not touched since the very beginning of everything, since a fireball skillbook, since the first time he had ever reached inside a feeble human body and felt a thin thread of mana answer!
Oh!
That was what this was! Truly human!

He reached inside himself, and his Osmontian Source Infinity was still there, still his, still coursing through him exactly as it always had, except now he could only touch it at the scale a Rank F Hunter could touch anything. A trickle. A thread!

And truly, even this was not accurate as an F Rank Hunter could not truly touch something like Osmontian Source Infinity. So it was more accurate to say that he could display the power as THE True Human Emperor...at the level of a Rank F Hunter as designated in his home world.

The whole ocean was inside him and he was permitted to draw a single sliver from it, because that was the privilege the Word had left him, the standing of a human at the very start of the road, the weakest a striving person begins as!
It was surreal past describing to be nearly as weak as a normal human again, and to have chosen it, and to be standing in the middle of an army while he did.
|THE Aura of THE Protagonist is registering the change in your condition.|

|You have designated yourself an F-Rank Hunter within a domain containing an army of former True Lifeforms and Infinite Lifeforms, all reduced to the same human baseline. The adversity you now face is calculated against your CURRENT standing, not your true one.|

|You are, functionally, a single human standing alone against tens of thousands of humans, any one of whom could potentially kill you with their bare hands should they reach you. The adversity multiplier has scaled tremendously.|

|Osmontian Biomass generation is climbing accordingly. Current intake: 400,000, and rising as the army grasps its situation. Projected sustained yield while this state holds: in the tens of millions. This is the single richest field THE Aura of THE Protagonist has ever stood upon.|

Slowly, clenching his fists, testing a body that no longer had a leash on it, and he looked up toward the descending white beast and the three figures upon it.

His eyes moved across them and locked onto Anaximander, and recognition crossed his bloodied face as if he had seen this scholar before, as if the mild man in the white robes was not a stranger to him at all!
And Noah felt the strangest thing he had felt in a very long time.
His own immensity was gone.

The crown hung loose on his head, but the Causes, the Foundations, the A-Rank seas, the fused authority that could resuscitate a dead Observable Existence, all of it designated absent, all of it stepped back behind a line his own Word had drawn, and what was left standing on Hvitrmarr's descending back was a man.
Just a man!

And Noah, THE True Human Emperor, felt himself returned to a sensation he had not touched since the very beginning of everything, since a fireball skillbook, since the first time he had ever reached inside a feeble human body and felt a thin thread of mana answer!
Oh!
That was what this was!
Truly human!

He reached inside himself, and his Osmontian Source Infinity was still there, still his, still coursing through him exactly as it always had, except now he could only touch it at the scale a Rank F Hunter could touch anything.
A trickle.
A thread!
And truly, even this was not accurate as an F Rank Hunter could not truly touch something like Osmontian Source Infinity.
So it was more accurate to say that he could display the power as THE True Human Emperor...at the level of a Rank F Hunter as designated in his home world.

The whole ocean was inside him and he was permitted to draw a single sliver from it, because that was the privilege the Word had left him, the standing of a human at the very start of the road, the weakest a striving person begins as!
It was surreal past describing to be nearly as weak as a normal human again, and to have chosen it, and to be standing in the middle of an army while he did.
|THE Aura of THE Protagonist is registering the change in your condition.|
|You have designated yourself an F-Rank Hunter within a domain containing an army of former True Lifeforms and Infinite Lifeforms, all reduced to the same human baseline.
The adversity you now face is calculated against your CURRENT standing, not your true one.|
|You are, functionally, a single human standing alone against tens of thousands of humans, any one of whom could potentially kill you with their bare hands should they reach you.
The adversity multiplier has scaled tremendously.|
|Osmontian Biomass generation is climbing accordingly.
Current intake: 400,000, and rising as the army grasps its situation.
Projected sustained yield while this state holds: in the tens of millions.
This is the single richest field THE Aura of THE Protagonist has ever stood upon.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5542: THE Mortal Coil! III
paragraphs: Noah's eyes gleamed as the golden tide poured into his reserves.
He was farming an entire army by standing in front of it as a man!

And as Hvitrmarr's claws touched the ground, and the vast White Steed settled her weight onto the scorched earth of THE Ymnaros, Noah stepped forward on her back and looked down at the horrified army, and he spoke, calm and grand.
"For the first time in your entire existence," he said, "all of you are going to get a feel for what it means to be human."
"No power. No authority. Not for anybody here." His gaze swept them. "Every one of us, absolutely the same, at the exact same baseline."
He then he glanced, almost kindly, toward the two craters.

"For you two, it's rather unfortunate. You were flying." His voice stayed even. "Falling from a height like that as a human does a great deal of damage. You've broken a lot of bones. You very likely have internal bleeding right now, and you have never once in your lives had to know what that is."
And Noah looked at the two titanic figures wailing in their craters, and let everyone watch them!
They were experiencing what it meant to be human, and it was horrifying.

Both of them wept, openly, helplessly, tears and snot running down enormous faces as they sobbed and wailed from a pain so far past anything in their experience that their minds had nowhere to put it. Beings that had spent ages as apex existences, that had split their enemies open and reanimated the dead for sport, reduced to sobbing humans in the dirt because a nerve was doing the job a nerve does!
And neither of them could make it stop, and neither of them understood that it would not simply stop the way everything unpleasant had always stopped for them before.
And every being in the garden watched, in horrified silence, as though the two were being held up as examples.
And their conditions were getting worse.

One of them, Noah saw now, had come down wrong. When it had first lifted off the terraces to rise, its own ascent had shoved a jagged shelf of rock up out of the broken ground, and when the power died and it fell, it had come down onto that shelf neck-first, and the stone had gone into the side of its throat, and now, as a human, it was bleeding from the neck in long steady pulses that darkened the scorched earth around its head.
The garden watched it bleed.
The wailing from that one grew weaker.

The screams thinned into whimpers, and the whimpers into a wet shallow breathing, and the enormous body that had thrashed in its crater began to move less, and then less, and then only its chest, and then the pulses from its throat slowed to match, and across a garden full of beings that had never watched anything of their own kind die of something as small and stupid as a rock, an Infinite True Lifeform cried quieter and quieter until it stopped, and lay still!

The surviving titan, broken in its own crater, turned its weeping face and watched its companion go still, and the terror that came over its features then was a wholly new thing in that ancient face, because it had finally understood that the pain it was in was not a punishment that would end but a process that was going somewhere, and that the somewhere was where the other one had just gone.
Death!
Noah stepped down off Hvitrmarr and walked toward it.

He walked grandly across the ruined gold, a small figure crossing a giant's graveyard, and he looked up at the surviving True Lifeform with an expression that was almost gentle, and he explained to it what was happening.

"A human body holds about five liters of blood. You can lose a little and feel nothing. Lose about a third of it, and the body starts to panic, the heart races trying to move what isn't there, everything goes cold from the outside in as the body gives up its edges to protect its center." He nodded toward the still corpse.

"Your friend lost it out of the neck, which is fast. Past about half, the center can't be protected either, and the whole thing simply shuts down, one system at a time, while you stay awake for most of it."
He let the silence hold.

"The pain you're feeling right now, the pain that's so big you can't think around it, a human feels a version of that from a broken arm. One arm. You have broken most of what you have, and you're bleeding on the inside where nothing can reach it, and your body is going to spend the next while shutting its own doors one by one while you feel every single one close." His voice did not rise.
"That's what you are, underneath. That's what all of you always were, underneath. This is... the mortal coil."
HUUM!
And around him, the Infinite Lifeforms of the host moved backwards!
They stepped away from him, thousands of them, this small unarmed human walking through their ruined battlefield describing death like a thing he had studied!
But....a certain Infinite True Lifeform was not finished.
WAA!
Ashkavaal moved.

She jumped from where she stood at the base of the obelisk and crossed the whole ruined distance in a single human leap of a giant's body, and she came down in front of Noah and rose to her full height.

She was titanic, more than five times the height of the man standing in front of her, a mountain in the shape of a woman even with every river of Infinity dimmed off her skin, and she looked down at him with her stained hands and her somber cold face.

"You said we are all human here." Her voice came low and level. "For you to lay a domain like this over reality with your own Pantheon, you must be bound by it too. That is how it works. That is how it always works."

"So. We may all be humans here." Her dimmed eyes fixed on the small figure below her. "But we are not all equal. You are still a bug compared to me. A human bug in front of a human mountain." Her stained fingers curled. "Let me give you a taste of your own medicine."

A titanic Infinite Lifeform stripped of every shred of her power, and still a giant, still a mountain of a body that could close one hand around Noah entirely, glaring down at THE True Human Emperor who stood barely a fraction of her size in the ruined gold!
And Noah, small, human, smiled coldly.

Behind him, larger than the Infinite Lifeforms and larger than the corpses, THE White Steed did not move a single muscle as she stared down at Ashkavaal over the top of Noah's head, one gold eye fixed on the giant who had just made a decision.
In a domain where all of existence had been brought down to the human condition, to the mortal...
Someone wanted to step on THE True Human Emperor?!
