chapters.title: Chapter 5543: THE Mortal Coil! IV
paragraphs: Ashkavaal's hand came down to squish him.

It was the size of a small mountain and it moved with the full unhurried confidence of a being who had just done the math and found a human at the bottom of it, and it reached for Noah to close around him and be done with the whole ridiculous afternoon!
And Noah calmly read out a skill he had used years ago in dungeons.
"Fireball."
HUUM!
A ball of deeply cerulean flame formed in the air in front of him.

It was small, the humble first spell of a Rank F Hunter who did not yet know he would one day bring back Observable Existences and Steeds, except the mana feeding it now was Osmontian Source Infinity drawn through the narrow straw the domain allowed him, and even a single river of THAT ocean was not the same thing as a beginner's mana at all.
The cerulean fireball smashed into Ashkavaal's descending palm and flung the titanic hand away, scorched black across its whole surface, the giant's arm knocked wide.
And Noah moved brutally.

More cerulean fireballs erupted in the air in front of him like bullets leaving a barrel, one after another after another, a stream of them, and they slammed upward into Ashkavaal's chest and her body was shockingly thrown up into the air by the impacts, a mountain of a woman lifted clean off her feet!

And while she hung there more of them came in from other angles, fireballs curving in on separate trajectories that Noah's narrow trickle of Infinity guided true, each one landing with a heavy wet impact that burst skin and blew muscle apart in cerulean flashes!
She could not scream in time. She could barely fall in time!

By the time THE Second Breath came back down she was no longer recognizable as a woman or as anything, only a spinning mass of ruined flesh turning over in the air, and it smashed down onto the scorched land seconds later and did not move, and there was no sign of life left in it at all!
Oh!
The most powerful Infinite True Lifeform in the garden. Dead! Killed by the first spell Noah had ever learned!
A heavy silence spread across the whole ruin.
Noah stood in the middle of it, and he turned slowly and let his gaze move across all of them, every ashen face in the army.
"Kneel," he said, "and your deaths will be quick."
HUUM!
The words were heavy!
Then one of the Infinite True Lifeforms reined in its fear, and threw back its head, and roared.
"HE IS ONLY ONE MAN!" it bellowed across the army with fear and rage!
"There are TENS OF THOUSANDS of us! SWARM THIS MOTHERFUCKER!"
And the army came!
And Noah...waded into it.

What followed was not a battle so much as a demonstration, brutal and one-sided and moving, a single human body crossing an army and unmaking it as it went. He reinforced himself where he needed to, pulling his narrow rivers of Osmontian Source Infinity across his skin an instant before impact so that a giant's fist that should have pulped him instead broke itself on him.
Then he punched back, and where his fist landed the body of an Infinite Lifeform simply exploded, ages of existence blown apart by a jab!
He moved through them and they died.

He turned and threw a barrage of cerulean fireballs into a knot of charging shapes and they came apart in the air. He ducked under a swung arm and drove his palm up through a torso and out the other side. And at one point, hemmed in on every side by rushing bodies, Noah raised his hand and uttered a single word.
"Sever."
HUUM!
A bolt of blue lightning released from his hand, and it chained.

It leapt from body to body across the packed host, hundreds of them, jumping conductor to conductor exactly the way it had jumped across many enemies a lifetime ago, and every Infinite Lifeform it touched exploded as it passed through, a line of bursting bodies chasing the bolt across the battlefield!
Noah watched it chain and felt something warm and strange move through him.
Nostalgia.
He had loved this spell!
So he cast it again.
"Sever."
HUUM!
And again the blue lightning chained across the rushing army, and again hundreds of them burst apart along its path, and it was pure one-sided brutality, a man walking through an army of humans!
And after a certain point, it broke them.
Noah cut down the last surviving Infinite True Lifeform, and he cut down more than eighty percent of the entire army.

The rushing tide that had been trying to swarm him simply stopped, and reversed, and the beings who had come to end the reinforcements began to back away, and then to run, terror finally beating out fury as they fled across the ruined gardens in every direction!
Noah gazed at all of them coldly.
Anaximander came to stand beside him in the sudden quiet, stepping over a scorched corpses, his anger cooled back into the mild watchful thing Noah knew.
"I didn't jump in because..." the scholar said, looking out at the fleeing remnants. "It seemed like you wanted to experience something. Thank you for intervening."
Noah nodded calmly.
He turned away from the scattering army, following the direction of Anaximander's gaze, toward the obelisk that still shone its steady blue-gold through all the ruin.
Toward Theron Adranos.

The golden-haired man stood before the shrine, in the midst of the corpses of his own people, and he was looking at Noah with a heavy gaze. He nodded once to Anaximander, an acknowledgment between two who clearly knew each other, and then he spoke toward Noah.

"I cannot thank you enough for the intervention." His voice was low and worn. "I wish to take a moment to bury my brethren here. We are born ordinary in these lands, and we die ordinary in these lands."
He looked down at the white and blue bodies scattered around the obelisk's base. "Sir Anaximander. Could you lend me a hand?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5544: Extinction I
paragraphs: Anaximander crossed to the dead and looked down at them, and began to help.

Noah stood in the middle of a field of corpses and took one more breath of it. There was a human satisfaction in standing in the aftermath of a thing he had done with almost no effort, and he let himself have it a moment longer. Brutal as the field was, it was human too. Humans were bloody. Humans were not always pretty.

Hvitrmarr walked over to him the ordinary way, on four legs across the ruin. Without her authority she was still enormous, and she crushed corpse after corpse flat beneath her without noticing she did it. On the ridge of her spine Ryaenara held on and did everything she could not to be thrown off a moving reptile, looking down at Noah and shaking her head at the whole scene.
The grand prompts bloomed in front of him.
|Adversity resolved. THE Aura of THE Protagonist final tally for the engagement:|
|Osmontian Biomass gained: 61,400,000.|
|You faced an army as a single human at F-Rank standing. The adversity multiplier held at its peak throughout. This is the richest single harvest THE Aura of THE Protagonist has produced.|
|Total Osmontian Biomass reserves: 86,400,000.|
|THE Tide That Owes Nothing has been triggered.|

|You have granted death to True Lifeforms and to thousands of Infinite Lifeforms. Death, cleanly given to those who had earned an ending, is its own kind of giving, and the Tide answers giving of every kind. A boon is returned, and it has taken a shape.|
HUUM!
Something spun out of the settling gold and dropped into his open palm.

An obsidian blue necklace, a single dark stone on a fine dark cord. The stone did not hold still. Inside it Infinity turned over and over, an ocean of it folded into a jewel small enough to close a hand around, cerulean light moving in its depths the way light moves in deep water, far down and alive.
|THE Woven Return: THE Tessellated Heart of the Borrowed Flame.|
|A necklace holding a contained thread of Infinity. It arrives interlinked with the knowledge of what you just witnessed.|

|Every Infinite Lifeform you faced drew their Infinity, without knowing it, from a single distant being. A Descendant of Those Who Remain, whose entire existence is Infinity that it lends outward across multitudes who mistake the loan for a possession. Its designation, carried to you along this necklace's own borrowed thread: THE Infinity Eater.|

|Infinity is not something it has. Infinity is something it is. It has spread thin threads of itself into every wielder who draws Infinity without a source of their own, and it feels through each one, and what it lends it owns, and what it owns it may reclaim, or wear, or drown from the inside, at any moment it chooses. Any being who wields Infinity without a well of their own is a mouth THE Infinity Eater has not yet decided to close.|

|The necklace is itself a strand of that borrowed flame, contained and yours. Through it, one who holds sufficient Infinity of their own may reach along the threads to their far end and send a message to THE Infinity Eater directly. Should you even send a message though? Why would you?|
Noah went still, turning the stone over in his fingers.

His own Infinity had a source. It came from his Infinite Cause, seated inside him. It had never occurred to him that this was a defense. But it was! A power he had made himself had no thread running out of it, and a thing with no thread could not be reached down and reclaimed. There was no loan. There was no lender. He owned himself completely!
The thing at the far end of ten thousand borrowed threads was another matter. Noah frowned at the stone, and set the problem down as he let THE MORTAL COIL go.

The Word drew back into him like a tide pulling off a shore. Across the gardens the weight of the world returned. Power welled up again in everything still alive to hold it, in Ryaenara, who drew a sharp breath as her existence came back to her, in Hvitrmarr, whose reined weight settled once more against her scales, in Noah himself, his ocean widening back from a single river to the full crowned depth of THE Quintessential Osmontian.
And as it did, something buzzed.
"Oh?"
Noah paused, surprised as he felt a small insistent vibration, from something he had put away. He waved a hand and took it out.

The tiny egg. The Tide's reward for the resuscitation of Hvitrmarr, the strange small thing he had tucked away! It sat trembling in his palm at a high frequency, and an utterly despotic and ancient aura began to rise off it!
The egg cracked.

The shell split along a seam that had not been there a moment before, and a beam of gray light shot up out of it, straight up past Hvitrmarr's height and higher, until it stopped at a point in the sky.
HUUM!

There, the point folded inward, drawing space toward a center that felt less like a place than a wound. Gray threads thick as rivers pulled in from everywhere at once and lashed themselves around it, layer over crossing layer, until a webbed cocoon hung over the gardens of THE Ymnaros like a second sky, and the ancient weight that had leaked from the egg now poured off the cocoon in a steady tide.
Everything below went still!

Out at the edges of the ruin, the last fleeing remnants of the army simply fell, and where they fell they began to rot. Theron Adranos straightened from the grave he was digging. Anaximander turned, and his mild face went heavy. Ryaenara said a word in a language older than the Scales, low, under her breath. And Hvitrmarr, who had faced down an army of giants without moving a muscle, took one slow step back!
The cocoon opened.
The webbing unwound itself strand by strand, without hurry, as though the thing inside had waited long enough that a few moments more cost it nothing!
What came out of it was enormous, and it was old, old the way the bottom of the sea is old. It unfolded against the sky in a body built for a war by an age that had lost the war anyway.
Gray flesh like weathered stone, scarred in places where the scars had scars. Plates that had grown across it rather than been forged onto it. Too many limbs, each too long.
Hanging off it and swaying were chains and cords and rags of materials no one living could have named, the wreckage of old bindings it had broken or simply outlasted.
Across its eyes was a blindfold made of hands.

Small ones, mummified and gray, hundreds of them layered palm over palm around the titan's head, fingers laced into fingers in a pattern nothing sane had arranged. Whether the hands were there to keep existence out of its eyes or to keep its eyes off existence was not a question the sight of it invited anyone to ask.
It matched no taxonomy. It looked foreign down to the bone, ancient and wrong!
Even Noah was shaken. He stood in his field of corpses with the cracked egg still warm in his palm and looked up at the thing, and for a moment did nothing else.

Then the titan moved. It lowered itself out of the sky with the same slow dignity, and came down before Noah with a weight the ground took in silence because the ground had no other option. And without a sound, it knelt. It folded its too-many limbs and brought the blindfolded head low, down and down, until the band of gray hands hung level with the small human standing in the ruined gold, and there it held, kneeling, silent as the deep!
|THE Tide That Owes Nothing has completed a Woven Return long held in reserve.|
|The reward: an extinct lifeform.|
|At the core of its existence sit 36 Causes. They are not the Causes as you know them. They are Blighted Causes and Calcified Causes.|
|It is loyal only to you. It can come whenever it is called, from wherever it is, across whatever stands between.|

|How this Return was woven: when you resuscitated Hvitrmarr, you resuscitated a Cursed Lifeform bound to Those Who Remain, and you did it through replacement, collapsing terminal Causes and seating new ones. That act altered cause and effect across existence and time. Weavings of that shape had not moved through existence since the age this lifeform died in. The Tide followed them back to the only thing they still resembled, found this, and began the long work of returning it to you. The egg was that work. It has been maturing since the moment she was cured.|
|What is known of its history: it, and all others like it, were driven to extinction by the direct order of Those Who Remain.|
|Any further information...|
|...has been blocked.|
|The extinct lifeform has closed the record with its own will, and has given a single reason for doing so.|
|It wishes to introduce itself to you.|

sentences.text: Anaximander crossed to the dead and looked down at them, and began to help.
Noah stood in the middle of a field of corpses and took one more breath of it.
There was a human satisfaction in standing in the aftermath of a thing he had done with almost no effort, and he let himself have it a moment longer.
Brutal as the field was, it was human too.
Humans were bloody.
Humans were not always pretty.
Hvitrmarr walked over to him the ordinary way, on four legs across the ruin.
Without her authority she was still enormous, and she crushed corpse after corpse flat beneath her without noticing she did it.
On the ridge of her spine Ryaenara held on and did everything she could not to be thrown off a moving reptile, looking down at Noah and shaking her head at the whole scene.
The grand prompts bloomed in front of him.
|Adversity resolved.
THE Aura of THE Protagonist final tally for the engagement:|
|Osmontian Biomass gained: 61,400,000.|
|You faced an army as a single human at F-Rank standing.
The adversity multiplier held at its peak throughout.
This is the richest single harvest THE Aura of THE Protagonist has produced.|
|Total Osmontian Biomass reserves: 86,400,000.|
|THE Tide That Owes Nothing has been triggered.|
|You have granted death to True Lifeforms and to thousands of Infinite Lifeforms.
Death, cleanly given to those who had earned an ending, is its own kind of giving, and the Tide answers giving of every kind.
A boon is returned, and it has taken a shape.|
HUUM!
Something spun out of the settling gold and dropped into his open palm.
An obsidian blue necklace, a single dark stone on a fine dark cord.
The stone did not hold still.

Inside it Infinity turned over and over, an ocean of it folded into a jewel small enough to close a hand around, cerulean light moving in its depths the way light moves in deep water, far down and alive.
|THE Woven Return: THE Tessellated Heart of the Borrowed Flame.|
|A necklace holding a contained thread of Infinity.
It arrives interlinked with the knowledge of what you just witnessed.|
|Every Infinite Lifeform you faced drew their Infinity, without knowing it, from a single distant being.
A Descendant of Those Who Remain, whose entire existence is Infinity that it lends outward across multitudes who mistake the loan for a possession.
Its designation, carried to you along this necklace's own borrowed thread: THE Infinity Eater.|
|Infinity is not something it has.
Infinity is something it is.

It has spread thin threads of itself into every wielder who draws Infinity without a source of their own, and it feels through each one, and what it lends it owns, and what it owns it may reclaim, or wear, or drown from the inside, at any moment it chooses.
Any being who wields Infinity without a well of their own is a mouth THE Infinity Eater has not yet decided to close.|
|The necklace is itself a strand of that borrowed flame, contained and yours.
Through it, one who holds sufficient Infinity of their own may reach along the threads to their far end and send a message to THE Infinity Eater directly.
Should you even send a message though?
Why would you?|
Noah went still, turning the stone over in his fingers.
His own Infinity had a source.
It came from his Infinite Cause, seated inside him.
It had never occurred to him that this was a defense.
But it was!
A power he had made himself had no thread running out of it, and a thing with no thread could not be reached down and reclaimed.
There was no loan.
There was no lender.
He owned himself completely!
The thing at the far end of ten thousand borrowed threads was another matter.

chapters.title: Chapter 5545: Extinction II
paragraphs: Noah looked up at the thing that had knelt to him, and gave it an order.
"Introduce yourself to me."
HUUM!

The hands moved. The band of small gray palms laced across the titan's eyes unlaced itself finger from finger, slow and deliberate, and where it parted a gray light began to leak, thin at first and then steady, spilling down the ruined gardens like water finding its level.

Behind him, Ryaenara made no sound. When Noah caught her face at the edge of his vision the humor had gone out of it, and under the stillness sat something he would have called fear on anyone else. At the foot of the obelisk, Anaximander had stopped working. Theron Adranos stood beside him, and both men had gone gray in the face.
The light reached Noah, and everything stopped.

Existence caught and held around him, the way it did when he stretched an instant thin to think inside it, except he had not done this. His vision folded and reopened somewhere that was not the gardens of THE Ymnaros. The light of the sky here came from a source he could not find, and the air carried the weight of a place a long way back, counted in years he had no number for!

He stood in a dark sky. Beside him, filling half of what he could see, hung the visage of the extinct lifeform, no longer kneeling and no longer small against anything, present the way a mountain is present.
It spoke, and the voice came up through him rather than into him.

"Consider a flame," Damodred said. "You would say it is a thing. It has a name, it has a shape, you could point to it. And yet a flame is not a thing at all. It is an event. It is something that is happening, burning itself forward moment to moment, and the instant it stops happening there is no flame left over to bury. There is only the dark where it was."
The great head turned, unhurried.

"I am Damodred. And once, I was happening. I was grand, if you like the word, though grandeur is only a flame that has learned to admire itself. We were known as the Laestrygonians. And there came a day when Those Who Remain decided that our particular fire was one that existence could do without."
Below them, an ancient domain unfolded.

It came up out of the dark in pieces, the way a drowned country surfaces, and Noah understood he was being shown a corpse dressed in the memory of when it had been a home. Cities and whole Dimensions at once, climbing across a black plain in tiers built to outlast the ground beneath them, towers of dark seamed stone that had been grown rather than cut, each rooted downward into the plain by structures that ran out of sight.

Roads worn to a shine by feet no longer present ran between them. Rivers carried the same gray light the titan bled. And over all of it hung a sky crowded with more cities, hung upside down from nothing, their lights answering the lights below.

"Watch them, my first and new Master" Damodred said, gentle as a man pointing out a bird. "And ask yourself what a people is. It is a pattern that has decided to keep itself. That is all. A shape that insists, against everything, on continuing to be that shape."

The people moved through the memory in their millions, built like Damodred, huge and gray and scarred even in their prime, a race that seemed to have come into existence already looking like the survivors of something. And they were strong.
Each of them held Causes at the core of their existence, and the Causes were wrong in a precise and terrible way, wounded and then hardened, the same 36 that sat inside Damodred now.
The memory showed what that meant when it was tested.

A Primeval Lifeform came down on one of the hanging Dimensions, apex because earliest, its weavings sitting beneath every framework these people climbed. And the Laestrygonians met it in their thousands and took it apart, their calcified Causes refusing to yield to a thing that expected all younger things to yield as a matter of course.
"The oldest things in existence assume the young will bow," Damodred said. "It is a reasonable assumption. It is almost always correct. We were the place the assumption went to die."
Whatever came for them, they came out on top. They prospered. Their Dimensions climbed and hung and shone, and for an age no power in existence could make them kneel.
Then the memory changed its light, and Noah knew, before it showed him, that he was about to watch it end.
Armies of Descendants veiled in shifting many-colored light descended.

They came in numbers the memory did not trouble to count, filling the crowded sky between the upside-down Dimensions, and at their head moved something the Laestrygonians had no name for beyond the one it was given. The memory could render it only as an absence, a place in the sky where the light declined to go, and out of that place a voice reached down across the whole domain.
|Your lifeform is vile, and not conducive to existence. Perish.|
HUUM!

"That was the first time we heard that voice, and the last. You will notice," Damodred said, and here for the first time the calm thinned, not into rage but into something more precise beneath it, "that it did not threaten us. A threat is a kind of respect. A threat admits you are real enough to be argued with. It simply announced."
Noah watched the extinction the way Damodred needed him to watch it, without looking away.

The calcified Causes that had thrown down Primevals held, at first. The Dimensions that had stood longer than their own ground held. And then, one by one, they stopped holding, because the thing in the sky was not fighting them. It was overruling them. It unmade the sentence of their existence with the flat authority of a lineage that believed existence was theirs.

The hanging Dimensions came down into the standing ones. The gray light in the rivers went dark. The millions who had never once knelt were made to stop, ended and struck out of the record of what was permitted to be.

"Death…" Damodred said over the ruin, softly, "almost no one who fears it understands it, because fear is a poor teacher. Death is not the enemy of life. Death is the shape life makes at its edge, the way the shore is the shape the sea makes where it stops. To live is to be the kind of thing that ends. We knew this. We had made our peace with the shore." The voice cooled by a single degree.

"What was done to us was not death. Death would have been ours. This was a hand reaching in from outside the whole arrangement to declare that our particular wave was not allowed to have broken in the first place. That is not an ending as much as it is an erasure of the beginning. And that, I have never made peace with."
The memory slowed.

It showed a last work, carried out in the dark while the domain came down around it. The Laestrygonians reaching into their own dying Causes and laying something inside them, a marking, a seed, the memory of themselves written into the one part of existence that might outlast everything.

"We laid our Existential Genetic Markers into our Causes," Damodred said. "Think of a message placed not in a bottle but in the tide itself. We could not choose when it would wash up, or where, or into whose hands. We could only trust that existence is fond of repeating its rare accidents, and that one day, somewhere far ahead, Causes strange enough would meet and mingle in just the way ours once had, and stir what we had left sleeping."
The uncovered gray eyes found Noah at last.

"You, The Master, have grasped the markers of our Causes. What you did to the Steed sent that old shape back through existence, like a note struck once, long ago, sounding again. I am the first to wake to it."
The dark sky held around them, and the ruined domain hung below, and the titan told him what it wanted!
"I place myself at your service. And I ask one thing in return. It need not be soon. I know the weight of what I ask."
"The dissolution of the one who put out the flame of my people. THE Sleepless Fiend, and every Progeny it fathered. Root and line. This...is what I seek."
BOOM!
Noah stood in the memory of a murdered people, and the extinct thing beside him waited on his answer.
"Does The Master believe... such a thing is possible? Can it be done?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5546: What is a Cause?
paragraphs: Did he believe it was possible?
To move against the Progeny of one of Those Who Remain, and against the very ancient entity that had fathered them across the dark of epochs…
THE Sleepless Fiend of Those Who Remain...!

As the fiendish ancient aura of THE Primeval Osmontian Marrow rippled softly across his hair, Noah evaluated everything, knowing he was already hunted by the Cursed Descendants of THE Krazhor-Nul Dimension and realizing the Fiend's lineage ran through that exact same cursed blood!

He had already made an enemy of one branch of Those Who Remain simply by existing well! The question was never whether adding another branch was dangerous, but what it actually cost when stacked atop an active war he was already fighting, and as he weighed the outcome in the quiet depths of his mind, the added weight was smaller than it looked.
His existence answered before his mouth ever opened, his Intent leaning forward without hesitation as he looked down at the enormous scarred titan.
"In existence," Noah said, "anything is possible. I won't make you a definitive promise. But this is something we can work toward."
HUUM!

The veil of severed hands twitched as Damodred bowed heavily, his colossal frame of petrified muscle and calcified scars folding down further than any kneel, sending a tremor through the ruined strata of the domain!
The titan showed nothing aloud, yet Noah could feel the boundless loss and ancient rage churning behind that calm exterior, for this ancient being was also human by its own unyielding definition!
Noah let him have the moment, standing composed amidst the falling ochre dust before asking what he truly sought from this antiquity.
"Tell me about Causes," Noah said, his eyes glowing with the fiendish light of THE Protagonist's Omniscient Regard as he looked up into the uncovered gray eyes.
"I know First Causes, and the Prime Causes seated under them. I know Miniature Causes. Now I am hearing of Calcified Causes and Blighted ones. Enlighten me."

The veil twitched again as Damodred nodded, waving one massive, scarred hand as the dark sky and ruined basalt domain thinned away into a clean gray space of absolute nothingness- a realm constructed purely for showing rather than remembering!
"You already know more than most," Damodred spoke, his voice carrying the deep, melancholic resonance of an ancient being.
"So let me begin where the question truly begins."
As the giant opened his great hand, a single point of pristine light ignited in the empty gray space, hovering between them like a living star!

"Before a Dimension or Observable Existence can hold so much as one beam of light, before space can even trouble itself to stretch across the void, there must first be a reason that space is permitted to exist at all. A reason. That reason is what we name a Cause."
The point of light held firm, small and certain amidst the gray expanse!

"In the low realms this is easy to miss, for down there crude matter and crude energy are enough to hold a realm together on their own, allowing a lifeform to spend a whole existence believing power is only a matter of how much Primordial Source or energy it has managed to gather. But climb. Climb high enough into higher dimensionality, and you find that physical law is far too thin to bear the weight it is asked to carry."
As Damodred spoke, the point of light swelled into a small, turning realm, and Noah watched as a hairline crack ran through its fragile physics.

"An Observable Existence carries a staggering conceptual weight, not merely of mass but of meaning, so immense it ought to fall to nameless foam the instant it forms. It does not fall apart only because a Cause holds it. A Cause is the origin point, the true beginning underneath the beginning, the anchor that grants all that weight its permission to stand"
The hairline crack sealed instantly, and the small realm steadied and shone with declared grandeur.

"As lifeforms rise, they learn this truth in stages. First they think power is only pulling on Mana, on Infinity, or on THE Primordial Source. Then, higher, they learn to weave a Cause into their Pulses, their Infinity, their Source, and their Intent, swinging it like an absolute blade to force reality into compliance."
The gray eyes held steady on Noah, reflecting ages of witnessed war.
"And then there are the existences who go past merely using a Cause. Beings whose bones and blood and organs are forged out of these anchors themselves."
Noah thought of the colossal white dragon whose back he rode across dimensional gaps.
"Steeds," Noah said.

"Steeds," Damodred agreed, and the word carried the heavy weight of an ancient ossuary. "I know this because Master's curing of one is the very reason THE Tide That Owes Nothing pulled me across existence to your side. A living Observable Existence, seated out of pure Causes at the root of its lineage, shaped from the first moment to bear a burden that would turn any ordinary entity to vapor. You ride the proof of it even now. And now..."
The titan raised a second finger as three more points of light ignited beside the shining realm, hovering in the gray space like patient beacons.
"To understand how existence truly moves, you must know that a Cause is not one fixed thing. It can take four states or more."
The first point brightened into a clean, cold, unwavering illumination!

"First Causes. The pristine anchors, seated at the very beginning of a lineage or a framework, carrying the pure and uncorrupted intent of the ones who first carved existence into being. A First Cause does not easily degrade. Its authority is immutable, the original blueprint, untouched by time, holding forever the full weight of the moment it was carved."
The second point began to pulse with a warm, living rhythm, its light shifting from moment to moment like a burning heart!

"Prime Causes. The living anchors seated beneath the First. Where a First Cause is a legacy handed down from ancestors, a Prime Cause is a present will, active and evolving, able to steer its own progression. If the First Cause is the legacy, the Prime Cause is the wielder alive now, still deciding what it will become."
Noah nodded slowly, understanding his own nine Cause weavings with Hvitrmarr with greater clarity!
Then the third point of light changed, and Noah's attention sharpened as the illumination did not brighten, but sickened into an ochre hue!
A dark, corruptive thread wound through its center, and where the thread passed, the light frayed and wept like an open wound.

"Blighted Causes. A Blighted Cause is not some clean anchor that was later dirtied. It is born to its nature, a kind of Cause the same as any other, save that its nature is rot. It does not stop working. It goes on holding weight, and all the while it leaks rot and agony into the existence built atop it, consuming that existence slowly from the anchor outward while never once failing at its task."

Damodred turned his great hand, and an image formed in the gray, depicting a colossal Laestrygonian titan whose chest glowed with a diseased, burning color as fine dark lines spidered along its calcified frame.

"An example! One of my own bore a Cause we named THE Ember That Eats the Hearth. It anchored him faithfully, and all the while it burned him from the middle out, a low constant fire that never caught and never went out, and he held an entire Dimension upright on that agony for a full age." The gray eyes were unblinking.
"The blight is not weakness. It is a strength that charges you everything, forever."

The sick picture faded as the fourth point took its place, having gone entirely the other direction! It stopped moving completely, hanging hard, pale, and utterly still, and looking upon it, Noah felt the cold density of ancient, petrified bone!
"Calcified Causes..."

"Their nature is stillness, and out of that stillness comes a density I would struggle to describe. It becomes an absolute wall. Force arrives and finds nothing to push, for there is nothing left in it that can move to be pushed."

He conjured a barrier of pale calcified stone, and against it, the memory of a Primeval Lifeform striking down played out, the strike stopping instantly, the way a roaring wave stops against an ancient cliff that does not even know it is being struck!
"A Calcified Cause cannot adapt. It cannot evolve. It cannot yield, which sounds like a virtue until you remember that a thing which cannot yield can also never grow."
The gray eyes returned to Noah, and something in the titan's old voice turned at last toward the truth it had been circling all along.

"And I am made of these. Many of them. By every law you know, Master, I have no business standing here speaking with you at all, for a being built of Calcified Causes is a being that cannot progress. I ought to be static. Immense, unkillable at my own tier, and frozen...a mountain that will never be anything but the same mountain until existence itself forgets it."
Damodred opened both his great hands, and the two dark images returned side by side...the weeping blighted light and the pale frozen stone.
"My Calcified Causes are stone. But my Blighted Causes are fire, that low agonizing fire that never once goes out. And a stone set against a fire that will not stop does not stay merely a stone!"

The two lights began to turn against one another in a violent, grinding orbit, and where the weeping fire touched the frozen stone, the stone shifted, forced to move by the unyielding pain pressed against its structure!

"The blight spurs the calcification. The agony catalyzes the stone. We could not grow the way the living grow, through nourishment and will, so we grew the only way left to the damned...through pain and endurance, one forcing the other ever forward. The Laestrygonians persevered into grandeur upon nothing but the refusal of two wounds to let each other rest."
Damodred let the images fade, the gray space holding silent.
"That is what I am, Master. A dead pattern that taught its own scars to keep climbing. It is not a gift. But it is mine. And now, in a way, it is yours."
And as the weight of the titan's ancient truth settled over the empty domain, Noah looked upon all of it with shining eyes!

THE Sleepless Fiend of Those Who Remain...!

He had already made an enemy of one branch of Those Who Remain simply by existing well!

The question was never whether adding another branch was dangerous, but what it actually cost when stacked atop an active war he was already fighting, and as he weighed the outcome in the quiet depths of his mind, the added weight was smaller than it looked.
His existence answered before his mouth ever opened, his Intent leaning forward without hesitation as he looked down at the enormous scarred titan.
"In existence," Noah said, "anything is possible.

HUUM!

Now I am hearing of Calcified Causes and Blighted ones.

That reason is what we name a Cause."
The point of light held firm, small and certain amidst the gray expanse!

chapters.title: Chapter 5547: Collision!
paragraphs: Damodred regarded him from behind the veil of ancient, severed hands.
"If an old dead thing may offer the Master a recommendation."
The great head inclined slowly, sending a subtle shudder through the empty gray domain.

"You have been trying to do something, and it has not been working. You hold two sets of Causes right now, do you not? Nine of your own, seated in your Infinite Cause. And nine more, the First Causes of THE Steed you cured, which now stand behind you."
The gray eyes held Noah with unblinking, ancient focus.

"You have been trying to mix them. To fuse the two sets into one. And they will not fuse, Master, no matter how you press them, because they cannot. They are not the same kind, and no amount of will makes a stone into a fire."
Noah said nothing, for the titan was right. He had felt that exact conceptual resistance within his own existence.
"But..." Damodred spoke, opening one massive, scarred palm as the atmospheric density of the gray space deepened.

"My own Causes could never fuse either. Yet I taught them to collide instead, to strike against one another forever, and out of that endless collision came all our grandeur. You could do the same. Not fuse your nine Prime Causes and THE Steed's nine First Causes. Collide them. Set them crashing into each other without end, so that the push and pull of the impact pours their benefit straight into your existence, elevating you endlessly and feeding you adversity from the inside for as long as you live."
The old voice carried a terrible, unyielding calm that resonated through the strata of the void!

"Give yourself an eternal wound that heals into strength. You could climb higher than THE Laestrygonians ever did. You have living Causes where mine were only wounds and stone. You... could become grander than we were at our height."
Noah's lemniscate-ringed eyes sharpened, his gaze locking onto the titan with sudden, predatory intensity!
"How?"
"To collide your own Causes, you must command them. And Causes do not answer just any voice. They answer only the voice of the existence they belong to, spoken in that existence's own tongue."
He waved a colossal hand, and in the empty gray space, a shape of pure, resonant sound seemed to hang, vibrating with the ancient authority of an uncarved script!

"There are many kinds of Tongue across existence. But a True Tongue is a particular thing, Master, and a simple one once you see it plainly. A True Tongue is nothing more than your own personal language of your own existence. It is you, saying yourself. Those who have raised their Pantheons and begun to lay down their weavings of time speak it most easily, because by then their existence has already learned to repeat itself, and a True Tongue is only your existence repeating itself out loud, on purpose."
The gray eyes did not blink as the giant continued, delivering the mechanics of an extinct epoch without hesitation!
"Speak your own tongue. Fill the words with the intent to steer your Causes toward collision. That is all the command is."
Damodred paused, his voice hardening without softening the truth.

"And it will hurt. At first it will feel as though your existence is detonating inside you, because in a way it is. But acclimate to it, endure the first shock and do not flinch away, and when it settles you will hold many Causes that empower you every moment you draw breath. This is the very art that got my people extinguished. It made us too grand to be permitted."
He raised a single, scarred finger, teacherly once more.
"And...simply striking the Causes against each other is not enough. A blow is not a reaction. For a true reaction to happen, three conditions must be met, all of them, together."
He counted them off, and as his fingers moved, the gray space displayed three points of light knocking against one another in a slow, precise demonstration!

"First, collision frequency. The Causes must actually crash into one another, again and again, not drift past. Second, sufficient energy. Each collision must carry enough force to break the old bonds and forge new ones, or the Causes simply touch and part unchanged. Third, correct orientation. The Causes must align perfectly in dimensional space, so that the reactive parts of each one truly meet, and not merely their edges."

As Noah watched, the demonstration in the gray space came together, two points striking at the exact speed, at the exact angle, and with sufficient force, generating a sudden, glorious bloom of new light that expanded through the gray!
"Frequency. Energy. Orientation."
Damodred let the three conditions sit in the air between them, his voice echoing softly.
"Why does the Master not give it a try?"
Noah did not hesitate, his mind already three steps ahead as the realization settled into his core, for the answer had been sitting in his own mouth the entire time!

His True Tongue! The personal language of his own existence, the language that was only Noah Osmont saying Noah Osmont out loud! What was it, truly, but THE Osmontian Tongue?! Five Letters and one Word! He had spent this entire journey learning to speak himself into reality!
Was this also the gibberish he heard from Ryaenara when he first met her? It was simply her speaking with her own tongue?
Noah closed his eyes and he began!
He uttered the Letters low and grand, a rising mantra of absolute sovereignty echoing through the empty domain!
"I AM OSMONT. I AM QUINTESSENTIAL. I AM HUMAN. I AM THE PROTAGONIST!"
HUUM!
And following them, the Word sang out from his soul!
"I AM THE MORTAL COIL. I AM! I AM! I AM!"
WAA!

He did not speak them as mere names this time. He spoke them as a supreme command, pouring his full Ananke Intent into every syllable, the intent to take the eighteen Causes inside him and drive them into one another like particles hurled together in an existential accelerator, bending frequency, energy, and orientation to his unyielding will...!
BOOM!
His existence detonated!

chapters.title: Chapter 5548: Lapse! I
paragraphs: The first attempt threw his focus backward! It was exactly as Damodred had promised and worse, a nuclear tempest of pure conceptual force going off inside his own being as his Causes slammed together too hard, at broken angles, the raw energy of the collisions finding nowhere clean to discharge as his whole existence shuddered under the strain as though it might tear apart!
He gritted his teeth, refusing to flinch, his eyes blazing with cerulean-crimson light as he spoke the mantra again!
"I AM OSMONT. I AM QUINTESSENTIAL. I AM HUMAN. I AM THE PROTAGONIST!"
HUUM!

The second attempt was better! The third better still! And somewhere in the reciting, as his Ananke Intent discovered how to align the reactive faces of one Cause directly into another, the chaotic detonations stabilized!
It became a rhythm.
A glorious, magisterial rhythm!

Eighteen Causes, nine of his own Prime Causes and nine First Causes of THE Steed, began to collide inside his existence under the three absolute conditions the titan had named! They crashed together at the right speed, at the right angle, and often enough to matter, over and over, and wherever they struck, they bloomed into glorious, cascading light.

Multicolored waves poured off the impacts, and multicolored strings sang out across his inner world, every wave and every string carrying a tremendous, ancient density that washed over the whole of his existence as the weight of ages pressed into him from within.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!

It was like endless cosmic drums beginning to beat within his soul, a rhythm of perpetual collision without pause, and from every crash of Cause on Cause, the waves and strings spilled outward as though whole singularities were being born inside him with each passing nanosecond!
|You have grasped an ancient art unique to THE Laestrygonians. Analysis follows.|

|THE COLLISION OF CAUSES has begun. Rather than fusing your nine Prime Causes and the nine First Causes of THE Steed, you are now driving all eighteen into perpetual, structured collision, governed by frequency, energy, and orientation, commanded through THE Osmontian Tongue as your True Tongue.|

|Effect: with every passing second, you grow stronger. Not in one facet, but collectively, across the whole of your existence at once. Every collision feeds its benefit directly into you. All facets rise together, endlessly, for as long as the collision is sustained.|
|Secondary effect: the Osmontian Biomass cost of all future elevation is being reduced, and continues to fall the longer the art runs.|

|Warning retained for the record: this art carries perpetual internal adversity by design. It is the art for which THE Laestrygonians were driven to extinction. It empowers without limit and it costs without end.|

Noah read every word in the prompts, a slow shake of his head accompanying the wonder moving through him even as the internal drums beat on and the ancient, multicolored waves kept washing through his existence!
He looked up at Damodred, his eyes gleaming with quiet, imperial dominance.
"Just where are you sitting, currently?" Noah asked, his voice ringing with declared power. "Show me your power."
HUUM!
Noah activated THE Protagonist's Omniscient Regard!
Damodred bowed, the veil of severed hands dipping low toward the gray floor.
"Gladly, Master. Though I would have you understand, I hold but a fraction of what I wielded at my peak. Still. It is not nothing."
The Regard settled over the titan, and the Character Sheet bloomed in Noah's vision like a monument of calcified history!
|CHARACTER SHEET|
|Designation: Damodred. Last of THE Laestrygonians. The First to Return.|
|Standing: a fraction of his living peak, and still immense.|
|Facets of Existence: SS-Rank, Oir. Across the board. Finished craft, exact making, seated in a being that should by every law be frozen.|
|Intent: SS-Rank. THE Autarkis Intent. The third order, sovereignty above inevitability.|

|Pantheon: THE Sepulcher of the Unyielding Dead, SS-Rank. A Pantheon that is not a realm one enters but a graveyard that enters you, seating an opponent inside the accumulated stillness and agony of an extinct people.|
|Core: 36 Causes, Blighted and Calcified both, held in perpetual collision every moment of his existence. The very art he has just taught you, run without pause across ages.|
|Disposition: absolutely loyal to the Master. Grieving, patient, and certain. He does not hurry, because he has already waited longer than most things have existed.|

|Notable thread: he waits, quietly, for the Master to call forth MORE of his kind from extinction. He is the first to return. He does not believe he will be the last. He is content to serve, and to wait, and to see how many Laestrygonians the Master's Tide might yet pull back into the light.|
It was something utterly surreal to see, and it made Noah take a moment to truly evaluate the wonder that landed on his lap!
But as Causes collided more and more in his existence...new prompts bloomed in Noah's vision, and these were different, for they were not describing what was, but what was beginning to be!

|Notice. A unique capability is forming at the meeting point of three things: THE Ananke Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian, your Osmontian Source Infinity, and THE Collision of Causes now running perpetually within you.|

|The eighteen Causes crashing inside your existence do not only elevate you. They produce. Every collision births raw power, waves and strings and newborn singularities, and until now that power has poured inward, feeding your ascent. It need not only pour inward.|

|By uttering THE Osmontian Tongue as a mantra, and steering the intent not toward elevation but toward release, you may take the immense power thrown off by each collision and unleash it OUTWARD, as an attack. The particular Causes you drive together determine the shape of what emerges. No two collisions yield the same weapon.|
|This capability is now yours to wield. Designation: THE Cataclysm of Colliding Causes.|
Noah read it, and a slow, imperial smile touched his mouth.
An engine that made him grander with every breath, and now a weapon fired from the same furnace.
He raised one hand toward the empty gray expanse of Damodred's showing-place, and he spoke the mantra again, low and grand, but this time he bent the intent outward, toward release!
"I AM OSMONT. I AM QUINTESSENTIAL. I AM HUMAN. I AM THE PROTAGONIST!"
HUUM!
And inside him, he chose.

He reached into the churning eighteen and seized two, driving them together on purpose, aiming their reactive faces into one another with the frequency and the energy and the orientation the titan had named.
His Prime Cause of Tyranny, and one of Hvitrmarr's First Causes, the ancient anchor of Valor.
They collided!
BOOM!

And from Noah's open palm erupted a lance of layered cerulean and gold, a spear of pure dominance shot through with a Steed's unbreakable courage, and it tore across the gray space and struck the far nothing with a weight that made the whole domain shudder, a strike that did not merely destroy but commanded the space it hit to break, valor lending the tyranny a fearlessness that would not be refused!
Noah's eyes gleamed!

He gritted his teeth, refusing to flinch, his eyes blazing with cerulean-crimson light as he spoke the mantra again!
"I AM OSMONT.
I AM QUINTESSENTIAL.
I AM HUMAN.
I AM THE PROTAGONIST!"
HUUM!
The second attempt was better!
The third better still!
And somewhere in the reciting, as his Ananke Intent discovered how to align the reactive faces of one Cause directly into another, the chaotic detonations stabilized!
It became a rhythm.
A glorious, magisterial rhythm!
Eighteen Causes, nine of his own Prime Causes and nine First Causes of THE Steed, began to collide inside his existence under the three absolute conditions the titan had named!
They crashed together at the right speed, at the right angle, and often enough to matter, over and over, and wherever they struck, they bloomed into glorious, cascading light.

Multicolored waves poured off the impacts, and multicolored strings sang out across his inner world, every wave and every string carrying a tremendous, ancient density that washed over the whole of his existence as the weight of ages pressed into him from within.
BOOM!
BOOM!
BOOM!

It was like endless cosmic drums beginning to beat within his soul, a rhythm of perpetual collision without pause, and from every crash of Cause on Cause, the waves and strings spilled outward as though whole singularities were being born inside him with each passing nanosecond!
|You have grasped an ancient art unique to THE Laestrygonians.
Analysis follows.|
|THE COLLISION OF CAUSES has begun.

Rather than fusing your nine Prime Causes and the nine First Causes of THE Steed, you are now driving all eighteen into perpetual, structured collision, governed by frequency, energy, and orientation, commanded through THE Osmontian Tongue as your True Tongue.|

Not in one facet, but collectively, across the whole of your existence at once.
Every collision feeds its benefit directly into you.
All facets rise together, endlessly, for as long as the collision is sustained.|

|Warning retained for the record: this art carries perpetual internal adversity by design.
It is the art for which THE Laestrygonians were driven to extinction.
It empowers without limit and it costs without end.|

HUUM!
Noah activated THE Protagonist's Omniscient Regard!
Damodred bowed, the veil of severed hands dipping low toward the gray floor.

Though I would have you understand, I hold but a fraction of what I wielded at my peak.
Still.
It is not nothing."

The third order, sovereignty above inevitability.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5549: Lapse! II
paragraphs: <On Those Who Remain>
We are accustomed to viewing existence as a reality where living beings enter from different doorways, distinct and separate from the stage beneath their feet.
Yet this... is the primary illusion. An ocean does not construct waves the way a mason builds a wall; the ocean simply waves, and in doing so, it expresses its own nature.
So it was with Those Who Remain. They were not merely builders standing outside the halls of reality, but the very impulse that caused the dark to tremble and take shape.
Among Those Who Remain, only a few distinct identities survived the erosion of ages to be remembered by name. Among these few, THE Sleepless Fiend was noted as a particularly eccentric existence.

Where others of its kind sought static absolute authority or spoke final decrees, THE Sleepless Fiend was consumed by a curious, playful fascination with the nature of Causes. Rumors across ancient epochs whisper that it treated Causes as living experiments, grafting First Causes into living marrow and weaving foundational anchors into organic forms merely to see what burdens those existences could bear.
It is a narrow view to believe that only those explicitly known as Descendants carry the legacy of Those Who Remain.

Look closely at the staggering spectrum of lifeforms moving across Dimensions and Time. They are not mere accidents of ambient density. In truth, many are the lingering, self-sustaining ripples of those ancient trials: existences whose bodies, instincts, and very identities were carved out of manipulated Causes eons ago, still acting out a play designed by a weaver who refused to sleep.
Among the Descendants of Those Who Remain, many carry names that make epochs tremble, but a rare few sit upon heights so grand that their legends threaten to eclipse the progenitors themselves.

THE Infinity Eater was such an existence. It spun thin, imperceptible threads of itself outward across the weavings of space and time. Across untold multitudes, lifeforms tapped into these delicate threads of Infinity, foolishly mistaking the borrowed tide for their own awakened power.
They knew nothing of the weaver. Through every thread of Infinity woven across the dark, THE Infinity Eater felt every breath, every intent, and every pulse of energy.

Whatever it lent, it could reclaim at a whim. It could wear another's existence like a fitted garment or drown their soul from the inside without casting a single spell. In truth, any Infinity-wielder who lacked a root or a Source of their own was never a master of power; they were merely a mouth that THE Infinity Eater had not yet decided to close.

There is the record of the Fall of the Pale Dimension, where a colossal alliance of Primeval Ones and True Lifeforms gathered to erase THE Infinity Eater from existence. Thousands of sovereign entities unfurled their immensity, their weapons shining with endless, infinite energy as they encircled him.
THE Infinity Eater stood alone upon a ruined escarpment of petrified earth, silent and unmoving. He did not summon an army. He did not draw a blade. He merely reached out and plucked the threads.

In that singular, terrifying instant, more than half of the opposing army gasped as their own Infinity revolted. Their Trueness caved inward, their Intent shattered in their throats, and their bodies moved against their will as the borrowed force reclaimed its master.

With hollow, silent eyes, more than half of those ancient lords lost control of their existences, turned around, and came to stand beside THE Infinity Eater, drawing their weapons against their former allies.
Let this be the standing lesson for those who seek the heights. Power is never ownerless, and force without a true, personal origin is merely a collar worn by the blind.

Be relentlessly careful to understand the exact root from which your strength springs, and trace the stream back to its source before you drink too deeply. Otherwise, you may lose your existence before you even know it has been claimed.
<THE True Human Emperor>
After getting a feel of his existence and its ongoing processes in that space, Noah nodded to the massive visage of Damodred.
"Let's go back."
The Laestrygonian severed hands blindfold twitched as gray brilliance spilled.
The gray space folded away, and the ruined domain of the showing rushed back into color and weight, and Noah opened his eyes in the light of THE Ymnaros.
And he looked around and understood at once that Damodred had not done what he had assumed.

The titan had not stretched a single moment into infinity the way Noah stretched instants to think inside them. Time had passed out here, the whole long teaching unspooling at its true length while existence went on around them.
The dead were buried.

Theron Adranos and Anaximander had finished the work, the small white and blue bodies laid into the scorched ground beneath rows of low mounds, and Ryaenara stood among them. All of them were simply waiting for him now.
And Anaximander wore a conflicted expression!
The scholar looked as though he wanted to ask something and could not make himself do it, the mild curious face caught on a hesitation!
Noah smiled, and looked at the mounds a moment, and then at his friend.
"There shouldn't be hesitation between friends," he said. "What's up?"
Anaximander sighed and opened his mouth.
And Theron Adranos put a hand on the scholar's shoulder, and stepped forward instead.
"I put Sir Anaximander in a difficult position," the golden-haired man said, "by asking a heavy request of him."
He drew a breath, and told him.

"THE Ymnaros is facing an invasion we have not faced before these past days. Our Dimension is colliding....fusing, slowly, into another Dimension entirely, one filled with Infinite Lifeforms, the same kind you cut down in this garden." His jaw tightened.

"Our defenses were built for enemies who come through the doors. They do not work against this, because the two Dimensions are becoming one, and where they overlap, the enemy can appear anywhere at all. Inside our strongholds. Beneath our feet. In a garden that should have been a hundred layers deep in safety." He gestured faintly at the ruin around them. "The way they appeared here."
"We call it the Dimensionlapse," Theron said. "And from what I saw here today...that capability of yours. The one that strips the power from all those nearby..."
He looked down at his own hands then, and turned them over.
"When you imposed it, I did not feel any different. I felt like me. Whole. Myself. The same strength I have always carried, untouched, while others fell out of the sky around me."
Noah's attention sharpened!

"Our toughest battles are occurring or already coming," Theron went on. "Against the mightiest of the invaders, in the places the Dimensionlapse has fused most deeply. If your power leaves the Superpowered Lifeforms standing at the height of their strength while it strips our enemies bare, then it may be the very thing that lets us overcome an invasion that has been grinding us down."
His voice steadied into something formal.
"I do not ask it for free. Existence is give and take. Nothing in it is free."
He half-turned, and looked at the obelisk behind him, the tall stone still pouring its steady blue-gold light up into the smoke, the shrine his people had died in rows to keep.

"This is one of many," Theron said quietly. "Doorways, all of them. They open onto the place the invaders have bled us for, generation after generation. What grows there is the thing every Infinite and Source Lifeform in reach has spent ages trying to take from us." He looked back at Noah.

"A Panacea. It grew in our lands on its own, and it is what made us the Superpowered Lifeforms that we are. And to others, they say, it can do something stranger still. They say it can cause the emergence of a Purpose. The emergence and nurturing of a Cause."
BOOM!

"I can bring you through," Theron finished. "You are the allies of Sir Anaximander, so that you may confirm all of it with your own eyes rather than take a desperate man's word. And if Existence deems it fitting, then afterward, we could work together."
Noah's eyes shone.
He looked at the obelisk that so many had died to protect! He thought of Dimensions fusing and colliding into one another. Dimensionlapse!

That did not sound natural to him at all, not remotely. The Infinite True Lifeforms had besieged this place for ages and failed to break it. Had they stopped trying to break it, then, and started trying to merge it instead, to fold THE Ymnaros into a Dimension of their own so that no wall or door could keep them out any longer?
And laid over all of it, the last thing Theron had said, the thing that mattered most of all.
A Panacea that could cause the emergence and nurturing of a Cause!
He looked at Theron, and then at Anaximander, and his decision was already made.
"It is only human to help each other. Let's go in and see."
Yes. It was human to help!

But it was also human to make gains while helping, and Noah had never once in his life been able to deny himself an unfathomable treasure when one was laid in front of him! A Dimension besieged for ages by Infinite and Source Lifeforms both. A Panacea everyone in reach wanted badly enough to grind a whole people down for it!
And a thought rose in him, quiet and enormous, as he looked at the doorway.

What if this was the place? What if THE Ymnaros became the first ground he claimed, the first stake driven for the rule of THE True Human Emperor, a unique Dimension full of the more human beings he had come to meet, defended by people his power left standing while it stripped their enemies bare?
Maybe.
Maybe!

chapters.title: Chapter 5550: Find Her!
paragraphs: <Outside THE Krazhor-Nul>
In the dark beyond the ancient Dimension, where the naked strings of existence ran undressed of matter and law, a gathering stood upon nothing at all.
Jarl Erling was among them, and he was not the largest!

The titanic bronze Descendant with the bone-braided beard and the crimson fissures running molten through his body stood shoulder to shoulder with others of his kind, and there were several, and every one of them wore the same sentence written into their blood. Cursed Descendants of Those Who Remain.
Lords of continental thrones and lone floating mountains, keepers of harnessed Steeds and generations of failed experiments, each of them dying on a schedule no one had ever managed to argue with.
Every single one of them had shining eyes.

They looked out across the darkness together, and the light in those eyes was not the light of power, for they all had power beyond measuring. It was worse than that. It was the light of men who had spent their entire lives counting down and had just been handed a reason to stop counting.
Those who had learned of a cure!
"All I have," Jarl Erling said, "are the brief signatures of existence."
His voice rolled out across the dark, and none of the others interrupted him, because he was the one who had seen it happen and they were the ones who had come running.

"Brief. A handful of moments. The one with Living Causes, the one who can cure the curse, took what was mine out of my Dimension before I could close my hand on it." The molten fissures across his chest pulsed with the effort of saying it.
"But existence remembers what passes through it. And I have the signatures."
He turned his enormous head, and looked at one of them in particular.
"So I will rely on the prowess of Jarl Ingrid," he said, "and the rest of you, to track them down."
And in the air before the gathered Jarls, the images hung.

Noah Osmont, crowned and rendered out of a stolen signature of existence and turning slowly in the dark. And beside him, vast and luminous and impossible, THE Infiniverse. A living Observable Existence with vibrant Causes moving through her, the answer that every Descendant experiment across every age had been reaching for and failing to grasp!
Shining eyes fixed on both images and did not look away.
<Between Dimensions>
Far from that gathering, in another stretch of the frothing black entirely, one rider crossed the deep.
Jarl Skallagrim rode atop a single Cursed Steed.

It should not have been possible. To bring a Cursed Steed out of THE Krazhor-Nul was a thing the Dimension itself resisted, for the Steeds were seated into that place by the sentence that made them, bred to bear burdens within its bounds and bound to it by the same standing curse that was slowly killing them. They did not leave. They had never left!
That was the architecture of the promise, that those who left were abandoned by Salvation!
Skallagrim had paid the cost anyway.

He had come out with seven. Seven remained after he had torn the eighth apart with his own hands in a poisoned garden, seven dying colossi whipped forward into the dark by a keeper whose calm was worse than any rage.
One had made it through.

The rest had not survived the crossing. Their terminal Causes had guttered out somewhere in the dark between, one after another, the curse in them finally collecting what it was owed the moment they stepped past the boundary that had held them for ages, and Skallagrim had ridden on through the dying without once looking back at any of them.
Six Steeds spent as fare! The rot at his fissures had spread for it, and the two years he did not have were fewer now than they had been.
He did not care. One was all he needed!

The Steed shuddered.

"The sister you had beside you for thousands of years. The one chained in the same harness, dying on the same schedule, bearing the same sentence." His voice stayed level, conversational, the terrible lucidity of it carrying across the frothing dark.
"The sister who abandoned you the moment that she was cured. Who broke her chains and looked at me with those uncursed eyes and went, and did not take you with her. Not you. Not one of you."
The dying Steed made a sound that had no dignity in it.
"Hold to that," Skallagrim said. "Whatever is left in you that can still want something, point it at her."

He straightened on its back, and looked out into the endless dark ahead, at the drifting membranes of Dimensions hanging in the black like islands in an ocean, every one of them a place she might have gone.
"Follow her scent, and we shall have our own cure." The rot glowed dull red along his fissures. "Across Dimensions and time. Find them."
"Find Hvitrmarr!"

The ninth district of the Cultivation Farms had taken longer than the eight before it.

They had learned. That was the thing about beings who had spent ages perfecting an art of harvest, they were not stupid, they were only comfortable, and comfort was a thing that could be burned off a lifeform quickly enough if you burned hard enough!

By the seventh district the masters had stopped lounging. By the ninth they had stopped meeting him in the open altogether, and instead they had rigged the whole domain he crossed, sinking their weavings into the pyramids themselves so that when THE Creature came down through the butcher-red sky, the ground rose to fight him alongside its owners.
It had worked, for a while.

Eleven of them. Source True Lifeforms, three of them Cenozoic, and they had fought together properly for the first time since he entered this Dimension, drawing on their Gu, spending their stored burdens like coin, feeding ages of stolen bearing into weavings meant to break a single trespasser apart at the anchors.
Now they were dead, and THE Creature stood in the crater of what had been their stratum, and he was heaving!

In the dark beyond the ancient Dimension, where the naked strings of existence ran undressed of matter and law, a gathering stood upon nothing at all.
Jarl Erling was among them, and he was not the largest!

The titanic bronze Descendant with the bone-braided beard and the crimson fissures running molten through his body stood shoulder to shoulder with others of his kind, and there were several, and every one of them wore the same sentence written into their blood.
Cursed Descendants of Those Who Remain.
Lords of continental thrones and lone floating mountains, keepers of harnessed Steeds and generations of failed experiments, each of them dying on a schedule no one had ever managed to argue with.
Every single one of them had shining eyes.
They looked out across the darkness together, and the light in those eyes was not the light of power, for they all had power beyond measuring.
It was worse than that.
It was the light of men who had spent their entire lives counting down and had just been handed a reason to stop counting.
Those who had learned of a cure!
"All I have," Jarl Erling said, "are the brief signatures of existence."
His voice rolled out across the dark, and none of the others interrupted him, because he was the one who had seen it happen and they were the ones who had come running.
"Brief.
A handful of moments.

The one with Living Causes, the one who can cure the curse, took what was mine out of my Dimension before I could close my hand on it." The molten fissures across his chest pulsed with the effort of saying it.
"But existence remembers what passes through it.
And I have the signatures."
He turned his enormous head, and looked at one of them in particular.
"So I will rely on the prowess of Jarl Ingrid," he said, "and the rest of you, to track them down."
And in the air before the gathered Jarls, the images hung.
Noah Osmont, crowned and rendered out of a stolen signature of existence and turning slowly in the dark.
And beside him, vast and luminous and impossible, THE Infiniverse.
A living Observable Existence with vibrant Causes moving through her, the answer that every Descendant experiment across every age had been reaching for and failing to grasp!
Shining eyes fixed on both images and did not look away.

They had never left!
That was the architecture of the promise, that those who left were abandoned by Salvation!
Skallagrim had paid the cost anyway.
He had come out with seven.

One had made it through.
The rest had not survived the crossing.

chapters.title: Chapter 5551: A Challenge!
paragraphs: His obsidian flames guttered low and ragged around a frame that had taken real damage. The Blank Caudal dragged behind him through the ochre dust, white hair matted dark, and along his left side ran a wound that had gone all the way to something structural, a splitting seam where one of the Cenozoic ones had gotten an Intent  into him before dying badly for the privilege.

Calcified stones lay in ridges across the whole broken domain. The air was thick with the released corpses of nine ruptured Gu, ages of stolen bearing hanging in the red light with nowhere left to go, and beneath his feet the strata ran down through crushed pyramid stone and petrified bone into layers of older ruin still!
He breathed!
And behind his ribs, and behind him, and somehow also very far away, the statue spoke.
|Two hundred and six.|
The ancient voice arrived from the direction time came from, calm and vast as it always was, and THE Creature said nothing, because two hundred and six was not a thousand.
Then the statue did something it had never done.
It smiled.

He felt it happen inside himself, the seated colossus of worn gray stone shifting its faceless face into an expression, and it was not the serene ancient nonchalance he had carried since the thing first came to him. It was brutal. It was the smile of something that had been watching a fight go on too long and had decided, quite suddenly, that it was bored.

|You are not learning. Two hundred and six. At this rate the trial completes, and you will have learned nothing from it that you did not already know when you began. You are merely doing what you are good at, thoroughly, for a long time.|
|Existence did not seat this trial in you to watch you excel at something you have already mastered.| The statue's voice deepened, and the whole ruined district seemed to lean in around it.
|A trial that only measures is a ledger. A trial that changes the one measured is a trial. So Existence will up the stakes.|
THE Creature straightened out of his heaving, obsidian flames pulling in tight around the split in his side.
"Explain."
|There is a reason the Farms of this Dimension are so rich.|

The gray of the statue's voice shifted, and images came with it now, pressed into him rather than shown: the pyramids, the chained lines, the Gu at every peak, and beneath all of it something else, something enormous and buried and slow.

|The masters did not discover this art. They inherited the conditions for it. Beneath the Fields, deep in the oldest strata of THE Ghor-Vazhal, a Primeval Lifeform is dying. It has been dying for ages. Its lifeline was cut by a Progeny of Those Who Remain, and what was cut did not sever cleanly, and so it has been bleeding out across an entire Dimension ever since.|

|The sacrifices feed it. The offerings feed it. Every life that climbs those steps and enters a Gu is rendered down, and the masters take their profit, and what they do not take drains downward through the strata into the thing beneath, which cannot live and cannot finish dying and so simply drinks, age after age. Trillions of lives. Not spent on greed alone. Spent on keeping a corpse from becoming a corpse.|
THE Creature went very still.

The whole architecture of the place reorganized itself in his understanding as the words landed. He had been razing districts. He had been tearing the roofs off a house without once asking what the house was built on. Every pyramid he broke, every Gu he ruptured, every master he put his heel through, and beneath all of it the actual engine had gone on drinking, patient and enormous and entirely untouched by anything he had done.

|Collapse it, and the Farms die with it. Not one district. All of them. The reason this Dimension eats will be gone, and what remains will only be beings who are used to eating, which is a far smaller problem and one that largely solves itself.|
"What...is the cost of this one?" THE Creature said.
The brutal smile came back into the ancient stone.
|One hour.|

|Find it, and collapse it, within one hour of this moment. It is buried in the deepest strata of a Dimension that has no measured end, and it is guarded, and you have already been bled today. That is the point. Existence is not interested in whether you can carry a weight. It knows you can carry. It wishes to see whether you can commit and persevere.|
"And what is offered?"
The statue was quiet for a moment, and when it answered, something in the ancient voice changed.
|What is offered is not power.|

The stone eyes burned in the far dark of him. |Succeed, and you receive the first portion of the inheritance of the previous bearer. What it is, I will not say, because I am not permitted to say, and because you would not understand it before you hold it.|
THE Creature's flames rose.
The previous bearer!
His eyes were immensely cold as he only nodded
"I accept," he said.
He did not take long about it!
And the statue smiled brutally a second time as if it had attained something, as if its words were not done, and it was now finishing!
|One hour. And if you fail, you will willfully give control of ten percent of yourself to Existence as a cost.|
A tenth of his Existence itself, the whole of what he was, handed over willingly to this thing!
THE Creature remained entirely unfettered.

His flames steadied. The wound in his side kept splitting and he let it. He looked out across the shattered ninth district, across the ridges of calcified stones and pyramids, out toward a butcher-red horizon that went on past any counting, and he understood exactly what he needed to do!
One hour.

To find a dying Primeval One buried in the deepest strata of an endlessly vast Dimension, a Dimension crawling with horrid True Lifeforms who by now all knew precisely what he was and what he had been doing to them for nine domains running, and to reach it, and to break the thing that an entire civilization of monsters had spent ages feeding.
He rolled his shoulders once. The Blank Caudal lifted out of the dust behind him, white and gold and patient.
"Then let us begin," THE Creature said.
And he shot downward into the deeper strata of this Dimension!
