chapters.title: Chapter 5552: Analysis! I
paragraphs: <THE Quintessential Pantheon of THE Infiniverse>
Deep inside Noah, inside the living Observable Existence he carried and who carried him, a sea of blue-gold Osmontian Source Infinity stretched out past any horizon inside a certain realm.
The whole ocean gave off a low sustained hum, the sound of a thing that had never once needed a source outside itself!
Above it hung floating islands.

Hundreds of them, drifting at their own patient heights. They mimicked the old Spiritual Lands- terraced peaks of pale stone laced with veins of gold, waterfalls of raw Infinity pouring off their undersides and falling forever into the sea below.
Mist of pure Source drifted in the gaps between.
It was beautiful! But Ruination and THE Infiniverse were not here for the beauty.
They had come here to work.
All around the two of them, filling the air above the sea and between the islands for as far as the drifting mist allowed, hung diagrams.
Manifestations of everything they had just learned about Causes.
THE Infiniverse stood upon the surface of her own sea, luminous and severe, hands clasped behind her back, and Ruination hovered near her.
"To ensure the Master never has to die again," Ruination said, "we have to anticipate everything in all possible futures."
The strings moved.
"He died once inside the Steed. He came back only because THE Hepatarch answered, and I will not build a strategy on the assumption that it always will."
"So we work backward from every ending we can imagine, and we close them. And right now, Causes seem to be the nexus behind a great many of those endings."
The first bubbles bloomed in the air above the sea, written in threads of pale light.
CAUSES.

"They are behind you," Ruination said. "Behind every Observable Existence that has ever held together. Behind Steeds, who are made of nothing else. Behind the Master's own ascent, and behind the eighteen colliding in his chest at this moment."
A second bubble bloomed, and a string ran out to join it.
"And behind all of that, one being keeps appearing."
THE SLEEPLESS FIEND.
"One of Those Who Remain experimented on Steeds to fill them with Causes. Then he cursed them. An entire lineage of living Observable Existences, sentenced to slow collapse."
More bubbles formed!
THOSE WHO REMAIN. DESCENDANTS. CURSED DESCENDANTS.
Strings snapped between them, drawing the shape of a lineage that believed existence belonged to it, and a second lineage beneath it dying on a schedule.
"The account we have is that his Progeny touched the Steeds, and so he cursed them and cut his losses. That...doesn't make much sense."
A string pulled taut between the Fiend and the Steeds, and hung there, vibrating.
"Were the Steeds actually already unstable? Was the curse not a punishment at all, but a containment? A sentence laid on an experiment that had gone somewhere he did not want it to go?"
She let that hang, and drew the last string.
LAESTRYGONIANS.
"Because this is the same being," Ruination said, "who moved to bring an entire race to extinction because of their Causes."
The diagram hung complete above the blue-gold sea, bubbles and strings and branching lines, and at the center of every path stood the same thing.

"So the question is..." Ruination said. "Why would something that powerful be so interested in Causes? What is it about them that a being who could unmake a lineage with a sentence would spend ages tinkering with, and then twice destroy whatever came out of the tinkering? Why ruin an entire race over their anchors?"
THE Infiniverse studied the diagram in silence.
Then she raised one hand, and pulled.

The bubble marked CAUSES came apart at her gesture, unfolding into its component structures, First and Prime and Blighted and Calcified and the unnamed others, and she reached past all of them into the strand that ran back into herself, into her own foundation, and drew that out beside the rest for comparison.
"There is something wrong with the Master's nine," she said.
Ruination's strings stilled.
THE Infiniverse set the two side by side in the air, and the difference was immediate even in the diagram.

"These are the nine Prime Causes that hold an ordinary Observable Existence together. Cognitio. Bellum. Mortis... The common nine, seated beneath a First Cause, doing the work they were made for." Her hand moved.
"And these are the Master's nine. Existence. Paradox. Chaos. Mana. Quintessence. Adversity. Tyranny. Harvest. Apocalypse."
The two sets hung together, and one of them was simply larger.

"They are not the same order of thing," THE Infiniverse said. "His are distinctly grander. They resuscitated a dead Observable Existence. They were seated into the Organs of a Steed and joined to her First Causes without collapsing. And now they are colliding against pristine First Causes, striking them, forcing reactions out of them, and holding their own in that collision."
She turned to Ruination.

"A Prime Cause cannot do that. A Prime Cause is the living relative beneath the ancestor. It does not stand as an equal to a First Cause and grind against it as a peer. If his nine can do that, then his nine have not been Prime Causes for some time. We have simply kept calling them what they were when he made them."
"They evolved past Prime," Ruination said.
"They are not the common nine, and they are not First Causes either. He carved them himself, out of his own identity..."
She closed her hand, and the label on the diagram changed.
"They should not be called his Prime Causes. They are his own unique Causes, bearing his identity. They are his... Osmontian Causes."
HUUM!
The sea churned.
The whole blue-gold ocean rose in a single slow enormous swell beneath their feet, the hum of it deepening, and on the drifting islands above, the crystalline groves rang all at once!
Ruination watched the swell pass.
"I will let the Master know," she said.
"Now, these Osmontian Causes. How do we use them to pull on the genetic markers of the Laestrygonians the way he pulled Damodred?"

The whole blue-gold ocean rose in a single slow enormous swell beneath their feet, the hum of it deepening, and on the drifting islands above, the crystalline groves rang all at once!
Ruination watched the swell pass.
"I will let the Master know," she said.
"Now, these Osmontian Causes.
How do we use them to pull on the genetic markers of the Laestrygonians the way he pulled Damodred?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5553: Analysis! II
paragraphs: The bubble for DAMODRED appeared, and a string ran from it back to CAUSES, and then to THE TIDE THAT OWES NOTHING.

"Because the mechanism as we understand it is narrow," Ruination said. "He cured a Cursed Lifeform bound to Those Who Remain through Cause replacement. That act altered cause and effect across existence and time. The Tide followed the altered weavings back to the only thing they still resembled, found an extinct people's markers sleeping in their own Causes, and matured an egg from it."

"Is that reproducible? Or was it a single accident? Does it only ever come as a Tide reward for curing a Steed, and are there even any more Steeds we can reach? Or, now that we know its origin, can we replicate it deliberately?"
THE Infiniverse thought about it!

"THE Tide That Owes Nothing does not follow a procedure. It follows him, and it returns what he gives interlinked with what he is. That is why it can reach things that are extinct. It is because the Tide does not consider extinction a category that applies to a gift, so long as there is enough logic and foundation beneath the pull to make the gift coherent."

She gestured at the Damodred bubble. "The Laestrygonians laid markers into their Causes deliberately, as a chance. The chance required rare Causes to clash and meld in the right way. The Master's cure of the Steed produced exactly that shape. The logic was already there. The Tide only had to notice it and lock on. That was the door being opened. Now that it is open, does it really need to be opened again?"
Ruination's strings paused mid-write.

"We know what we are looking for now," THE Infiniverse continued. "Before, the Tide had to discover a resemblance across an age of dead weavings on its own. Now the target is known, named, and precedented, and we have one of them standing beside the Master as proof of concept."
She drew two new strands out of the unfolded Causes diagram and set them apart from the rest.

"So. If we focus deliberately on Blighted Causes and Calcified Causes, study them, hold them in our understanding, perhaps even channel them at the moment THE Tide is triggered by some other act of giving, then that focus becomes a hook. Something for the Return to lock onto. The Tide chooses what to give. But a hook can influence what it reaches for...a specified Return"
Ruination absorbed that, and the diagram above the sea rearranged itself into something that looked, for the first time, less like a mystery and more like a plan!
THE Infiniverse had begun to work, and Ruination stood back and let her.
She raised one hand, and a Status Panel bloomed above the sea.
|STATUS PANEL: NOAH OSMONT|
|Designations: THE Quintessential Osmontian. THE True Human Emperor. THE Fledgling Liege of the First Lineage. Human.|
|Scale framework: First Infinite Scale of Existence complete; Second Infinite Scale approaching its next stage.|
|FACETS OF EXISTENCE: A-Rank, Idho. Osmontian Source Infinity. Volume. Output. Trueness. All Nine Foundations. Currently rising continuously under THE Collision of Causes.|
|INTENT: THE Ananke Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian. A-Rank, Idho. Second order.|
|OSMONTIAN TONGUE: five Letters, one Word. I AM. OSMONT. QUINTESSENTIAL. HUMAN. PROTAGONIST. THE MORTAL COIL.|

|CAUSES: nine, seated in THE Infinite Cause. Designation under review, previously logged as Prime Causes, now correctly THE OSMONTIAN CAUSES. Currently colliding in perpetuity against nine First Causes of THE Steed.|
|ARTS: THE Collision of Causes. THE Quintessential Confluence. THE DOMAIN OF THE MORTAL COIL.|

|APPENDAGES: THE Estuary Eye. THE Pinion Vigil. THE Hepatarch of the Undying Root. THE Amaranthine Heart. THE Primeval Osmontian Marrow. THE Circlet of the Quintessential Ruin. THE Quintessential Pantheon of THE Infiniverse.|
|OSMONTIAN BIOMASS: 89,800,000. Elevation costs falling continuously.|

|RETAINERS AND BONDED EXISTENCES: Hvitrmarr, Remnant Dimension Steed of the First lineage, THE Autarkis Intent. Damodred of THE Laestrygonians, SS-Rank across all facets. THE Infiniverse. Ruination...|
|HELD, UNUSED: THE Tessellated Heart of the Borrowed Flame. THE Lingering Word. One True Declarative Human Ruling.|
Ruination looked around her Master's quantified panel and found the first flaw in the second line she read.
A-Rank Idho. It was honest, accurate, and useless as a threat assessment, because it did not describe what happened when her Master arrived somewhere.

He rode a Steed who had come down on a Cenozoic True Lifeform and unmade it in one motion, its Ananke-grade Intent caving inward under THE Autarkis Intent like wet parchment under a falling mountain. So the practical answer was that he already overcame Cenozoic Scale beings whenever he pleased, because he did not have to do it himself.
Which was precisely why she did not trust the number.
Ashkavaal had also been Cenozoic, partially grasped temporal weavings, and her Master had killed her with a beginner's fireball at Rank F standing.
That established the floor of the Sixth Scale. Nothing else.
Ruination pondered about the quantification of power from here!
She set Jarl Skallagrim's weaving apart from the Scale diagram, where it hung refusing to sit beside a single rung of it.
These fuckers were hard to designate!

She redrew it. Where the Scale diagram had hung, the grade ladder rose in its place, F Beith through A Idho, then S Ebad, SS Oir, SSS Muin, and above that the unnamed rung waiting to be carved in THE Osmontian Tongue when he reached it.
The grades measured the thing itself rather than the rung it occupied. They could describe a Cursed Descendant, a Laestrygonian, and her Master. Vakochev's framework could describe none of the three.
Ruination enlarged Damodred and analyzed him at this time.
The strongest weapon under her Master's command was considerably stronger than her Master.
SS-Rank facets. SS-Rank Autarkis Intent. An SS-Rank Pantheon!
Her Master's own facets sat at A-Idho. Hvitrmarr, simply by being ridden, delivered S-Rank to any battle she entered. And Damodred, by being here, delivered SS!
So what was his standing? A, because that was his own hand? Or SS, because SS answered when he spoke?
She smiled lightly while thinking where exactly to put her Master.
That left the largest thread on the board.
She set Theron Adranos into the air, and his weaving read as almost nothing.
The Superpowered Lifeforms emanated no authority. Less presence upon existence than the scorched dirt he had knelt in.
He had stood inside THE DOMAIN OF THE MORTAL COIL and felt nothing.
Which should have been impossible, because the Word nullified all authority and made no exceptions.
She also had to quantify this!
The panel turned slowly above the sea.
Across the water, THE Infiniverse worked on in her silence, taking Blighted Causes apart and putting them back together, building a hook to throw into the Tide.
Two of them at their labors, in the middle of his own Source!

chapters.title: Chapter 5554: The Well! I
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
Outside the obelisk, Noah turned and nodded once toward Hvitrmarr.

She understood before the gesture finished. Where a colossal white queen had stood in the ruined gold, white flame gathered inward and folded, gigantic mass drawing down through itself in a spiral of pale sovereign light, and when the light thinned a woman stood in the wreckage of the gardens.

Tall. White-haired. Twin spiral horns of ivory rose back from her temples, and her eyes had not changed at all, gold with ring inside ring for pupils. Her robe was white and dazzling and it was not cloth. Causes moved through it!
She rolled her shoulders once inside a shape she had not worn in a long while, and said nothing.
Ryaenara looked her up and down and made a small sound of pure appreciation as she whistled.
Damodred did not look at all, because a mountain does not turn its head for a change of clothes!
Theron Adranos watched all of it without comment, and then he stepped up to the obelisk.

He set his palm flat against the blue-gold stone. There was no incantation, no weaving, no authority pressed into it, and Noah watched carefully and confirmed what he already suspected. Theron gave off nothing. He simply touched it, and the obelisk knew him!
The light running up its faces reversed.

It poured downward instead of up, sheeting off the carved lines, pooling at the base and spreading outward across the scorched dirt in a slow widening ring, and where the light crossed the ruined ground the ruined ground was not there anymore. A doorway opened in the middle of a butchered garden, and through it came air that smelled of water!
"Come," Theron said. "See it, and then decide."
They went through!
Existence flickered with multicolored light all around as it felt unique!
Noah had crossed the dark between Dimensions on the back of a Steed and much more.
None of it had prepared him for the quiet on the other side of that stone!
|You have entered THE Hallowed Verdance of the Undivided Well.|

They stood on a shore of pale sand so fine it moved like water underfoot, and before them opened a basin without any visible far side. Water filled it. Not dark water and not still water, but a vast luminous expanse of gold-shot turquoise, lit from beneath rather than above, so that the whole immensity glowed upward and cast its light onto everything around it in slow drifting patterns!
Where the shallows lapped the sand they left rings of soft blue phosphorescence that faded and rekindled with each small wave.
Above and around it, the land had grown wild!
Now, he didn't usually care for environments too much unless it was his own Shore or Infiniverse, but this place...damn, it deserved to be looked at properly as it was too magisterial!

Cliffs of dark stone rose in tiers around the basin, and from every tier fell water, hundreds of falls, some thick as rivers and some thin as thread, dropping in long slow ribbons through air that seemed to hold them a moment longer than it should.

Mist hung in the gaps and caught the underlight, and out of the mist grew forests, huge trees with trunks so pale they read almost silver, their canopies dense and dark and hung everywhere with luminous vines that pulsed faintly in a rhythm Noah realized after a moment was synchronized, the whole valley breathing light in and out together.

Great flat islands drifted above the water, unmoored, drifting slowly on nothing, and they trailed their own waterfalls from their undersides in curtains that fell hundreds of miles and dissipated into mist before they ever touched the sea.
Ryaenara swore quietly, and then swore again with more feeling.
And at the center of it all, rising out of the sea, stood the pillar.

It was a tree. But it had no leaves and no branches and no crown, only a single colossal trunk of radiant pale wood climbing up out of the water and continuing until the mist and the distance swallowed it entirely. Its bark ran with veins of light in slow upward currents.
It did not seem to be growing. It simply stood, immense past reckoning, the axis the entire valley had arranged itself around, and the light beneath the sea was brightest at its roots.
And around that trunk, floating some distance out from the wood, hung a necklace.
Noah's attention locked onto it instantly, and so did everyone else's.
It was enormous, scaled to the pillar rather than to any wearer, a broad collar of gold that circled the trunk without touching it.

A collar, wide and layered, built of many rows of golden tubular beads strung tight and close so that the whole formed a single deep band, and along its lower edge hung a fringe of small teardrop pendants that swayed gently though there was no wind out over the water.

At its front, where a collar's clasp would sit, the rows converged into a single broad plate, and on that plate was worked a design Noah could not resolve even with his eyes, something that his sight kept sliding off.
It was translucent as he saw the pillar's light through it.
An illusion, then, or a manifestation!
Theron Adranos had gone still beside them, and when Noah looked at him, the golden-haired man had lowered his head.
"That is THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity," Theron said, and the reverence in his worn voice was total.

"It is not here. What you are looking at is its manifestation, and it appears in every domain like this one, above every well, in every valley behind every obelisk we have ever guarded. The same collar, the same size, the same silence. A child born in these lands sees it before she sees her own reflection."
He let out a breath.
"It is the legend at the core of what we are."
"Oh?" Noah said.
"I would have to start with the water for you to understand the legend," Theron said, "because the water is what everyone comes to steal, and the collar is what nobody understands."
He gestured out across the luminous expanse.
"This is THE Undivided Well. Look down. Not at the surface. Through it."
Noah looked, and found them.
Beneath the gold-shot turquoise, at depths that shifted as the light moved, they grew in their thousands. Flowers!

Or things that had decided to be flowers, radiant and slow-turning, each one a bloom of layered petals in blue and white and pale gold, and each one shed light rather than reflecting it, so that the entire sea was lit from below by the crop growing in it.

Some were small. Some were the size of islands. They opened and closed on a rhythm that matched the pulsing of the luminous vines in the forests, and looking at them for more than a moment made Noah aware of his own Causes turning inside his chest!

"THE Vermeil Bloom" Theron said. "The Panacea. That is what it is, and the word Panacea is what outsiders call it, and it is not wrong, only small. It cures. It elevates. It has done stranger things than either." He looked out over the water.

"It grew here on its own. Nobody planted it and nobody tends it. It is what made us. Every Superpowered Lifeform who has ever lived traces what they are back to this water, and that is why we are what we are, and why we give off nothing, and why we are hunted."

"It cannot simply be taken," Theron continued. "Every invader for ages has learned this, and most of them refused to believe it until they had thrown armies at it. The Well permits entry only to those who are PURE."

"Not clean. Not innocent. Not good, whatever that would mean. Pure in existence. True to what you actually are, without a seam between the thing you claim to be and the thing you are. The Well reads that, and if it does not like what it reads, you do not enter, and it does not matter in the least how powerful you are."

"And it has an inherent limit of once a year. One entry, one being. Whoever has gone in cannot go in again until the year has turned, no matter their standing, no matter their need. Those who are impure are refused, and those who have already gone are refused, and between those two rules the Well has fed a people for ages and never once been emptied."
Then Theron turned, and looked up at the collar hanging around the pillar, and his whole bearing changed.
"And that is the water," he said. "Now the legend."
"We hold that the collar came before the water."
Theron said it simply.

"That THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity is not a relic of this place but the ORIGIN of it. That every Panacea in every well in every valley of THE Ymnaros bloomed out of that collar's making, and the Blooms beneath your feet are its overflow. Not a gift it gave. A residue it left." He looked out at the translucent gold.
"If that is true, then everything we are, every Superpowered Lifeform who ever drew breath in these lands, is a downstream consequence of an object nobody has ever worn."
He raised a hand toward it.

"We hold that a Superpowered Lifeform will come who exemplifies what we are more truly than any of us has managed. Not the strongest. We have had monsters. Not the wisest, we have had those as well, and buried them. The one who is most COMPLETELY what a Superpowered Lifeform is, whose existence gives off nothing and contains everything, without a single seam in it anywhere." His voice roughened.

"And when that one comes, they will adorn the collar, and in adorning it they will wield the core power of our kind.  The thing itself, at its source, undiluted, the power that the Blooms are only the runoff of. And they will usher in an era of glory for a people who have spent every age we have ever had being farmed for our own inheritance."
Noah studied the hanging gold and did not interrupt.
"We do not know what that power is," Theron admitted.

He lowered his hand. "But we know the sign. When the worthy one finally stands beneath it, the collar's image will react. It will answer them. And when it answers, a pathway opens, and that pathway leads to the true collar, which does not hang above any well in any valley. It sits at the core of THE Ymnaros itself."

"That is the legend," Theron finished. "My people have died in rows in front of these obelisks for ages, guarding wells full of runoff, waiting for a manifestation to twitch. We have never seen it move."
The valley breathed light in and out around them, and the necklace hung motionless around the radiant pillar, and said nothing to anybody.
Noah nodded slowly, and turned his head away from the collar, and looked out at the sea.
At the Blooms turning in their thousands beneath the gold-shot water, lit from within, growing on their own out of an origin nobody had ever touched.
Was he a pure existence?
He had killed many. He had done many things!
He was greedy, and he was selfish!

"You are welcome to obtain the Panacea yourself, if the Well permits you. And those with you are welcome to try. Any of them. Walk into THE Undivided Well and see whether it lets you through, and if it does, take a Bloom."

He looked at each of them in turn, the horned woman in the Cause-woven robe, the profane Antiquity, the mild scholar, the mountain of calcified scars. "I would not presume to guess which of you it will accept. It has surprised us before, and it has broken hearts here more often than that."
Noah looked out across the luminous sea, at the radiant leafless pillar, at the collar of gold that had never once moved for anyone.
He would see who among his people was pure enough to attain these treasures!

Or things that had decided to be flowers, radiant and slow-turning, each one a bloom of layered petals in blue and white and pale gold, and each one shed light rather than reflecting it, so that the entire sea was lit from below by the crop growing in it.
Some were small.
Some were the size of islands.

They opened and closed on a rhythm that matched the pulsing of the luminous vines in the forests, and looking at them for more than a moment made Noah aware of his own Causes turning inside his chest!
"THE Vermeil Bloom" Theron said.
"The Panacea.
That is what it is, and the word Panacea is what outsiders call it, and it is not wrong, only small.
It cures.
It elevates.
It has done stranger things than either." He looked out over the water.
"It grew here on its own.
Nobody planted it and nobody tends it.
It is what made us.
Every Superpowered Lifeform who has ever lived traces what they are back to this water, and that is why we are what we are, and why we give off nothing, and why we are hunted."
"It cannot simply be taken," Theron continued.
"Every invader for ages has learned this, and most of them refused to believe it until they had thrown armies at it.
The Well permits entry only to those who are PURE."
"Not clean.
Not innocent.
Not good, whatever that would mean.
Pure in existence.
True to what you actually are, without a seam between the thing you claim to be and the thing you are.
The Well reads that, and if it does not like what it reads, you do not enter, and it does not matter in the least how powerful you are."
"And it has an inherent limit of once a year.
One entry, one being.
Whoever has gone in cannot go in again until the year has turned, no matter their standing, no matter their need.
Those who are impure are refused, and those who have already gone are refused, and between those two rules the Well has fed a people for ages and never once been emptied."
Then Theron turned, and looked up at the collar hanging around the pillar, and his whole bearing changed.
"And that is the water," he said.
"Now the legend."
"We hold that the collar came before the water."
Theron said it simply.
"That THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity is not a relic of this place but the ORIGIN of it.
That every Panacea in every well in every valley of THE Ymnaros bloomed out of that collar's making, and the Blooms beneath your feet are its overflow.
Not a gift it gave.
A residue it left." He looked out at the translucent gold.
"If that is true, then everything we are, every Superpowered Lifeform who ever drew breath in these lands, is a downstream consequence of an object nobody has ever worn."
He raised a hand toward it.
"We hold that a Superpowered Lifeform will come who exemplifies what we are more truly than any of us has managed.
Not the strongest.
We have had monsters.
Not the wisest, we have had those as well, and buried them.
The one who is most COMPLETELY what a Superpowered Lifeform is, whose existence gives off nothing and contains everything, without a single seam in it anywhere." His voice roughened.
"And when that one comes, they will adorn the collar, and in adorning it they will wield the core power of our kind.
The thing itself, at its source, undiluted, the power that the Blooms are only the runoff of.
And they will usher in an era of glory for a people who have spent every age we have ever had being farmed for our own inheritance."
Noah studied the hanging gold and did not interrupt.
"We do not know what that power is," Theron admitted.
He lowered his hand.
"But we know the sign.
When the worthy one finally stands beneath it, the collar's image will react.
It will answer them.
And when it answers, a pathway opens, and that pathway leads to the true collar, which does not hang above any well in any valley.
It sits at the core of THE Ymnaros itself."
"That is the legend," Theron finished.
"My people have died in rows in front of these obelisks for ages, guarding wells full of runoff, waiting for a manifestation to twitch.
We have never seen it move."
The valley breathed light in and out around them, and the necklace hung motionless around the radiant pillar, and said nothing to anybody.
Noah nodded slowly, and turned his head away from the collar, and looked out at the sea.
At the Blooms turning in their thousands beneath the gold-shot water, lit from within, growing on their own out of an origin nobody had ever touched.
Was he a pure existence?
He had killed many.
He had done many things!
He was greedy, and he was selfish!
"You are welcome to obtain the Panacea yourself, if the Well permits you.
And those with you are welcome to try.
Any of them.
Walk into THE Undivided Well and see whether it lets you through, and if it does, take a Bloom."
He looked at each of them in turn, the horned woman in the Cause-woven robe, the profane Antiquity, the mild scholar, the mountain of calcified scars.
"I would not presume to guess which of you it will accept.
It has surprised us before, and it has broken hearts here more often than that."
Noah looked out across the luminous sea, at the radiant leafless pillar, at the collar of gold that had never once moved for anyone.
He would see who among his people was pure enough to attain these treasures!

chapters.title: Chapter 5555: The Well! II
paragraphs: When it came to who should give a test of just how purr they were...Noah turned and looked at a certain Steed!
"You first," Noah said.
Hvitrmarr inclined her horned head and walked to the edge of the pale sand. She simply stepped off, and THE Undivided Well took her.
In truth, the question everyone had come here to ask was answered in that first moment, before anybody had time to be nervous on her behalf.
There was no ripple of refusal, no pause while something unseen considered her. The water opened the way a door opens for a hand that has always had the key.

Compared to the way she moved in the air, she moved through that sea like something coming home. Her white hair fanned out behind her, and the nine First Causes drifting in the weave of her robe brightened as the underlight found them, so that she went down trailing her own small constellation.

Below her, the Blooms turned in their thousands. Radiant flowers of blue and white and pale gold, opening and closing on a slow shared rhythm, and they lit her from beneath as she passed over them. Noah watched from the shore and found he had nothing at all to say about it.

Since she was not the sort to take more than she needed, she chose a bloom about the size of a shield. She closed her hand around its base and drew it free with a care that looked, from above, a great deal more like asking than taking.
Then she rose, and broke the surface without a sound, and came back across the water to the sand. She held THE Vermeil Bloom out to Noah in both hands, and its light shone up into her face.
"For you, Master."
Noah reached for it.
"Hold on."

Ryaenara had already got to her feet, and she said it loudly enough that every head on the shore turned. She was rolling her shoulders, and her eyes were on the sea with the exact expression she wore before a fight she intended to enjoy.
"Before you take that. I want to see... if I'm pure."

"I've been alive for too long. I've kept my word to people who didn't deserve it and broken it with people who did, and I have never once pretended to be anything I'm not. If anybody here is exactly what she says she is, it's me."
She reached the edge and dove, and... the water threw her back!
It happened so quickly that it took a moment to understand!
The surface rippled outward in a hard ring from the point she struck, and it did not part for her, and she came off it in a spray of gold-shot droplets and landed on her back in the sand.
"What?!"
She was furious!
Of course she was up again almost at once. She stared at the water, and then at her own hands, as though they had gone behind her back and done something she had not authorized.
"What?"

She went a second time, faster, and the Well shoved her out again, and she landed skidding through the fine sand. By the third attempt she had stopped being polite about it. Her Intent came off her in a heavy vibrant tide, and she drove herself at the surface like a thrown spear!
Despite all of that, the Well did not fight her. It did not brace, and it did not push back, and it never once answered her power with power of its own. It only declined!
Then nothing happened at all, for a while.
The waterfalls kept falling on the cliffs behind them, and the luminous vines in the silver forests kept breathing their light in and out, and none of it had any opinion.
Ryaenara sat in the pale sand with her Intent still burning around her and nothing anywhere to burn it against, and she looked...lost.
Theron Adranos looked away. There was no judgment anywhere on his worn face!
Noah went and stood beside her as he laughed inside a bit.
"Hang in there. We dont always have to be good at everything. And...So long as you are pure to yourself, I don't see why it should matter what a lake thinks about it.."
Ryaenara scoffed and stood and dusted off her legs as she voiced out...
"Hmph." She jerked her chin at the water. "Why don't you try, then? You talk big, but you may not be considered pure yourself, and I would like very much to watch you bounce."
Noah nodded and walked to the edge calmly.
Behind him the shore went quiet in a different way than before, and he could feel all of them at his back.
He asked himself the question honestly, one last time.
Was he pure? He had no idea, but he stepped off the sand anyway!
The Well opened for him.

There was no resistance at all. No test he could feel, no weighing, no moment where something considered him and came to a decision. The water simply took him in as it had taken Hvitrmarr, warm and clean and closing over his head!

It was quiet down there. An entire Dimension had bled over this water for ages, and the dark stone of the cliffs above was layered with the calcified strata of every ambition that had failed to reach the basin. Only slow light and slow current, and the great patient pillar rising up through all of it toward a sky he could no longer see.

Since the Blooms turned all around him as he went down, he had time to notice that his own eighteen Causes were turning in his chest to a rhythm not quite the same as theirs, and not quite different either. He chose one, and reached out, and closed his hand around its base!
The prompts came then.
|THE Vermeil Bloom. Panacea. Analysis follows.|
|Nature: a self-originated growth. It was not seeded, cultivated, or designed by any hand present in this Dimension.|

|Function, first order: it cures degradation. Terminal Causes, failing anchors, curses seated into a lineage, corruption grown into an existence at the root. What has begun to fail may be made whole. What has been sentenced may have the sentence lifted. May. Nothing is guaranteed.|
|Function, second order: it elevates. In a lifeform that consumes it, the Bloom does not add power. It resolves the existence into a truer version of itself, and grants power as the consequence.|
|Function, third order: in a being that possesses no Cause, the Bloom can potentially precipitate the emergence of one. A Purpose. An anchor where there was none.|
Noah read the third line twice, and then a third time.
Compared to what it had cost him to cure one Steed, that line was almost obscene!
|Ancillary observation, appended by THE Protagonist's Omniscient Regard rather than by the Bloom itself.|
|THE Vermeil Bloom is not a whole thing. Its structure reads as a component. Specifically, it reads as an accessory of ?????, in the way a shed scale reads as an accessory of the beast that shed it.|

|Further: the accessory is not inert. It is seeking. Every Bloom in this water, and in every water like it across this Dimension, is oriented. They have been looking for a very long time, and the Regard cannot determine what for.|
Noah's brows rose slowly beneath the water.
An accessory of something that was...seeking.

Theron had said the legend held that the collar came first and every Panacea was its overflow, and he had used the words runoff and residue, and had clearly never expected either of them to be read literally. But if each of these flowers was a piece shed from something larger, and if all of them were pointed outward and hunting, then what exactly were these Panaceas looking for?
The Bloom in his hands...answered him before he finished the thought!
HUUUM!
Black-gold light broke out of it, running along every petal in fine hot lines and then leaping off into the water, and it was nothing like the pale gold of the Well!
The lattice of it spread outward through the turquoise, and the nearest Blooms caught it, and then the ones beyond those, and then the ones beyond those!
BOOM
BOOM!

Ten thousand of them, if there were ten thousand down there. The whole crop of that sea lit in a spreading wave with Noah at the center of it, until the gentle underlight had drowned entirely beneath a black-gold radiance climbing up out of the deep, and every flower in the water had turned toward one man and begun to burn!

Above the surface, the valley went the same color. The waterfalls caught it, and the mist banks caught it, and the luminous vines lost their patient rhythm and blazed, and the drifting islands overhead lit from underneath!

As a result of all that, or perhaps as the reason for it, the great pillar at the center of THE Hallowed Verdance began to vibrate along its whole immeasurable length, and the currents of light in its bark reversed and ran downward toward the water.
And...the collar hanging around it began to shine!

THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity had hung above every well in every valley of this Dimension for the entire recorded history of a people. It had never moved for their greatest, nor their most beloved, nor for any of the ones they had been certain of, and generations had died in rows on the sand in front of the obelisks waiting for it to do anything whatsoever.
Now its rows of golden beads lit black and gold from within, and its teardrop fringe swayed, and the unreadable design on its front plate turned slowly and faced the water!
On the shore, Theron Adranos stood with his mouth open and did not manage to speak!
Ryaenara found her voice first.
"No fucking way." She took a step forward into the shallows, staring at the burning sea and then up at the shining collar above it. "No fucking way, right? Are you serious?"

Nobody answered her, because the two who might have were not looking at her at all. Hvitrmarr stood in the shallows with her own Bloom forgotten in her hands and her gold eyes fixed on the necklacs. Behind her the veil of ancient hands had turned upward!
In the black-gold light of ten thousand seeking flowers, the Steed and the dead thing watched an object older than any Panacea answer a man who had never once been anything but himself!
Pure!

chapters.title: Chapter 5556: Path I
paragraphs: <THE Ymnaros>
Far from THE Hallowed Verdance, past another obelisk in another valley, the same water lay under the same underlight, and everything else about the place was wrong.
The obelisk itself still shone its blue-gold. It had gone on shining while the men and women who guarded it were killed at its foot, and it was shining now over what had been left there afterward.
They had been laid out!
Two dozen Superpowered Lifeforms in white and blue, arranged in even rows on the pale sand inside the doorway, hands at their sides, faces turned up.
Nobody had done it out of respect. You could see that in the spacing, which was too regular, the spacing of inventory rather than of mourning. Someone had wanted them countable.
Inside the Well itself, more of them drifted.

The bodies had been put into the water. They turned slowly in the underlight among the Blooms, white and blue among blue and pale gold, sinking and rising on the currents, and the Panaceas went on opening and closing around them in their patient shared rhythm as though nothing at all had changed in the garden.
And all around that shore, in rows, stood the Infinite.

Dozens upon dozens of True Infinite Lifeforms holding the whole basin in a ring, their Infinity compounding quietly off them and pressing the mist flat, and among them the tall silent shapes of the Cenozoic in numbers that no single Observable Existence should ever have had to look at in one place!
They had been at this for some time.

One of the Cenozoic went in as the light shifted. It walked to the edge with the deliberateness of a thing that had already been refused once and had reasoned its way to a different approach, and it entered the water.
The Well threw it out.

The surface rippled in a hard concentric shove and the thing came off it and landed among the rows of the dead, scattering two of them out of their neat alignment, and it rose without expression and walked back to its place in the ring.
Another went. Another shove. Another rejection.

A third tried it slowly, wading, testing whether patience read differently to the water than force did. The Well waited until it was up to the knee and then declined it as flatly as it had declined the others!

A fourth arrived carrying one of the corpses, on the theory, presumably, that the water might read the passenger rather than the carrier. The Well rejected them both, and the body came back with it, and the thing dropped it on the sand and did not look down!

So it went. Dozens of them, ancient, Cenozoic, holding between them enough power to unmake an Observable Existence outright, taking turns at a lake and being turned away by it one after another without so much as a fight to lose.
Far above all of that, well clear of the water, four figures hung in the black-shot air.
Three of them did not fit on any ladder.
Every other existence in the valley could be placed, weighed, and slotted somewhere on a Scale, and these three simply could not, in the same way that Jarl Skallagrim could not!

The first was made of hanging chain. Or wore it, or had been wound in it so long ago that the difference had stopped mattering, a titan-shape of black links draped in coils from shoulder to ankle, and where the links crossed there were faces worn into the metal by pressure alone, and none of the faces were finished.

The second had no surface anywhere on it. It was a titan of running dark liquid held in the shape of a body by nothing anyone could see, and the liquid moved constantly downward and never emptied, and at the places where eyes belonged there were only two points where the falling was faster.

The third stood in stone armor grown over with a pale calcified crust, and it was the only one of the three that had bothered with a face, and the face was serene, and it had been serene for a very long time.
And at their center, smaller than any of them, floated a man in a crimson robe.
He was the reason the other three arranged themselves the way they did.

He looked ancient in the manner of things that predate their own memory of themselves, and he also looked wild, hair loose and moving in no wind, and beneath both of those he looked mad in a way that was not theatrical at all!

There was no raving in him. There was only the sense, immediate and unpleasant, of a mind that had gone somewhere a long time ago and had never seen a reason to come back, and had been extremely capable the whole time.
He watched the Cenozoic being bounced off the water below, and he seemed to find it neither amusing nor frustrating.
The one in chains spoke, and it spoke with the careful respect of something enormous addressing something it considered its better.
"The Dimensionlapse has given us the opening we waited ages for, Master." Its voice came out of the worn faces in the metal rather than from anywhere on its body.
"Their walls are meaningless now, their Halls route nothing, and we can arrive anywhere inside THE Ymnaros we please. After so long being kept at the door, we are inside the house."
The crimson-robed man said nothing.

"But we have taken multiple valleys," the chained titan continued, "and we cannot take the water in any of them. The Panaceas are almost impossible for us to grasp ourselves. If they are the object, then the practical route is the one we have been avoiding, which is to take the Superpowered Lifeforms alive in numbers, and keep them, and make them harvest for us."
The liquid one poured downward and said nothing. The calcified one remained serene.

"Which is what I do not understand" The faces in the chain shifted. "This Dimension is not the richest. It is not the best defended, nor the best positioned, and its people are strange and small and have nothing that other places do not have more of. Why here, master? Of all the Dimensions in existence, why are we in this one?"
And before any answer came, the valley answered for him.
At the center of the Well, the great pillar began to shine.

The colossal leafless trunk that rose out of the water and continued past sight lit along its whole immeasurable length, the currents in its bark running downward, and around it the illusory collar of gold that had hung there in silence for the entire recorded history of a people blazed resplendent with black-gold light!
Every Infinite Lifeform in the ring turned to look.

The one in chains fell silent. The dark liquid stopped falling for perhaps half a heartbeat and then resumed. And the crimson-robed man, who had not reacted to anything at all since he arrived in this valley, frowned.
It was the first expression he had worn.
"That," he said, "is why we are here."
He did not take his eyes off the collar.

"Across existence there are objects that do not belong to any age that can be dated. Remnant Existential Treasures. Older than the Primeval Ones, older than the frameworks the Primevals sit beneath, and most of the ones anybody has ever managed to trace lead back to Those Who Remain themselves."
WAA!
"They are not artifacts. Artifacts were made by somebody who wanted something. These are remnants. They were... left."
The three around him waited.

"This little necklace," the crimson-robed man said, "hanging in a fishpond, in a valley, in a Dimension full of costumed farmers who give off no authority. A great many patient beings have suspected for a very long time that it is one of them. I came to confirm it, and to take it, and I expected to spend an age doing so."
Then his voice changed, and the madness in him came up out of the calm without raising its volume at all.
"So why."

"Why the fuck is the legend of these ungrateful costume-wearing fuckers activating now? This age. This month. This afternoon, while I am standing in the water they die for?" His hair moved in its absent wind.

"For ages they dreamed about it. Generations of them died in rows in front of these stones waiting for that thing to twitch, and it never twitched, not for their best, not for their most loved, not for any of the poor hopeful bastards who were certain. And I arrive to claim it, and something appears and trips the pathway toward it within a breath of my getting here."
He laughed once. It was a short, entirely humorless sound!
"Is existence trying to fuck with me? Haha. Unbelievable."
The frown smoothed away!

"Fine. Come on. I will burn this place down to make certain I have hold of it before whatever tripped that pathway walks to the end of it." He turned in the air, robe moving, already deciding logistics.

"Ground the blood of a few million of these Superpowered Lifeforms into the water. That should be enough to force the matter, and if it is not, we will find out with the next few million. There are enough of them, and they do not run."
He looked back once at the shining collar, and the madness in him settled into something patient.
"Alright, you all. Let's move."
And the three titans that fit on no ladder inclined themselves, and followed, and there was not a moment of hesitation in any of them, nor any question about whether the order was reasonable.
Of course they followed.
They had been following for a very long time, and they would go on following, because they were THE Followers of THE Sealed One.
Who else would they follow?

Far from THE Hallowed Verdance, past another obelisk in another valley, the same water lay under the same underlight, and everything else about the place was wrong.
The obelisk itself still shone its blue-gold.
It had gone on shining while the men and women who guarded it were killed at its foot, and it was shining now over what had been left there afterward.
They had been laid out!
Two dozen Superpowered Lifeforms in white and blue, arranged in even rows on the pale sand inside the doorway, hands at their sides, faces turned up.
Nobody had done it out of respect.
You could see that in the spacing, which was too regular, the spacing of inventory rather than of mourning.
Someone had wanted them countable.
Inside the Well itself, more of them drifted.
The bodies had been put into the water.

They turned slowly in the underlight among the Blooms, white and blue among blue and pale gold, sinking and rising on the currents, and the Panaceas went on opening and closing around them in their patient shared rhythm as though nothing at all had changed in the garden.
And all around that shore, in rows, stood the Infinite.

Dozens upon dozens of True Infinite Lifeforms holding the whole basin in a ring, their Infinity compounding quietly off them and pressing the mist flat, and among them the tall silent shapes of the Cenozoic in numbers that no single Observable Existence should ever have had to look at in one place!
They had been at this for some time.
One of the Cenozoic went in as the light shifted.
It walked to the edge with the deliberateness of a thing that had already been refused once and had reasoned its way to a different approach, and it entered the water.
The Well threw it out.

The surface rippled in a hard concentric shove and the thing came off it and landed among the rows of the dead, scattering two of them out of their neat alignment, and it rose without expression and walked back to its place in the ring.
Another went.
Another shove.
Another rejection.
A third tried it slowly, wading, testing whether patience read differently to the water than force did.
The Well waited until it was up to the knee and then declined it as flatly as it had declined the others!
A fourth arrived carrying one of the corpses, on the theory, presumably, that the water might read the passenger rather than the carrier.
The Well rejected them both, and the body came back with it, and the thing dropped it on the sand and did not look down!
So it went.

Dozens of them, ancient, Cenozoic, holding between them enough power to unmake an Observable Existence outright, taking turns at a lake and being turned away by it one after another without so much as a fight to lose.
Far above all of that, well clear of the water, four figures hung in the black-shot air.
Three of them did not fit on any ladder.
Every other existence in the valley could be placed, weighed, and slotted somewhere on a Scale, and these three simply could not, in the same way that Jarl Skallagrim could not!
The first was made of hanging chain.

Or wore it, or had been wound in it so long ago that the difference had stopped mattering, a titan-shape of black links draped in coils from shoulder to ankle, and where the links crossed there were faces worn into the metal by pressure alone, and none of the faces were finished.
The second had no surface anywhere on it.

It was a titan of running dark liquid held in the shape of a body by nothing anyone could see, and the liquid moved constantly downward and never emptied, and at the places where eyes belonged there were only two points where the falling was faster.

The third stood in stone armor grown over with a pale calcified crust, and it was the only one of the three that had bothered with a face, and the face was serene, and it had been serene for a very long time.
And at their center, smaller than any of them, floated a man in a crimson robe.
He was the reason the other three arranged themselves the way they did.

He looked ancient in the manner of things that predate their own memory of themselves, and he also looked wild, hair loose and moving in no wind, and beneath both of those he looked mad in a way that was not theatrical at all!
There was no raving in him.
There was only the sense, immediate and unpleasant, of a mind that had gone somewhere a long time ago and had never seen a reason to come back, and had been extremely capable the whole time.
He watched the Cenozoic being bounced off the water below, and he seemed to find it neither amusing nor frustrating.
The one in chains spoke, and it spoke with the careful respect of something enormous addressing something it considered its better.
"The Dimensionlapse has given us the opening we waited ages for, Master." Its voice came out of the worn faces in the metal rather than from anywhere on its body.
"Their walls are meaningless now, their Halls route nothing, and we can arrive anywhere inside THE Ymnaros we please.
After so long being kept at the door, we are inside the house."
The crimson-robed man said nothing.
"But we have taken multiple valleys," the chained titan continued, "and we cannot take the water in any of them.
The Panaceas are almost impossible for us to grasp ourselves.
If they are the object, then the practical route is the one we have been avoiding, which is to take the Superpowered Lifeforms alive in numbers, and keep them, and make them harvest for us."
The liquid one poured downward and said nothing.
The calcified one remained serene.
"Which is what I do not understand" The faces in the chain shifted.
"This Dimension is not the richest.
It is not the best defended, nor the best positioned, and its people are strange and small and have nothing that other places do not have more of.
Why here, master?
Of all the Dimensions in existence, why are we in this one?"
And before any answer came, the valley answered for him.
At the center of the Well, the great pillar began to shine.

The colossal leafless trunk that rose out of the water and continued past sight lit along its whole immeasurable length, the currents in its bark running downward, and around it the illusory collar of gold that had hung there in silence for the entire recorded history of a people blazed resplendent with black-gold light!
Every Infinite Lifeform in the ring turned to look.
The one in chains fell silent.
The dark liquid stopped falling for perhaps half a heartbeat and then resumed.
And the crimson-robed man, who had not reacted to anything at all since he arrived in this valley, frowned.
It was the first expression he had worn.
"That," he said, "is why we are here."
He did not take his eyes off the collar.
"Across existence there are objects that do not belong to any age that can be dated.
Remnant Existential Treasures.
Older than the Primeval Ones, older than the frameworks the Primevals sit beneath, and most of the ones anybody has ever managed to trace lead back to Those Who Remain themselves."
WAA!
"They are not artifacts.
Artifacts were made by somebody who wanted something.
These are remnants.
They were... left."
The three around him waited.
"This little necklace," the crimson-robed man said, "hanging in a fishpond, in a valley, in a Dimension full of costumed farmers who give off no authority.
A great many patient beings have suspected for a very long time that it is one of them.
I came to confirm it, and to take it, and I expected to spend an age doing so."
Then his voice changed, and the madness in him came up out of the calm without raising its volume at all.
"So why."
"Why the fuck is the legend of these ungrateful costume-wearing fuckers activating now?
This age.
This month.
This afternoon, while I am standing in the water they die for?" His hair moved in its absent wind.
"For ages they dreamed about it.

Generations of them died in rows in front of these stones waiting for that thing to twitch, and it never twitched, not for their best, not for their most loved, not for any of the poor hopeful bastards who were certain.
And I arrive to claim it, and something appears and trips the pathway toward it within a breath of my getting here."
He laughed once.
It was a short, entirely humorless sound!
"Is existence trying to fuck with me?
Haha.
Unbelievable."
The frown smoothed away!

Come on.
I will burn this place down to make certain I have hold of it before whatever tripped that pathway walks to the end of it." He turned in the air, robe moving, already deciding logistics.

That should be enough to force the matter, and if it is not, we will find out with the next few million.
There are enough of them, and they do not run."
He looked back once at the shining collar, and the madness in him settled into something patient.
"Alright, you all.
Let's move."
And the three titans that fit on no ladder inclined themselves, and followed, and there was not a moment of hesitation in any of them, nor any question about whether the order was reasonable.
Of course they followed.
They had been following for a very long time, and they would go on following, because they were THE Followers of THE Sealed One.
Who else would they follow?

chapters.title: Chapter 5557: Path II
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
In truth, Noah did not know what to make of any of it!

He had never believed in destiny. Or rather, he had never believed in a destiny that arrived from outside, handed down by something that had decided things about him in advance. Destiny as a thing to be designed, on the other hand, was a different matter entirely, and he had built a Civilization of it once and hung its threads where he wanted them.
So he was not a chosen one.
Although, of course, there was the grand fact of the fifth Letter.

Because he had written PROTAGONIST into himself, deliberately, and the whole point of that Letter was that adversity fed him and that fate-adjacent things bent when they got too close. Was that what had happened here? Had a legend belonging to a people he had met a little while ago simply mistaken a Letter for a prophecy? Or had it been something else in him, the Osmontian Causes, the Marrow, the eighteen collisions running in his chest, some part of what he was resonating with a thing that had been waiting to resonate for ages?
There were no coincidences, in his experience. There were only mechanisms he had not identified yet!

Not that he was complaining! The question that actually mattered was how difficult the next part would be. The manifestation reacting did not hand anyone the collar. It opened a pathway toward it. And nobody had ever walked that pathway.
He put the Bloom away, and rose out of the water.
The commotion above was heavier than he had left it. Theron Adranos was trembling, openly, in front of everyone!
Anaximander had a wry look on his face when Noah came up onto the sand.
"Brother," the scholar said, "how do you always do these things? I am not complaining, since it may well be the thing that carries us through what is coming. But wow."
Noah shook his head and looked out at the distant trunk.
"I'm as lost as you are," he said calmly. "I might have tripped something by mistake. It's entirely possible none of this has anything to do with me."
As it turned out, that was the wrong thing to say in that valley.
Because the sky churned then, harder than it had been churning, the black-gold light in the mist thickening overhead, and a voice came out of all of it at once.
|No, it is definitely connected to you.|
Everyone went quiet.

Ryaenara stopped mid-motion in the shallows. Anaximander's wry expression emptied out. And Hvitrmarr and Damodred both moved without a word spoken between them, the steed coming up on Noah's left and the titan settling in behind his right shoulder, close enough that the valley darkened where he stood!
Theron went to his knees in the sand as his face filled with reverence!
"O Ancestral Voice." His own voice cracked on it. "Has the time truly come?!"
The Ancestral Voice.
Noah's eyes went sharp, and he reached out with everything he had, and found nothing whatsoever. No presence, no weaving, no location, no origin. The voice was not coming from a direction!
|Since we are all pressed for time, I will be brief, and I would prefer not to repeat myself.|

|At this moment, invaders are butchering Superpowered Lifeforms across this Dimension. Laying them out in rows and putting them in the water and grinding them down, for greed, and in some cases for pleasure.|

|If nothing is done, they will have everything regardless. The collar. The wells. The Blooms. All of it, at their leisure, after the last of my descendants is used up. I have watched it get worse while waiting for a candidate who met the standard.|
|So I made a gamble. I lowered the restrictions on who may be considered worthy to grasp THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity.|
|You meet the lowered tier of requirements.|

|Which means it is now a race, and the thing you are racing is time. Obtain it, and there may still be Superpowered Lifeforms left in this Dimension to be saved. Fail to, or dawdle, and there will not be.|
Out at the center of the Well, the pillar answered.

A column of golden-black light bloomed off the trunk and climbed, and where it reached the height of the drifting islands it opened, folding out and inward at once until a doorway of black and gold hung in the sky above the water.
Noah looked up at it with shining eyes.
"Who are you?" he asked.
|Does it matter?|

|I am the dying voice of a Primeval thing that could not let go of something. Ancestral Voice is more than enough for you to be going on with, and it is what they have called me for ages, and I have never bothered to correct them.|

|Now. Time is of the essence, as a madman has begun to butcher Superpowered Lifeforms in numbers even I did not anticipate. So. Will you move? Will you go and see whether those measly credentials of yours can actually obtain THE Aurate Collar?|

|If that dragon standing beside you had been the one chosen, this would have been considerably easier. If that monster wearing severed hands for a blindfold had been chosen, easier still. Alas, they do not meet the requirements|
|Enter. And since you are the one who must attempt it, you enter alone, or the path dissipates.|
Noah shook his head, internally, at the sheer nerve of it!
Insulted, recruited, and put on a clock by something that would not even give a name!
He began to rise out of the sand.

He could not take Hvitrmarr, and he could not take Damodred, and while he thought about that he also thought about the words of how a madman had begun to butcher, and what those words meant about the next hour in a Dimension he had walked into for a look around.
So he turned to the two of them, and spoke calmly.

"You two. Take Anaximander and Ryaenara across to wherever they're being butchered." He looked at Hvitrmarr, then up at the veil of hands. "Kill the Infinite True Lifeforms. All of them you find. And if you sense anything too powerful, anything that doesn't measure, pull back. Okay?"
"Understood," Hvitrmarr said.
Since it was only human to help, and since he had said as much out loud before he came through that obelisk, Noah then raised his head toward the churning sky!
"Can you help guide them?" he asked. "To wherever the Superpowered Lifeforms are dying the most. You clearly care what happens to them, and my people can help."
There was, after all, no reason a voice that protective should not be put to work.

And he was thinking about several things at once. Whatever this pathway turned out to be, his forces would not be idle during it, and a Dimension full of invading Infinite Lifeforms was a Dimension full of corpses and loot with Infinity still in them.
The voice was quiet for a moment.
|I will direct them where they need to be.|
Noah nodded, and took a step, and appeared before the golden black doorway.
Then he looked back.
Hvitrmarr was frowning. He could feel it through the bond more clearly than he could see it on her face, the whole of her objecting leaving him alone.
And Damodred spoke, and his voice rolled up through the valley from somewhere behind his ribs.
'The Master's existence is surrounded by a grand weaving of his own making, and by a destiny he wrote himself. There is nothing in that doorway that was not already answering to him.'
'I will kill and collapse out here on your behalf. I will protect these little ones. Do not worry.'
The words sat heavily on the sand, and Hvitrmarr's frown did not leave, but her shoulders came down.
Noah nodded once to both of them, and stepped through the doorway, and was gone!
