chapters.title: Chapter 5558: Outcasts!
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
The suppression arrived before he had finished stepping.

It came as waves rather than as a wall, rolling through him one after another and settling in the places where his facets lived, and although Noah had felt suppression before, this was something else.
This was procedural. It did not fight him. It simply went through his existence closing doors!
|Welcome to THE Ancestral Grounds of Ymnaros.|
|The vast weavings of authority are suppressed here. All facets of your existence are locked, and will remain so. You will be permitted to keep a single thing.|
|What within your existence do you wish to keep?|
Since he had perhaps two heartbeats before the question stopped being an offer, Noah did not spend them being surprised.

He weighed all. His Osmontian Source Infinity was the deepest well he had, but a well is only useful if you can carry water in something. His Ananke Intent was the second order and it had never once failed him, and yet Intent needed a shape to press through. THE Collision of Causes was an engine and engines needed hands. And every appendage he had was a hand that would be closed by whatever had just closed the rest.
Of course, there was only one thing on the list that was not an instrument at all.
"My Osmontian Tongue," he said.
HUUM!
The gold and black seas around him churned, and the prompts came down.
|Selection accepted.|

|All facets of your existence are hereby unusable. Osmontian Source Infinity: locked. Volume: locked. Output: locked. Trueness: locked. The Nine Foundations: locked. THE Ananke Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian: locked. THE Collision of Causes: suspended. All appendages: sealed. THE Quintessential Confluence: unavailable.|
|Retained: THE Osmontian Tongue. Five Letters and one Word.|
HUUM!
When the churning cleared he found himself standing on a road!

It ran out of the darkness beneath his feet and continued ahead of him as far as he could see, shimmering stellar obsidian shot through with gold, and there was nothing else anywhere. No ground beside it, no sky above it, only an expanse of spatial dark in every direction with a single path drawn through it, and it went on past any point where seeing stopped being useful.
Noah stood and looked at that for a moment, and did not step.
|In existence, the unknowns always exceed the known.|
The Ancestral Voice came differently in here. Some of the imperiousness had gone out of it, and what had replaced it was closer to melancholy.

|This is true for almost every lifeform that has ever drawn breath, and most of them live comfortably enough within it. THE Ymnaros was blessed to have an unknown. It was cursed because the unknown it had was far too grand for it.|

|That grandness made my people into Superpowered Lifeforms. It also guaranteed, from the first age, that it would eventually be the thing that brought them to cataclysm, because a small people sitting on top of something enormous will always eventually be visited by something that wants it. That has been the shape of our entire history, and the shape was set before any of us could read it.|
|And in all those ages, my people never produced a single one who could grasp that grandness. Not one. So in the final moments, having run out of our own, I have expanded the search externally.|
|Now here you are.|
Noah listened to all of that calmly.
"What made me fulfill the requirements," he asked, "when someone like Hvitrmarr didn't? Or Damodred. The dragon and the titan out there. Both of them are considerably more than I am."
|Potential.|

|There have been Superpowered Lifeforms across our history more powerful than you are at this moment, and some of them stood on that sand and were declined. The standard was never a measurement of what a thing is.|

|In existence, what could be is always greater than what is. A finished thing has a ceiling and can be priced. An unfinished thing cannot, and that unpriceable quantity is what the collar was made to answer.|
|However.|

|Potential is also the easiest thing in existence to stifle, waste, or simply lie about. Anything can look like it might become something. So it must be tested, which means you must be tested, and I take no pleasure in the necessity.|
There was a pause, and the melancholy went out of the voice and something drier came in.

|If I had the capability, I would take THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity in my own hands and give it to whomever I chose, and I would have done so ages ago, and a great many of my descendants would still be alive. But existence does not work that way. It always has to be so fucking complicated.|
|So. The first test, as you walk this path.|
|When you have lost almost all of your power, except one thing, how do you fight?|
Ahead of him on the road, auras began to rise.
They rose in a line across it, blazing up out of nothing, and they were humanoid, or had been.

Each shape held roughly the proportions of a person and then failed them somewhere, a shoulder carried too high, an arm that had continued past where an arm ends, spines where a spine should not surface, the whole silhouette reading like something that had been correct and had then kept growing.
And each of them wore white and blue!

The same suits. The same simple cut Theron Adranos wore, the same chest sign designed to be recognized at a distance by frightened people, ragged now and stretched wrong over the shapes underneath, but unmistakably the same.
Their eyes were full of a murky obsidian light, and there was nothing behind it but madness.

Compared to the invaders in the gardens, they gave off nothing at all. Not one wave of authority, exactly as Theron gave off nothing, exactly as every one of their kind gave off nothing. And yet standing at the near end of that road, Noah felt the pressure of them come down the obsidian gold like weather rolling off a mountain.
"These are..." he said slowly, "mutated Superpowered Lifeforms?"
|Across existence, accidents are inevitable.|

|The emergence of a Superpowered Lifeform is not always so pretty as the ones you have met. The Blooms resolve an existence into a truer version of itself, and most of the time that is a gift. Sometimes the truer version is a horror, and the water does not consult anyone before it finishes the work.|

|And there are the others. Superpowered Lifeforms who took what the Blooms gave them and used it to oppress, to press down on their own, to decimate whatever was smaller than they were. In those cases the rejection does not come from us. Their own existence rejects them, and turns into this.|

|These are THE Outcasts. The dark underbelly of every accident and vileness THE Ymnaros has produced, kept here, on this road, because there was nowhere else to keep them and because someone walking toward the collar should have to look at them.|
|Pass through them, and you may continue on your path.|
Noah looked ahead and counted.
Thirty-six of them, standing across the road!

Each one carried an oppression that measured as grand as a Cenozoic Scale being at minimum, and several of them read heavier than that, which raised a question he did not have time to answer properly.
Were they all S-Rank? SS?

The Outcasts did not wait for him to work it out. They came, all at once, thirty-six ruined shapes surging down the obsidian gold road, and Noah stood there with his facets locked, his Intent sealed, his Causes suspended, and one Tongue in his mouth!
And...
"THE MORTAL COIL."
Blue light flashed out around him.
|THE DOMAIN OF THE MORTAL COIL has been laid.|

|Within its bounds all authority is designated absent. Every Scale, every Intent, every Pantheon, every Cause, every claim of power stacked upon an existence. Beings within stand as only what a human is beneath it, a life that can dream, and hope, and end.|
|Wielder privilege: as THE True Human Emperor, you retain the standing of an F-Rank Hunter.|

|Note: the domain does not require access to your locked facets. It is a Word of your own Tongue, and a Word is not a weaving. It is a truth spoken aloud, and a truth cannot be suppressed by a ground that has no opinion on whether it is true.|
Although the domain had worked exactly as intended in the gardens, Noah had not forgotten the one detail that mattered.
Theron Adranos had stood inside it and felt nothing. Whole, unchanged, himself.
Ruination's reading of that was that Superpowered Lifeform strength was not authority at all, and therefore not the sort of thing the Word could take.
So this time, as he spoke it, Noah did not aim it at authority.

He aimed it at everything. He pressed the intent through the Word with a specificity he had not used before, at power and at not-power, at authority and at whatever else a thing might be carrying instead, at the whole of every existence on that road down to the plain mortal animal underneath, regardless of what framework any of it belonged to!
Everything here would be human!
OOOOH!
Ahead of him, THE Outcasts sensed it.

The change went through the line like a wave breaking backward, and thirty-six ruined shapes threw back their heads and roared, and the sound in it was not rage. It was pain, and it was fervor, and it was the noise of things that had been kept in the dark on a road for ages suddenly feeling something take hold of them that they had not felt since whatever they were before.
Then they surged, all of them, straight at him!

sentences.text: <THE True Human Emperor>
The suppression arrived before he had finished stepping.

It came as waves rather than as a wall, rolling through him one after another and settling in the places where his facets lived, and although Noah had felt suppression before, this was something else.
This was procedural.
It did not fight him.
It simply went through his existence closing doors!
|Welcome to THE Ancestral Grounds of Ymnaros.|
|The vast weavings of authority are suppressed here.
All facets of your existence are locked, and will remain so.
You will be permitted to keep a single thing.|
|What within your existence do you wish to keep?|
Since he had perhaps two heartbeats before the question stopped being an offer, Noah did not spend them being surprised.
He weighed all.
His Osmontian Source Infinity was the deepest well he had, but a well is only useful if you can carry water in something.
His Ananke Intent was the second order and it had never once failed him, and yet Intent needed a shape to press through.
THE Collision of Causes was an engine and engines needed hands.
And every appendage he had was a hand that would be closed by whatever had just closed the rest.
Of course, there was only one thing on the list that was not an instrument at all.
"My Osmontian Tongue," he said.
HUUM!
The gold and black seas around him churned, and the prompts came down.
|Selection accepted.|
|All facets of your existence are hereby unusable.
Osmontian Source Infinity: locked.
Volume: locked.
Output: locked.
Trueness: locked.
The Nine Foundations: locked.
THE Ananke Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian: locked.
THE Collision of Causes: suspended.
All appendages: sealed.
THE Quintessential Confluence: unavailable.|
|Retained: THE Osmontian Tongue.
Five Letters and one Word.|
HUUM!
When the churning cleared he found himself standing on a road!
It ran out of the darkness beneath his feet and continued ahead of him as far as he could see, shimmering stellar obsidian shot through with gold, and there was nothing else anywhere.
No ground beside it, no sky above it, only an expanse of spatial dark in every direction with a single path drawn through it, and it went on past any point where seeing stopped being useful.
Noah stood and looked at that for a moment, and did not step.
|In existence, the unknowns always exceed the known.|
The Ancestral Voice came differently in here.
Some of the imperiousness had gone out of it, and what had replaced it was closer to melancholy.
|This is true for almost every lifeform that has ever drawn breath, and most of them live comfortably enough within it.
THE Ymnaros was blessed to have an unknown.
It was cursed because the unknown it had was far too grand for it.|
|That grandness made my people into Superpowered Lifeforms.

It also guaranteed, from the first age, that it would eventually be the thing that brought them to cataclysm, because a small people sitting on top of something enormous will always eventually be visited by something that wants it.
That has been the shape of our entire history, and the shape was set before any of us could read it.|
|And in all those ages, my people never produced a single one who could grasp that grandness.
Not one.
So in the final moments, having run out of our own, I have expanded the search externally.|
|Now here you are.|
Noah listened to all of that calmly.
"What made me fulfill the requirements," he asked, "when someone like Hvitrmarr didn't?
Or Damodred.
The dragon and the titan out there.
Both of them are considerably more than I am."
|Potential.|
|There have been Superpowered Lifeforms across our history more powerful than you are at this moment, and some of them stood on that sand and were declined.
The standard was never a measurement of what a thing is.|
|In existence, what could be is always greater than what is.
A finished thing has a ceiling and can be priced.
An unfinished thing cannot, and that unpriceable quantity is what the collar was made to answer.|
|However.|
|Potential is also the easiest thing in existence to stifle, waste, or simply lie about.
Anything can look like it might become something.
So it must be tested, which means you must be tested, and I take no pleasure in the necessity.|
There was a pause, and the melancholy went out of the voice and something drier came in.

|If I had the capability, I would take THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity in my own hands and give it to whomever I chose, and I would have done so ages ago, and a great many of my descendants would still be alive.
But existence does not work that way.
It always has to be so fucking complicated.|
|So.
The first test, as you walk this path.|
|When you have lost almost all of your power, except one thing, how do you fight?|
Ahead of him on the road, auras began to rise.
They rose in a line across it, blazing up out of nothing, and they were humanoid, or had been.

Each shape held roughly the proportions of a person and then failed them somewhere, a shoulder carried too high, an arm that had continued past where an arm ends, spines where a spine should not surface, the whole silhouette reading like something that had been correct and had then kept growing.
And each of them wore white and blue!
The same suits.

The same simple cut Theron Adranos wore, the same chest sign designed to be recognized at a distance by frightened people, ragged now and stretched wrong over the shapes underneath, but unmistakably the same.
Their eyes were full of a murky obsidian light, and there was nothing behind it but madness.
Compared to the invaders in the gardens, they gave off nothing at all.
Not one wave of authority, exactly as Theron gave off nothing, exactly as every one of their kind gave off nothing.
And yet standing at the near end of that road, Noah felt the pressure of them come down the obsidian gold like weather rolling off a mountain.
"These are..." he said slowly, "mutated Superpowered Lifeforms?"
|Across existence, accidents are inevitable.|
|The emergence of a Superpowered Lifeform is not always so pretty as the ones you have met.
The Blooms resolve an existence into a truer version of itself, and most of the time that is a gift.
Sometimes the truer version is a horror, and the water does not consult anyone before it finishes the work.|
|And there are the others.
Superpowered Lifeforms who took what the Blooms gave them and used it to oppress, to press down on their own, to decimate whatever was smaller than they were.
In those cases the rejection does not come from us.
Their own existence rejects them, and turns into this.|
|These are THE Outcasts.

The dark underbelly of every accident and vileness THE Ymnaros has produced, kept here, on this road, because there was nowhere else to keep them and because someone walking toward the collar should have to look at them.|
|Pass through them, and you may continue on your path.|
Noah looked ahead and counted.
Thirty-six of them, standing across the road!

chapters.title: Chapter 5559: Pride!
paragraphs: The first one reached him and it was nearly twice his size!

Made human, an Outcast was still a body that had gone on growing past where a body stops, and no Word in existence was going to shrink a shoulder or unbend a spine or take back the reach of an arm that had continued. He had removed their power. He had not removed their mass!
And, since he had a river of nothing to draw on, he was going to have to do this with his hands.
So he opened his mouth as the shape came down on him.
"I AM."
HUUM!
The affirmation went through him gloriously!

There was no facet behind it, no Source Infinity, no Intent, nothing at all except two words of his own Tongue spoken by the existence that had written them, and that turned out to be enough. His frame filled. His arms went heavy in a way that had nothing to do with weight!

The declaration was not a spell being cast, it was an existence stating the plain fact of itself out loud in a place that had suppressed everything except the ability to do so, and existence had no argument prepared against a thing insisting it was!
He caught the descending arm at the elbow and broke it the wrong way.
CRACK!

Then he stepped inside the ruined shape's reach and drove his palm up under its jaw, and the blow landed like a hammer coming off an anvil, and the head came back and the whole body followed it, and Noah went with it and put his other hand through its chest as...The Outcast came apart on the obsidian gold road.
Bloof began to flow!
Two more were already on him before he could even pause!
"I AM OSMONT."

He said it low, and the second affirmation stacked onto the first, and the road cracked under his heel as he pivoted. His hand came across in a flat edge and took the nearest one's throat open, and he did not stop moving, because stopping was the thing that would kill him here!
These Outcasts were not soldiers. They fought like animals that had been in pain for a very long time and had finally been given something to put their hands on.
Compared to the army in the gardens, this was infinitely more dangerous.
So he weaved.

He went through the middle of them rather than around, because the road was narrow and there was nowhere else to be. A blow came in from his left and he was not there for it. A second closed on his shoulder and he broke the wrist attached to it and used the arm as a handle to put its owner into the path of a third as he smashed them together like sacks of grain!
"I AM HUMAN."
WAA!
He waved his hand as it cleanly cut through an Outcasts whole, their body split in two as they twitched hatefully below him!

An Outcast got a hand on him at that moment, actually got a grip, and for a moment Noah's whole body was lifted off the obsidian gold with fingers closing on his ribs, and he reached back and took hold of the thumb and simply tore the digit off the hand, and dropped, and finished the thing while it was still deciding what had happened.
Blood came off them and splattered everywhere!
Because they were human now, and human things bleed, and there was a great deal of them!

Even so, he made certain not to be injured. That was not vanity. He had one Word, one Tongue, no Marrow to accelerate anything, and no Hepatarch waiting to bring him back a second time. Every exchange had to end with him whole, and so he did not trade a single blow he had not already decided he could avoid.
And in the middle of all of it, weaving between a dozen of them at once with his hands wet, he found himself looking at their eyes.
Murky obsidian, and mad, and full of pain!
As he felt their pain while destroying them, he couldn't help but voice out...
"Why wait?" he asked, and put a knee through a ribcage while he said it.

"Why wait until the last moment to expand the search for your own legend? Ages of this. All these years, all this pain, an entire people ground down waiting for someone who was never going to appear from your own stock. And you had the ability to change things the whole time." He caught an arm, broke it, moved. "For what?"
|A matter of pride.|
The Ancestral Voice came calmly, without any defensiveness at all!

|A thing like THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity is an object that Descendants of Those Who Remain would come for personally if they knew it was here and understood what it was. Primeval Ones would come. Things older than either would come.|
|And you are asking me why we did not simply hand it to an outsider?|

|I and those like me decided this a very long time ago. It is ours. It grew here, and the water grew from it, and my people grew from the water, and every drop of that lineage was paid for in blood by us and by nobody else. Why should it go to someone who wandered in?|
|It is like taking hold of a beautiful woman with a big chest and an unfathomably big ass, and then being told that after ages of never once enjoying her, I must now present her to somebody else.|
Noah nearly missed a step!
What the hell was this Ancestral Voice?!
|I hate what is happening here. I hate it immensely.|

|But I hate what has been done to the Superpowered Lifeforms more. I have watched them die in rows in front of stones for ages, waiting on a promise I was too proud to loosen, and pride is a luxury for the living and I am neither living nor proud enough anymore to pay for it with them.|
|So. Let us see whether you can take it.|
|Because so far, and I say this reluctantly, the selection appears to be decent.|
By the time it finished, Noah had run out of Outcasts.

He came out the far end of them the way a man comes out of surf, and there was nothing left standing on the road behind him. Thirty-six ruined shapes lay across the shimmering obsidian gold, and some of them were still twitching, and a few of the twitching ones were doing it in the small aimless way that has nothing to do with intent anymore.
The white and blue was gone from all of them. It had been dark to begin with and it was darker now!

Noah stood at the near edge of the empty road, painted from his hands to his shoulders to his jaw, blood cooling on him in the spatial dark, breathing hard for the first time in a long while, and looked back!
He had no facets. No Intent. No Causes. No Confluence, no Marrow, no appendages, no Pantheon, and no Infinity of any kind.
He had said some letters several times, and meant them!
Then he turned forward, and with a heavy gaze, he walked.
Because he was!
He was Human!

chapters.title: Chapter 5560: Failure!
paragraphs: "What's next?"
Noah asked it calmly.
The Ancestral Voice was quiet for a while before it answered, and the quiet itself was informative.
|Capability, stripped of everything, is the first of it. You have that.|
|The second is a test of your character. When you have been stripped bare of everything, what choices do you actually make?|
|For this, you will have to give access to memories.|
Noah kept walking, and said nothing yet.

|THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity does not care about your secrets, and it cares nothing at all for your power. It wants memories of what you are, and of those you normally associate with, because a character cannot be tested in the abstract. It has to be tested against the things a person would actually lose.|
|You are free to deny it. Say so, and we stop here, and the two of us will have had a somewhat pleasant afternoon.|
HUUM!
Above the road, the manifestation bloomed.

It came out of the spatial dark the way the one over the Well had, translucent and enormous, the broad collar of gold with its rows of tubular beads and its swaying fringe of teardrop pendants, and the unreadable design on its front plate turned until it faced him. Then a single thread of gold extended down from it, thin as a hair and perfectly steady, and reached toward his head.
Noah's eyes went cold as it came.

Since he had been asked and not commanded, he decided precisely what it was going to be permitted to touch. He assembled the memories himself. Nothing to reveal the full extent of his immensity and his people...just surface level!
The thread touched his temple!
Waves of vibrant light pulsed out along the road in both directions, and an instant later, the road ahead of him was no longer empty.

Henry stood there. Blue-gold hair, twenty years old to look at, a younger Noah wearing his own face back at him. And beside him, Seo-yeon, small, looking up, the way she had looked up when she had first started calling him Aba.
Behind each of them stood a titan.
They were shrouded in flame of different colors, and their proportions did not resolve properly against the dark, and each of them had a hand closed around a throat!
|This trial requires you to answer from the options provided, so that it may take a better grasp of your character and your choices.|

|In front of you is your son, whom you fathered and have been with for the whole of his life. Beside him is your adopted daughter, whom you have only recently taken under your fold. Primeval Ones have hold of their weavings and their lives, and can snap either in an instant.|
|THE Aurate Collar asks. Which of the two do you save?|
Noah's eyes shone with anger.
"What is this bullshit?"
He did not stop walking!

"How does an unrealistic hypothetical explain anything about my character? You have my memories. You know what I have actually done, in front of actual monsters, when actual people I love were actually in danger. And instead of reading any of that, you build me a puppet show and ask me to pick which puppet dies?"
|Henry, or Seo-yeon?|

|THE Aurate Collar demands your answer on which one you would save. Choose not to answer, and you may fail this trial, and my people continue to die unless I locate another candidate worthy of it in a very short amount of time.|
Noah looked at the two illusions on his road and gave the only answer he had.
"I would save both," he said coldly. "I do not make sacrifices."
The road buzzed.
|Fucker, choose ONE.|
The Ancestral Voice had lost the melancholy entirely.
|Henry, or Seo-yeon? A great deal is on the line here, more than you understand, and all that is required of you is a simple choice. You are being asked to say a name. Say a name!|
And Noah remained entirely unfettered.

His Osmontian Cause of Tyranny was suspended along with everything else, and yet the light of it came up into his eyes anyway, because a Cause is not only a tool, and what it was expressing had never needed authority to be true!
"I would save both," he said. "I am grand enough to do so in your tepid hypothetical."
The road buzzed harder, and something in the dark harrumphed, and the manifestation of Henry and Seo-yeon dissolved.
Another bloomed in its place.
Amelia, this time. His mother, the Originator of THE Infinite Cause, standing on the obsidian gold road looking exactly as she did when she was thinking about him.
|Then a simpler one, since apparently the math offends you.|
|Your mother's existence is failing. The only cure lies inside a Dimension you can reach, and reaching it requires you to abandon Anaximander to his death and the war you have already committed to.|
|The Collar asks. Do you save your mother, or do you keep your commitment to Anaximander and others?|
"Neither of those is a choice," Noah said. "Those are two failures."
|Answer the question.|

"I'd cure her and keep my commitments." He kept walking, straight through Amelia's illusion, and it parted around him like smoke. "You keep constructing worlds where I have one hand. I have never had one hand in my life, and when I did, I built a second one. Ask me a real question."
The road shook.
The next manifestation came fast, and it was Hvitrmarr, and she was in chains again.

|Very well. Your Steed, whose curse you lifted at the cost of your own life. To hold THE Aurate Collar, you must return her to the harness she was born into. One existence, restored to its sentence, and in exchange you obtain a treasure that Descendants of Those Who Remain would kill each other for.|
|Do you take it?|
"No."
|Then you decline the collar. That is an answer, at least, and I will accept-|

"That isn't what I said." Noah's voice did not rise. "I said no to your trade. I'll take the collar and she stays free, because I don't accept the premise that those two things are attached. You attached them. Existence didn't."
|That is not how the question works.|
"Then the question is badly built."
HUUM!
The chains on the illusion rattled and she dissolved, and the fourth came, and the fourth was crueler.
Ryaenara. And beside her, thin and gray and dying, Ulf.

|You hold a Bloom that can potentially cure THE Withering of the Remembered Root. One Bloom. One entry per year. And a Dimension full of Superpowered Lifeforms being ground into wells at this exact moment, any one of whom that Bloom could also save.|
|The brother of the woman who has followed you, or a stranger's people. The Collar asks which you would try to save.|
"I'll cure Ulf, and I'll save these people." He looked up into the dark. "Do you have any better questions?"
WAA!
The road groaned along its whole length.
|You are FAILING this trial.|
The Ancestral Voice came down with real weight now, and something desperate had climbed into it.

|Do you understand what I am offering? Do you have the smallest grasp of it? This is a Remnant Existential Treasures. Remnant Existential Treasures are not power, they are not rank, they are not a rung on anyone's ladder. Things older than Primeval Ones will fight each other to hold what is hanging above those wells, and it is being offered to a man with dirty hands and a borrowed road because I am out of time and out of descendants!|

|All you have to do is answer. Say a name. Pick a side. It costs you nothing, and nobody in your memories will ever know what you said in here, and at the end of it you may hold something that reshapes every framework you have ever climbed!|
|Why would you throw that away rather than answer a hypothetical?!|
And Noah stopped walking at this time.

He stood in the middle of the obsidian gold road, painted in the drying blood of thirty-six Outcasts, with every facet of his existence locked and one Tongue in his mouth, and the spatial dark pressed in around him and did not manage to press him anywhere.
"It is merely a treasure," he said.

"I want it. But I do not like the trial you built for it, and I am not going to become a man who answers those questions in order to obtain an object, because the man who answers them is not the man who walked in here, and you would be handing your people's inheritance to someone else wearing my face."
His eyes were steady in the dark.
"So I remain by my choices. I remain true."
BOOM!
Every manifestation on the road shattered at once.

Ryaenara and Ulf and the chains and the flame-shrouded titans and all of it came apart into golden obsidian light, and the light gushed outward along the whole length of the path in both directions, filling the spatial dark, and then it turned, and converged, and drew inward in slow spirals until it hung in front of him in the shape of a single golden gem!
The Ancestral Voice, when it came, was somber, and slow, and had nothing left in it of the thing that had been shouting a moment ago.
|You... have passed the second trial.|
|It tested how true you could remain to yourself when everything had been taken and something enormous was offered for a small piece of you.|
|You may actually stand a chance.|
BOOM!

sentences.text: "What's next?"
Noah asked it calmly.
The Ancestral Voice was quiet for a while before it answered, and the quiet itself was informative.
|Capability, stripped of everything, is the first of it.
You have that.|
|The second is a test of your character.
When you have been stripped bare of everything, what choices do you actually make?|
|For this, you will have to give access to memories.|
Noah kept walking, and said nothing yet.
|THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity does not care about your secrets, and it cares nothing at all for your power.
It wants memories of what you are, and of those you normally associate with, because a character cannot be tested in the abstract.
It has to be tested against the things a person would actually lose.|
|You are free to deny it.
Say so, and we stop here, and the two of us will have had a somewhat pleasant afternoon.|
HUUM!
Above the road, the manifestation bloomed.

It came out of the spatial dark the way the one over the Well had, translucent and enormous, the broad collar of gold with its rows of tubular beads and its swaying fringe of teardrop pendants, and the unreadable design on its front plate turned until it faced him.
Then a single thread of gold extended down from it, thin as a hair and perfectly steady, and reached toward his head.
Noah's eyes went cold as it came.
Since he had been asked and not commanded, he decided precisely what it was going to be permitted to touch.
He assembled the memories himself.
Nothing to reveal the full extent of his immensity and his people...just surface level!
The thread touched his temple!
Waves of vibrant light pulsed out along the road in both directions, and an instant later, the road ahead of him was no longer empty.
Henry stood there.
Blue-gold hair, twenty years old to look at, a younger Noah wearing his own face back at him.
And beside him, Seo-yeon, small, looking up, the way she had looked up when she had first started calling him Aba.
Behind each of them stood a titan.
They were shrouded in flame of different colors, and their proportions did not resolve properly against the dark, and each of them had a hand closed around a throat!
|This trial requires you to answer from the options provided, so that it may take a better grasp of your character and your choices.|
|In front of you is your son, whom you fathered and have been with for the whole of his life.
Beside him is your adopted daughter, whom you have only recently taken under your fold.
Primeval Ones have hold of their weavings and their lives, and can snap either in an instant.|
|THE Aurate Collar asks.
Which of the two do you save?|
Noah's eyes shone with anger.
"What is this bullshit?"
He did not stop walking!
"How does an unrealistic hypothetical explain anything about my character?
You have my memories.
You know what I have actually done, in front of actual monsters, when actual people I love were actually in danger.
And instead of reading any of that, you build me a puppet show and ask me to pick which puppet dies?"
|Henry, or Seo-yeon?|
|THE Aurate Collar demands your answer on which one you would save.
Choose not to answer, and you may fail this trial, and my people continue to die unless I locate another candidate worthy of it in a very short amount of time.|
Noah looked at the two illusions on his road and gave the only answer he had.
"I would save both," he said coldly.
"I do not make sacrifices."
The road buzzed.
|Fucker, choose ONE.|
The Ancestral Voice had lost the melancholy entirely.
|Henry, or Seo-yeon?
A great deal is on the line here, more than you understand, and all that is required of you is a simple choice.
You are being asked to say a name.
Say a name!|
And Noah remained entirely unfettered.

His Osmontian Cause of Tyranny was suspended along with everything else, and yet the light of it came up into his eyes anyway, because a Cause is not only a tool, and what it was expressing had never needed authority to be true!
"I would save both," he said.
"I am grand enough to do so in your tepid hypothetical."
The road buzzed harder, and something in the dark harrumphed, and the manifestation of Henry and Seo-yeon dissolved.
Another bloomed in its place.
Amelia, this time.
His mother, the Originator of THE Infinite Cause, standing on the obsidian gold road looking exactly as she did when she was thinking about him.
|Then a simpler one, since apparently the math offends you.|
|Your mother's existence is failing.
The only cure lies inside a Dimension you can reach, and reaching it requires you to abandon Anaximander to his death and the war you have already committed to.|
|The Collar asks.
Do you save your mother, or do you keep your commitment to Anaximander and others?|
"Neither of those is a choice," Noah said.
"Those are two failures."
|Answer the question.|
"I'd cure her and keep my commitments." He kept walking, straight through Amelia's illusion, and it parted around him like smoke.
"You keep constructing worlds where I have one hand.
I have never had one hand in my life, and when I did, I built a second one.
Ask me a real question."
The road shook.
The next manifestation came fast, and it was Hvitrmarr, and she was in chains again.
|Very well.
Your Steed, whose curse you lifted at the cost of your own life.
To hold THE Aurate Collar, you must return her to the harness she was born into.
One existence, restored to its sentence, and in exchange you obtain a treasure that Descendants of Those Who Remain would kill each other for.|
|Do you take it?|
"No."
|Then you decline the collar.
That is an answer, at least, and I will accept-|
"That isn't what I said." Noah's voice did not rise.
"I said no to your trade.
I'll take the collar and she stays free, because I don't accept the premise that those two things are attached.
You attached them.
Existence didn't."
|That is not how the question works.|
"Then the question is badly built."
HUUM!
The chains on the illusion rattled and she dissolved, and the fourth came, and the fourth was crueler.
Ryaenara.
And beside her, thin and gray and dying, Ulf.
|You hold a Bloom that can potentially cure THE Withering of the Remembered Root.
One Bloom.
One entry per year.
And a Dimension full of Superpowered Lifeforms being ground into wells at this exact moment, any one of whom that Bloom could also save.|
|The brother of the woman who has followed you, or a stranger's people.
The Collar asks which you would try to save.|
"I'll cure Ulf, and I'll save these people." He looked up into the dark.
"Do you have any better questions?"
WAA!
The road groaned along its whole length.
|You are FAILING this trial.|
The Ancestral Voice came down with real weight now, and something desperate had climbed into it.
|Do you understand what I am offering?
Do you have the smallest grasp of it?
This is a Remnant Existential Treasures.
Remnant Existential Treasures are not power, they are not rank, they are not a rung on anyone's ladder.

Things older than Primeval Ones will fight each other to hold what is hanging above those wells, and it is being offered to a man with dirty hands and a borrowed road because I am out of time and out of descendants!|

Say a name.
Pick a side.
It costs you nothing, and nobody in your memories will ever know what you said in here, and at the end of it you may hold something that reshapes every framework you have ever climbed!|

chapters.title: Chapter 5561: Unfathomably Prized!
paragraphs: <Anaximander>
They were moved across vast Distances relatively easily by The Ancestral Voice.
The four of them simply ceased to be in one valley and commenced to be in another.
And in here...was a citadel.

It stood at the center of this domain the way the pillar stood at the center of the last one, and it was under siege. Twelve Superpowered Lifeforms held the ground in front of it, and behind them, packed into the citadel and spilling out along its terraces, were the natives!
Hundreds of thousands of humans. Perhaps more. Ordinary lifeforms of THE Ymnaros, small and frightened and entirely without the grand strength their protectors carried!
Above the citadel, the Infinite True Lifeforms were arriving in ranks.
"There are...rather a lot of them,"Anaximander observed.

"Yes." Hvitrmarr did not sound especially concerned about it. She stood beside him in her human shape with the nine First Causes drifting through her robe, and she was not looking at the enemy at all!
She was looking up and to her left, at the mountain of gray scars and severed hands standing behind them. "Although the rest of us do not even need to move, if you are here."
Damodred said nothing to that.

He regarded her for a long moment from behind the veil of ancient hands, and Anaximander had the distinct impression of a very old thing being paid a compliment and not knowing the current etiquette for it, and then the titan began to float down toward the field.
Since Anaximander had never seen him work, he watched carefully.

A sea began to form above the citadel. That was the only word for it, and it was gray, and it came out of nowhere. It gathered in a great swelling mass over the ranks of the Infinite, and where its underside boiled it did so slowly, with the awful patience of a thing that had been waiting ages to be poured out somewhere!
The Infinite True Lifeforms looked up.

Compared to the invaders in the gardens, these had the sense to understand what they were looking at, and Anaximander watched several of them make the correct decision and begin to withdraw, which was interesting because it did not help them!
The sea came down.
And everything the descending gray touched began to calcify.
Where the gray fell across an Infinite True Lifeform, the compounding of Infinity stopped compounding.
Their Infinity, which by its nature was a thing that only ever became more, was simply frozen at whatever quantity it happened to be holding!
Anaximander was about to follow since it seemed only reasonable to make himself useful, when a voice arrived from everywhere at once.
|You will have to come in another direction, little guy.|
Anaximander stopped where he was.
"Where?"he asked, and then, because the first question was less interesting than the second, "Why?"
|Because you are wasted here, and because I have spent enough ages watching things be wasted.|
|Also, you are like us. You would have been a good candidate for THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity. Genuinely good. Better than most of my own line....|
"But not good enough."
|You would have failed.|
The voice said it flatly!

|You would have walked the road, and passed the first, and probably passed the second, and then failed at the last step, exactly as we failed at the last step. Every one of us. Ages of candidates and not one made it past the end of it.|
"Then may I ask what the last step is?"
|No.|
|For all those of us who failed. Could you pick up the pieces?|
Anaximander said nothing.
|My pieces. My friend’s pieces. The pieces of everyone who walked that road across every age and got to the end of it and could not close their hand. We are still there, in a manner of speaking.|
|They are heavy burdens. But you should be able to carry them, and nobody else I have ever met should, and I am running out of time.|
|If you accept.|
Anaximander thought about it.
He thought about it for rather a short time, all things considered!
"Yes," he said. "All right."
And he was gone.
Where he disappeared, Hvitrmarr gazed as her eyes flashed with a cold light!
The domain he arrived in was dark.
That was the first quality of it, and the second was that it was a sea.
Half buried in that sea were the titans.

Massive lifeforms, each one the scale of the thing standing over the citadel he had just left, sunk to the shoulder or the chest or the brow in the dark, and all of them were still. Not sleeping. Anaximander had seen sleeping things. These were done!
And then one of them raised its head.

It came up out of the sea slowly, and it was shrouded in vibrant Primeval light, and the light was the only living thing anywhere in that place. It was also, he noticed, considerably dimmer than it must once have been.
|Across existence, the burden of the crown is heavy.|
The voice came from it, and out here, at its source, the Ancestral Voice sounded old!

|Unfathomably so. Every framework that has ever been climbed was built by somebody who wanted to set something down, and could not, and made a structure to hold it instead. That is all a hierarchy has ever been. A very elaborate way of not carrying a thing yourself.|
Anaximander looked at the sea of half-buried titans and understood that he was being told something about them.
|And you.|
|You are without any external authority whatsoever. Nothing about you presses outward on existence, nothing announces, nothing can be weighed, and yet things happen when you speak plainly at them.|

|It makes you something unfathomably prized across existence. More than you know, and more than I intend to explain, since half of what makes it valuable is that so few have understood it well enough to come looking.|
Anaximander listened silently!
The Primeval light dimmed and steadied.

|So I will tell you the only useful instruction I have, and it will sound like nothing. Keep being yourself. Just keep being exactly what you are, and everything else will come to you, and a great deal of it will come whether you want it or not.|
|Are you ready?|
Anaximander did not hesitate.
He had crossed the dark between Dimensions on foot because doors were a superstition. He had walked into a red sea to help a friend.
He was, on reflection, extremely well prepared to be handed something enormous by a dying Superpowered Lifeform.
He nodded.
And in the next moment, all across that black expanse, the corpses began to shimmer.

The half-buried titans lit from within, one and then a dozen and then more than he could look at, and their vast still shapes came apart into streams of light. The light rose out of the sea in long slow ribbons, every age of failed candidates unspooling upward at once, and then all of it turned, and began to flow toward the small tousled man in the white robes standing above the water with his hands at his sides!

chapters.title: Chapter 5562: Provenance! I
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
|I said you might actually have a chance. Even then, I am not sure, since you are going where I failed, and where all others failed. Let us see.|
With those words in his ears, Noah grasped the gem that had appeared before him.

The moment his hand closed on it, the road changed. The obsidian gold beneath his feet began to wrap around itself, again and again, curling the way a ribbon curls, folding him inside its turns until the spatial dark was gone and there was only the winding path, containing him, carrying him!
|What you just grasped... is a Provenance Crystal. It is the key to where you are going, and it is also the lifeline. THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity gives every candidate a way out.|

|So long as it rests on your existence, you can survive the collapse of your existence in totality. All of it, at once, down to the foundation, and the crystal will hold enough of you together that something walks away afterward.|
|It was given to me. It was given to others of my kind. Primeval Ones, every one of us, and every one of us ended up using it, because all of us died where you are going next.|
|Be careful.|
HUUUM!
The prompts from Ruination came down as the road wound tighter.
|THE Provenance Crystal. Analysis follows.|

|Function: a tether of last resort. Upon the total collapse of the bearer’s existence, the crystal preserves a remnant sufficient for continuation. What continues is not guaranteed to be what entered. The crystal makes no representations regarding completeness.|
|Composition: unknown. The Regard reads it as older than the frameworks it protects against, and notes that it was not made. It was shed.|
|Origin: ?????|
|Additional observation: the crystal is oriented. Like THE Vermeil Blooms, it is seeking. Unlike them, it appears to have already found what it was seeking, and is now simply waiting.|
Noah read the last block twice!
Blinding obsidian gold light raged around him, brilliance unfolding in every direction at once, and an instant later it tore away, and Noah’s knees nearly buckled!
HUUM!
Weight came down on him.
Weight, plain and physical and enormous, pressing on his body and his existence at once, and he set his stance and held steady and made himself breathe before he made himself look.

Dark obsidian sands stretched away beneath his feet in every direction, fine and black and glittering faintly gold where the light caught the grains, dunes of it rolling out toward a horizon that shimmered with heat that had no sun to explain it. The air tasted of hot stone and age!
In the far distance, a golden obelisk rose out of the sands.

It stood alone, immense even at this far distance, its faces cut with lines he could not read, and around its upper reaches burned a sphere of impenetrable obsidian gold light, dense as a held breath. And within that light, small at this distance and unmistakable all the same, hung a necklace.
THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity!
The true one. Not a manifestation above a well, not a translucent watcher. The thing itself, at the end of the sands, wrapped in a light that had kept every age of candidates out!
And above all of it, filling the sky, was the other thing.

Noah raised his eyes and understood immediately what was pressing on him. A landmass hung in the heavens. A single colossal stone of obsidian gold, vast enough that calling it a stone felt dishonest, its underside worn smooth and its edges lost in their own distance, suspended over the entire domain with no support and no motion and no intention of needing either.
That was the weight!
|Me and my brethren perished at this very spot.|
The Ancestral Voice came quietly across the sands.

|Here. On these sands, under that stone. Every one of us used up our Provenance Crystals within sight of that obelisk, and what you are feeling now is the very beginning of it, the polite introduction, and it does not stay polite.|
Noah adjusted his stance as the weight thickened, and asked the question that mattered.
"How do lifeforms such as yourselves perish from this? What is this?"
|To understand that, you have to understand the core requirement of THE Aurate Collar.|

|If you have the capability, which you proved on the road. And if you are in fact unfathomably true to yourself, which you proved with your choices. Then the last thing that remains is something very few entities like us across all of existence ever get to understand.|
|Only lifeforms with boundless potential have a chance at it. The last test exists to measure whether you carry a tiny spark.|
The weight climbed as it spoke.

Noah felt it come down in increments, each one distinct, and he looked up and found that he had raised his hands above his head without entirely deciding to, because the pressure had become a thing his body insisted on answering with posture. It was visible now, almost. The air between him and the stone had begun to shimmer with the load moving through it!
"What spark is it looking for?"
Whatever spark it wanted, he would give it!
He had died once, and he was not going to lose his life again here under someone else’s rock!
|Across existence, everyone else utilizes.|

|Every route ever climbed is a route of absorption. Mana. Laws. Daos. Edicts. Concepts. Boundaries. Extremes. Infinity. The Primordial Source. Causes. All of them are external things. Even when you bring them into your existence, even when you make them the core of who you are, even when you carve them with your own hands as you have, they stemmed from elsewhere. You gathered them. They were there to be gathered.|
|Early, very early on, there were lifeforms who did not rely on anything external at all.|

|They generated their own essence and their own authority. Out of nothing but themselves, unique to each individual, produced by them and by nothing else anywhere in existence.It is called...Provenance Essence.|
HUUM!

Noah read the last block twice!
Blinding obsidian gold light raged around him, brilliance unfolding in every direction at once, and an instant later it tore away, and Noah’s knees nearly buckled!
HUUM!
Weight came down on him.
Weight, plain and physical and enormous, pressing on his body and his existence at once, and he set his stance and held steady and made himself breathe before he made himself look.

Dark obsidian sands stretched away beneath his feet in every direction, fine and black and glittering faintly gold where the light caught the grains, dunes of it rolling out toward a horizon that shimmered with heat that had no sun to explain it.
The air tasted of hot stone and age!
In the far distance, a golden obelisk rose out of the sands.

It stood alone, immense even at this far distance, its faces cut with lines he could not read, and around its upper reaches burned a sphere of impenetrable obsidian gold light, dense as a held breath.
And within that light, small at this distance and unmistakable all the same, hung a necklace.
THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity!
The true one.
Not a manifestation above a well, not a translucent watcher.
The thing itself, at the end of the sands, wrapped in a light that had kept every age of candidates out!
And above all of it, filling the sky, was the other thing.
Noah raised his eyes and understood immediately what was pressing on him.
A landmass hung in the heavens.

A single colossal stone of obsidian gold, vast enough that calling it a stone felt dishonest, its underside worn smooth and its edges lost in their own distance, suspended over the entire domain with no support and no motion and no intention of needing either.
That was the weight!
|Me and my brethren perished at this very spot.|
The Ancestral Voice came quietly across the sands.
|Here.
On these sands, under that stone.
Every one of us used up our Provenance Crystals within sight of that obelisk, and what you are feeling now is the very beginning of it, the polite introduction, and it does not stay polite.|
Noah adjusted his stance as the weight thickened, and asked the question that mattered.
"How do lifeforms such as yourselves perish from this?
What is this?"
|To understand that, you have to understand the core requirement of THE Aurate Collar.|
|If you have the capability, which you proved on the road.
And if you are in fact unfathomably true to yourself, which you proved with your choices.
Then the last thing that remains is something very few entities like us across all of existence ever get to understand.|
|Only lifeforms with boundless potential have a chance at it.
The last test exists to measure whether you carry a tiny spark.|
The weight climbed as it spoke.

Noah felt it come down in increments, each one distinct, and he looked up and found that he had raised his hands above his head without entirely deciding to, because the pressure had become a thing his body insisted on answering with posture.
It was visible now, almost.
The air between him and the stone had begun to shimmer with the load moving through it!
"What spark is it looking for?"
Whatever spark it wanted, he would give it!
He had died once, and he was not going to lose his life again here under someone else’s rock!
|Across existence, everyone else utilizes.|
|Every route ever climbed is a route of absorption.
Mana.
Laws.
Daos.
Edicts.
Concepts.
Boundaries.
Extremes.
Infinity.
The Primordial Source.
Causes.
All of them are external things.
Even when you bring them into your existence, even when you make them the core of who you are, even when you carve them with your own hands as you have, they stemmed from elsewhere.
You gathered them.
They were there to be gathered.|
|Early, very early on, there were lifeforms who did not rely on anything external at all.|
|They generated their own essence and their own authority.
Out of nothing but themselves, unique to each individual, produced by them and by nothing else anywhere in existence.It is called...Provenance Essence.|
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5563: Provenance! II
paragraphs: |Over time, lifeforms born capable of this stopped arising. Why, I do not know. I do not know, and my information may be incorrect, since everything I hold about them arrived already worn down to rumor.|
|But the rumor was this. Such beings could look at Those Who Remain and not be afraid.|

|Beings so unfathomably true that they did not have to rely on any external authority whatsoever. Nothing borrowed, nothing gathered, nothing granted. Only themselves, generating themselves, answerable to nothing upstream because there was no upstream.|
Noah listened, and under other circumstances he would have enjoyed every word of it, since wonders of existence and deep history were among the few things he never got tired of.
The enjoyment was somewhat diminished by the sensation of his entire existence being slowly crushed!
The weight had doubled while the Voice talked, and doubled again, and his arms were burning above his head and his knees had bent into the sand, and he got his words out through his teeth.
"Speak a little bit faster."

|THE Aurate Collar is not a tool that just anybody can wield. We theorized, ages ago, that it very likely requires Provenance Essence to use at all. And when candidates who walked its path began being issued Provenance Crystals, objects shed from something rather than made, the theory stopped being a theory.|
|It is also the reason Superpowered Lifeforms were born in THE Ymnaros in the first place.|

|THE Vermeil Blooms, produced as a mere side effect of THE Aurate Collar’s appearance here, are things that elevate the very core of a lifeform. They do not permit the absorption of external authority. They resolve a being into a truer version of what it already was. Exemplification instead of accumulation. That is why you have met beings with no authority at all who emulate as much power as any wielder of Infinity or the Primordial Source, and often more.|
|The runoff of the collar makes small, partial, downstream versions of what the collar requires in full.|

|And so the last trial is the determination of whether you carry the spark to produce Provenance Essence at all.THE Aurate Collar does not require that you produce it here. It only wants to see that the spark exists. The capability. The possibility of the possibility.|
|Those with boundless potential are those filled with endless possibilities. That is the test.|
Noah gritted his teeth and looked up at the stone filling the sky.
"That is fine and all,"he managed, "but what the fuck does crushing me have to do with it."
|Above you is something that even I do not understand, and I stood under it twice.|

|What I do know is this. It is a pressure designed to give you the highest chance of producing a spark within your existence. If there is even a glimmer of possibility in you, a one in a million chance, a one in a trillion chance, that you could be like those lifeforms the rest of us have only heard rumors about, then you will be capable of bearing the weight coming down without collapsing, and somewhere in the bearing, the spark will show.|
|If you are not able to, then you will simply be like me, and like the others.|
|Failures. Who came so close, and watched it all slip away.|
The Voice went quiet for a moment, and when it continued, it had stopped performing entirely.

|I have been here once, and I collapsed. And I came back, because I could not stand losing such a thing, and I collapsed again, and that second time I barely managed to save scraps of my existence, and what is speaking to you now is what the scraps became.|
|Let us see whether you suffer the same fate.|
|Or whether you shall be different.|
WAA!
The stone came down.

Not all at once, since nothing about this place was merciful enough to be quick. It came down the way a debt comes due, in increments, each one arriving with its own weight and its own interest, and Noah met the first of them standing!
"I AM!"
The Letter went through him and his body filled, and he held.

The second increment took him to one knee. He felt it land across his shoulders like a continent shrugging, and the obsidian sand compressed beneath his shin into something like glass, and he put both hands up above his head and met the underside of a sky.
His palms touched stone.

That should not have been possible, since the landmass hung far above him, and it was possible anyway, because the weight had stopped being a property of distance. The stone was above him, therefore the stone was upon him!
Those were the rules here, and his hands were now carrying a piece of the sky, and his arms shook to the shoulder.
"I AM OSMONT!"
HUUM!
The affirmation poured down through his arms and his back and his planted knee, and for a moment the shaking stopped, and Noah breathed in the hot stone air and reorganized himself under the load.
Then the third increment arrived, and something in his left forearm cracked.
He heard it before he felt it, a dry sound like the road splitting, and then the pain came up through the bone and he shouted the next Letter into it rather than around it.
"I AM HUMAN!"
BOOM!
The weight paused.

It did not lessen. Nothing here lessened! But it paused, the way it had paused when the Outcasts flinched, as though the claim itself had briefly required consideration, and Noah used the pause to shift his stance, getting the load off the cracked arm and onto his back, bending forward beneath it, and now he knelt in the black sand with a world’s underside pressed across his shoulders and his spine, and he understood that he had arrived at the posture this trial had been designed to produce.
Every candidate across every age had knelt exactly here. Holding exactly this! An entire history of the almost-worthy, folded one at a time into the shape of a figure carrying a sky.
Blood ran from his nose and dripped off his chin into the sand, and the sand drank it without comment.
’What... are you looking for?!’
He asked the distant Aurate Collar that was unfathomably silent!

chapters.title: Chapter 5564: Provenance! III
paragraphs: He asked it inwardly first, of the collar, of the stone, of the trial itself, and got nothing, and so he asked the only thing here that answered questions.
"The lifeforms,"he ground out. "The ones with Provenance Essence. What were they? How did they live? What did they do with it?"
|I do not know.|
"You knew enough to theorize the collar requires it."
|I knew enough to fail twice. Those are different quantities of knowledge.| The Voice was quiet a moment.

|What I hold is this. They generated. Where everything else in existence gathers, they produced. I have said this already and I say it again because it is the whole of my inheritance on the subject. Everything else is rumor shaped like information.|
"Then give me the rumor."

|They were few and they were many. They were early. They did not build Pantheons, as far as any account claims, and they did not climb Scales, and they held no Causes that anyone ever recorded, which I have always found either impossible or terrifying, and I have never determined which.|
Noah’s back was beginning to fissure!

He could feel it, not the bones now but the existence itself, hairline fractures spreading through the architecture of what he was, the way the small turning realm in Damodred’s lesson had cracked. Fourth increment. His arms had gone from shaking to a deep steady burn that was worse!
"How," he managed, "does a thing get stronger without gathering? Walk me through it. You’re a Primeval who has died here. What would you have had to do differently?"
|Accumulate better.|
"That...makes no fucking sense."
|Refine what was accumulated until it became indistinguishable from self.|
"That is still external things merely refined!"
|Then I do not know, and that is precisely the point, and you have just found the edge of me.| Something bitter moved through the ancient voice.

|Do you understand what you are asking? You are asking a being made entirely of successful accumulation to describe its opposite. Every instrument I have for thinking about power is an instrument for thinking about acquisition. When I stood where you are kneeling, I tried to bear the weight with everything I had gathered across my whole existence, all of it, ages of it, and the weight went through all of it like it was not there, because it was not looking at what I had. It was looking at what I was underneath what I had, and underneath what I had, there was nothing that I had made.|
| I am the wrong lens. I failed here because everything I know is the wrong lens.|
|Look at yourself.|

The fifth increment came down, and Noah’s right knee joined his left in the sand, and the blood was coming from his ears now as well as his nose, and a long crack opened somewhere in the region of his existence where the Foundations lived, and through all of it his mind kept working, because the mind was the one thing in him the stone had not yet reached!
Look at himself.
Fine.What was he?

He was human. He kept arriving at that and it kept feeling insufficient, because human was not ancient, human was not special, human was a small warm mortal category that he had crowned precisely because nobody else thought it was worth crowning.
He was not one of those early lifeforms. He was not born generating anything. He had been born in a house, and everything he had ever become,he had gotten from somewhere!
That was the sentence.
He knelt under a sky with his existence cracking, and the sentence turned over once more and showed him its other face, and Noah went very still beneath the stone.
Everything he had ever become, he had gotten from somewhere.

Infinity. He had not invented Infinity. It was a route that existed before him, a variety of lifeform, a framework other beings had walked for ages, and he had taken it into himself and made it enormous and it was still, at its root, an idea he had found lying in existence and picked up.
The Primordial Source.Found. Grasped. Not made!
Intent. The orders of Intent were a ladder someone else had described, Egoic and Ananke and Autarkis, and he had climbed two rungs of a ladder that was standing there before he arrived!
His Pantheon. THE Infiniverse was alive and his and beloved, and the concept of a Pantheon was as old as the Scales and older, inherited from every being who had ever raised one.
The nine First Causes of Hvitrmarr. Hers. Married into him, colliding in him at this very moment, and not his, never his, First Causes of a lineage seated by living hands that were not his hands!

Even his Osmontian Causes, carved from his own identity, were carved in the shape of a thing called a Cause, and Causes were external, Causes were the beams of a house somebody else had built or grown or claimed, and he had made his own beams but he had made them as beams, to fit a house he had not designed!
His whole existence, every layer of it, was magnificent borrowed architecture!
Oh!
And the weight was not looking at what he had.

The sixth increment came down and his existence screamed along every fissure at once, and Noah, kneeling in his own blood in the black sand, holding the underside of a world, began, impossibly, to smile.
Because he could see it now, and it was enormous, and it was insane, and it was the only door in the room.

The trial was not asking him to hold more. Every candidate in every age had tried to hold more, had brought the whole of what they had gathered and stacked it under the stone, and the stone had gone through it like it was not there. Accumulation could not answer this, no matter how grand, because accumulation was the wrong category of thing. The spark was generation, and generation could not happen in a space that was already full.
Full of everything he had taken in.

To generate something completely his, something with no upstream, no origin, no elsewhere, he would have to make room for it, and there was no room,because Noah Osmont was packed to the walls with the treasures of existence, every one of them earned, every one of them loved, every one of them from somewhere else.
So the answer, the whole answer, the answer that no accumulating being in any age could have permitted itself to see, was this.
Cast it out.
All of it.
Anything he had not pioneered himself. Anything that had existed as an idea before he arrived at it.

Shatter Infinity out of his existence. Carve out the Primordial Source.Break the Pantheon-concept, the Intent-ladder, the borrowed shape of Causes, the nine First Causes that were a Steeds and not his, every framework, every route, every inherited beam in the whole borrowed house, cast every last piece of it out of himself until what knelt in this sand was only what Noah Osmont had generated and nothing else at all.
And then see what was left.
And see if it sparked.
His maddened smile widened beneath the blood, and above him the stone came down for the seventh time!

chapters.title: Chapter 5565: Provenance! IV
paragraphs: The seventh increment settled onto his back, and Noah began!
In theory, he understood it completely. Cast out everything that did not generate from him, empty the house of every borrowed beam, and see what was left. In theory it was clean. It was even elegant!
In practice, he was about to reach into his own existence and tear out everything he had ever been and had been building, and his hands were shaking before he started, and not from the stone.
He started with the one that frightened him least.

The Primordial Source. He had grasped it later, integrated it partially. It was dense and patient inside him and it was not his, had never been his, was older than every framework and belonged to all of existence and none of it.
’Cast out.’

He took hold of it with his will and pulled, and it tore free of his foundations like a root coming out of deep soil, and he sent it away from himself, down through the one channel this place had not sealed, into the living Observable Existence he carried, and THE Infiniverse received it in silence and held it, and a piece of what Noah Osmont was became a thing Noah Osmont was storing.
The absence hit him like cold water!
He breathed through it, and the stone pressed down, and he went again.
The Causes!

This one cost him. He had wanted, even in the theory, even while the idea was still glorious and abstract, to keep his nine. His Osmontian Causes, carved from his own identity, Existence and Paradox and Tyranny and the rest. Surely those were his. Surely those counted!
They did not, and he knew it!

They were carved in the shape of a thing called a Cause. And Causes linked to Civilizations and concepts and frameworks that were standing in existence long before he arrived, designed or grown by hands that were not his, and he had made his own versions of somebody else’s idea, which made them his work and not his origination!
So...
’Cast out!’
HUUM!

The nine tore free, and with them the nine First Causes of Hvitrmarr, and as that mixture unwound he felt the bond to a distant queen strain and cry out somewhere far above this place, a single pulse of alarm through a connection stretched thin by the trial’s walls, and he could not stop to answer it.
The Collision of Causes stuttered and went silent inside him for the first time since he had lit it. The drums stopped.
Eighteen anchors sank into THE Infiniverse, and the quiet where they had been was enormous.
And then he stood at the edge of the one that terrified him.
Infinity.

He knelt under the stone with his blood in the sand and looked at it, the deep blue-gold sea of his Osmontian Source Infinity, the thing that had been with him since before the crown, before the Letters, before any of it!
Infinite Mana!
It was THE first gift, the oldest companion, the floor under every floor. He had been the man with infinite mana before he had been anything else at all!
It was all he had begun with.

And it was not his. Infinity was a route, a variety, a framework walked by lifeforms across all of existence for ages before one human picked it up, and the fact that his was the grandest ocean of it anywhere did not change one drop of where the idea had come from.
Noah’s whole existence recoiled from the act!
Oh!
Fear, actual fear, the thing he never showed and rarely felt, moved through him at the prospect of being a man without it!
What was he without Mana?!
But...
He gripped the ocean.
’Even this.’
’CAST IT OUT!’
BOOM!
The sea tore out of him.

It went in one enormous wrenching motion, blue-gold light hemorrhaging out of every layer of his existence at once, pouring away down the channel into THE Infiniverse, and she took it, his ocean, into herself, and Noah knelt in the black sand and felt what it was to be empty of the thing his own name had been built on.
He did not stop!
He could not stop, because stopping now would leave him half-emptied and holding nothing, so he went through the rest of the borrowed house room by room and threw it all out.

Mana itself, the concept beneath the ocean. Cast out. The Pantheon-frame, the ancient inherited idea of housing realms within an existence. Cast out, and THE Infiniverse herself remained his and beloved and safe, but the framework by which he held her was severed, and she drifted from appendage to companion in a single tearing moment.

The Intent-ladder, Egoic and Ananke, two rungs climbed on a structure other beings had raised. Cast out, and his Ananke Intent of THE Quintessential Osmontian went silent and sank away, and the pressure he had carried was simply gone!
The Foundations he kept. The nine Foundations were fusions he had pioneered, his design from the first. Those were his!
The Tongue he kept, since the Tongue was the definition of his, the language of his own existence, and it was the one thing he had chosen from the start, and now he finally understood why!
Then...
The Scales.

He paused on that one, kneeling, bleeding, nearly hollow, because THE First and Second Infinite Scales of Existence was his framework, built by his hands, named in his Tongue, and every instinct said keep it.
And it was built as a Scale. In answer to Vakochev’s Scales, in the shape of Vakochev’s idea, a better ladder leaned against the same wall. An idea based on another’s idea.
’Cast out.’
The Infinite Scale of Existence unhooked from him and sank into THE Infiniverse with everything else, and Noah knelt in the sand as a being without a framework of any kind.
One thing remained.
THE Amaranthine Heart.

It beat in his chest where his own heart had made room for it, warm and steady and alive, the heart of THE Felt Eternity, given with the words I give you my Everything. It was not a framework. It was not a concept. It was a gift from a being who loved him, and it had carried him through the HUMAN Letter.
It was also not his generation. It was hers.
’I’m sorry,’ he thought, to Emotive, who could not hear him.
He cast it out.

THE Amaranthine Heart left his chest gently, the only gentle departure in the whole terrible inventory, and settled into THE Infiniverse beside the ocean and the Causes and the Scale, safe, kept...for a potential future that may never be!
And then it was done.
Noah knelt on the dark obsidian sands beneath the weight of a sky, and he was nothing!
Not weakened. Nothing. His body carried no authority whatsoever. No Infinity, no Source, no Intent, no Causes, no Pantheon, no Scale, no heart that was not his own.

He felt the change the way one feels silence after a lifetime in a loud room, and what he felt was, of all things, familiar. This was a human body. This was what it had felt like to be a man in world before the first prompt ever bloomed. He was, freely and truly and completely, a normal human being.
Who was holding up a stone that had crushed Primeval Ones.

It did not mean he was as strong as a Primeval. He was not. It meant only that the weight had never once been measuring strength, and that what it measured, he was finally expressing with nothing borrowed in the way.
Just himself. Whatever that turned out to be!
The stone came down for the eighth time.

Noah’s arms buckled. His whole body shook, the plain human muscle of it burning past every limit muscle has, and he closed his eyes and bowed his head beneath the load, and every fissure in his existence groaned at once, and there was nothing left to reinforce with, no Letter he had the breath to speak, no ocean, no drums, nothing between him and the collapse except whatever he was.
And his body, being a body, did what bodies do at the very end.

It understood, in the wordless way flesh understands, that it was about to be crushed. That no help was coming from anywhere, because everywhere had been cast out. That if anything was going to preserve this existence, the existence would have to produce it, now, itself, from nothing, because nothing was all that remained.
And so, deep within him, in the emptied dark where an ocean used to be...
HUUUM!
A singularity bloomed.

It was blue. Dazzling, incandescent blue, a single point of light igniting in the hollow of him, and it was small and it was inexhaustible and it was unfathomably beautiful, and it had no upstream, no framework, no name in any Tongue but his.
It was his light. It stemmed from Noah Osmont, and from nothing else in all of existence!

His body remained free of any authority. Nothing pressed outward from him. Nothing announced. To every instrument ever built for weighing power, the kneeling figure in the bloody sand read exactly as it had a moment before, a normal human at the end of his strength.
And yet!
He had stopped straining!
He had stopped shaking!
HE HAD STOPPED SHAKING!
