chapters.title: Chapter 5566: Ignorance! I
paragraphs: The singularity rose with him!

That was the first thing Noah understood about it, kneeling in his own blood with the weight of a sky on his back. It did not sit inside him the way the ocean had sat, or press outward the way Intent had pressed. It rose as he rose, moved as he moved, and it was, without any close competition, the most calm and stable thing he had ever felt.
Internally, it was blinding. A point of incandescent blue burning in the emptied dark of him, bright past looking at directly!

Externally, it was nothing. Not one glimmer of aura left his body. Not one wave of anything crossed his skin. The instruments of existence, had any been pointed at him, would have found a bleeding human kneeling in sand.
And the moment it bloomed fully, what arrived with it was not power!
HUUM!

It was capability. Power was a quantity, and he had held quantities before, oceans of them, and this was not that. This was the wordless knowledge that he was capable. It generated from him completely. It had no upstream. It was his.
His Provenance!
’PROVENANCE!’
And then, without one glimmer of authority leaking from anywhere on his body, Noah began to rise.

It was the strangest sensation of his entire existence, and he had died once, so the competition was real. The weight above him did not lessen. Nothing about the stone changed at all. His body simply decided, joint by joint, that it could handle it, the way a body decides it can stand after illness, not through any surge of force but through a quiet reassessment of what was possible, and the reassessment kept arriving, and he kept rising!
His back straightened beneath the load!
One knee left the sand. Then the other!

The stone that had crushed Primeval Ones rode on his back, and then, slowly and deliberately, he brought it up onto his two raised hands, and stood beneath it holding the underside of a sky at arm’s length while his blood dried on his face.
Then one hand.
Then his fingers!
And then Noah pushed up, once, and the stone rose!
HUUUM!

It left his fingertips and climbed, the whole colossal landmass of obsidian gold ascending back into the heavens where it had hung, and it settled there and did not come down again, and across the entire domain the pressure released like a held breath finally let go!
The Ancestral Voice said nothing.

For the first time since the doorway, the voice that had narrated, insulted, mourned, and confessed through every step of this road had no words at all, and the silence stretched across the black sands, and Noah stood in the middle of it, small and bleeding and empty of everything, beneath a sky he had just put back.
Obsidian gold light filled the heavens.
It poured off the risen stone and down through the air and across the dunes, the whole domain igniting with it, and Noah closed his eyes and simply let himself feel.
The singularity hummed.
A constant, heavy hum, new and ancient at once, resonating out from the blue point through every layer of what remained of him, and where the resonance passed, things began to change!

He felt it at the smallest scale first, in the makeup of his cells, in the very structure of his atoms, the fine architecture of a human body beginning to break down and transform under a frequency that belonged to nothing else in existence.
And from the pores of his skin, filth began to leak.

Obsidian-gray sludge, thick and dark, welling up and running off him in slow rivulets, and Noah understood what he was seeing without anything explaining it. His Foundations, perfect across the Depths. His Physiology, rebuilt from Primeval Cells. Everything he had held and refined and elevated across the whole climb, and all of it, this entire time, had carried defects in it!

Murky filth folded into the joints of even his finest work, impurities so deep in the making that no elevation had ever reached them, because every elevation had been performed with borrowed instruments, and borrowed instruments left their fingerprints.
The Provenance hummed, and his existence expelled everything unworthy of it.
There were no prompts.
No analysis followed, and nothing anywhere was explaining to him what was happening!
It was just him. He was the one figuring it out, understanding it as it occurred, naming it as it moved, and it came to him that this was not an absence of the prompts.
This was what the prompts had been imitating all along.
And as his existence transformed, as the hum deepened and the filth ran, Noah felt an answering hum from far ahead.
He opened his eyes, and they wept gray filth like the rest of him, and he looked across the sands.
THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity.

It hung around the golden obelisk in the distance, wrapped in its sphere of impenetrable light, and it was humming back at him, and with his transforming eyes it looked entirely different than it had looked an hour ago.

He could see something on it now. Something that had been there the whole time, invisible to every eye that had ever looked at it, and Noah stared across the distance at what the collar actually was and understood, in a single cold drop of clarity, that not even the people of THE Ymnaros knew what was truly here!
Not even, perhaps, the being that had failed twice to take it.
And as he watched, the protective barrier around the obelisk began to disappear.

The sphere of obsidian gold light thinned, and paled, and came apart from the top down, dissolving the way the doorway light had dissolved, because the trial was passed and the way was open, and the collar hung in the clearing air with nothing between it and the sands at all.
|You are exceptional.|
The Ancestral Voice boomed across the domain.
And Noah’s eyes flashed, because the voice had not come from everywhere.
It had come from ahead.
Far in the distance, at the base of the golden obelisk, inches from the hanging collar, in a space where only Noah should have been able to stand, a figure had appeared.
Tousled hair. White robes. Hands no longer folded behind his back.
Anaximander.

His mild face was raised toward the collar, and his eyes were glazed with a cold and ancient light that had never once belonged to the scholar, and when the mouth moved, the voice that came out of it was the one that had narrated this entire road.
|You are exceptional. But I...|
|I have lived for too long to stand idly by.|
|I thank you for opening the door. I will do the rest from here.|
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5567: Ignorance! II
paragraphs: When the pool that has no color calls, the hand must give its own
For blood of True and Primeval both shall pay the ferry home
The dimension lost to time and space wait not for those who plead
They open only to the one who bleeds the eldest creed
Twice shall the crown be offered up, and twice shall it be worn
But only what is set down whole may pass where ash is borne
The mask that saves a thousand lives must die upon the face
For quintessence cannot truly bloom while shadows hold its place
Beware the kneeling of the proud, for kneeling is not loss
The silhouette unfinished waits where all the futures cross
What eats, and watches, and remains shall gather in one name
And that which you cannot reject, you must become, or be become

Noah’s eyes flashed with an incandescent light, his body still shedding gray filth into the sand, and across the distance the hands of Anaximander, moved by another, reached for THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity.
And every piece of it fell into place at once!

I hate what is happening here. The Voice had said that in the middle of the second trial, and dressed it in a crude joke about a beautiful woman being handed to somebody else. It had hated what was happening. It had said so!
Nobody asks what a dying guardian hates about its own rescue.
The dying voice of a Primeval thing that could not let go of something. Its own introduction. Everyone had heard grief in it!
The pathway shall open. Not for you. It had never once said for you!

And Hvitrmarr’s voice, thin and urgent through a bond stretched nearly to breaking, had reached him in the dark between the trials with the one thing she had thought he should know. Anaximander was taken elsewhere. The Voice came for him and took him another direction, and none of us know where.
A being with no external authority!

Noah had walked the last trial with all of it sitting in his mind, unproven and unforgotten. He had cast out everything he owned above a sand that had killed Primevals, with the suspicion filed and waiting, and he had done it anyway, because the door needed opening and he was the one who could open it, and because a man who has just generated his own light from nothing is a very different of a man than the one who entered.
So now he stood in the black sands, bleeding gray, transformed and transforming, and watched a stolen friend’s hand close the last inches toward a Remnant Existential Treasure.
And his eyes showed no surprise at all!
"Why are you in such a hurry," Noah asked, "when your prize is right before you? Can you tell me why?"
Across the sands, the hand stopped inches from the gold.
Anaximander’s body did not turn. The cold ancient light in his eyes stayed fixed on the collar, and the voice that came out of him was almost conversational!
|Because I could not possibly give such a thing to another.|

|Do you understand what this is? What it can do? With this in hand, I could save every Superpowered Lifeform in this Dimension without needing anyone. Without waiting on candidates, without lowering standards, without begging strangers to be worthy. Every descendant I have watched die in rows in front of stones, and I could end all of it myself, at last, after ages of watching.|
|And with this body, it is possible. Anaximander, containing my remnants, and all the others who failed before me. He can hold what none of us could hold alone.|
The glazed eyes tilted slightly, as though appraising the flesh they occupied.
|He is almost like you, you know. He just seems a bit different. I have not yet determined where the difference lives.|
Noah listened in silence.

His transformation had not stopped for any of it. The gray filth still ran from him in thinning rivulets, the hum of the singularity still worked down through his atoms, and he stood in the middle of his own remaking and asked his next question as calmly as the first.
"How did you get into Anaximander, though?"
|Carefully.|
The word came cold.

|A being like him cannot be taken. I did not cheat, whatever you may be preparing to think of me. His body cannot be harmed by others. His identity makes existence conform around it. Every art of possession ever devised breaks against a nature like his, and I knew it, and so I did the only thing that works on the truly unique and the truly powerful.|
|I asked.|

|Consent was critical. He agreed to carry the pieces of every failure across every age, freely, with his eyes open, because he is kind, and kindness is a door that beings like him never think to lock. What entered him, entered invited.What lies atop his consciousness now, he accepted the weight of. I broke no law of his existence.|
|I merely understood which laws he would suspend for a stranger who asked politely.|
Noah nodded to that, calmly, and sighed.

"I would let you continue," he said. "Honestly. I would let you reach out and try to take hold of THE Aurate Collar, and I would stand here and watch you burn for it, because I think you know less about what is hanging on that obelisk than you believe you do, and I can see something on it now that you cannot."
His eyes did not leave the figure at the obelisk.
"But my friend would burn with you. So I have to stop you."
The face of Anaximander turned at last, and it had become distasteful, a frown pulling at features that had never worn one, an expression fitted onto the wrong man.
|I have waited too long for this.|
|I have many depending on me. Every Superpowered Lifeform still breathing in this Dimension is my responsibility, and I will finish what I started, and I will not be lectured by a candidate.|
The glazed eyes narrowed.

|You show a spark. That is all. You have not attained the status of those beings, whatever you may feel blooming in you. A spark is a possibility, not a Provenance. And after I grasp the collar, I will take that spark from you as well, since leaving it loose in existence would be untidy.|
Oh?
Noah almost smiled.

This being thought he had passed the trial because he showed a spark. It had stood witness to the whole of it, and it had read all of that as a glimmer. A possibility. A one-in-a-trillion flicker of what might someday be!
He shook his head slowly, because he had not shown a spark.
He had caused the emergence of his own unique individual essence, generated from himself and nothing else across all of existence. His Provenance!

It hummed in him at this very moment, calm and blinding and entirely his, and the being wearing his friend had watched it happen and could not see it, because a thing with no external authority does not announce itself to instruments built for weighing authority, and the Voice was, in the end, exactly what it had confessed to being. A creature made entirely of successful accumulation, reading the whole of existence through the one lens it had.
But he did not need any of that.

That was the part the Voice had truly failed to account for. Noah watched the possessed hand begin to move again, closing the last inches toward the gold, and he knew with complete certainty that Anaximander’s body would not be able to handle what it was about to touch, and so he did not reach for his Provenance at all.
He said two words.
"Anaximander, Come!"
HUUM!

For blood of True and Primeval both shall pay the ferry home
The dimension lost to time and space wait not for those who plead
They open only to the one who bleeds the eldest creed
Twice shall the crown be offered up, and twice shall it be worn
But only what is set down whole may pass where ash is borne
The mask that saves a thousand lives must die upon the face
For quintessence cannot truly bloom while shadows hold its place
Beware the kneeling of the proud, for kneeling is not loss
The silhouette unfinished waits where all the futures cross
What eats, and watches, and remains shall gather in one name
And that which you cannot reject, you must become, or be become

Noah’s eyes flashed with an incandescent light, his body still shedding gray filth into the sand, and across the distance the hands of Anaximander, moved by another, reached for THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity.
And every piece of it fell into place at once!
I hate what is happening here.
The Voice had said that in the middle of the second trial, and dressed it in a crude joke about a beautiful woman being handed to somebody else.
It had hated what was happening.
It had said so!
Nobody asks what a dying guardian hates about its own rescue.
The dying voice of a Primeval thing that could not let go of something.
Its own introduction.
Everyone had heard grief in it!
The pathway shall open.
Not for you.
It had never once said for you!
And Hvitrmarr’s voice, thin and urgent through a bond stretched nearly to breaking, had reached him in the dark between the trials with the one thing she had thought he should know.
Anaximander was taken elsewhere.
The Voice came for him and took him another direction, and none of us know where.
A being with no external authority!
Noah had walked the last trial with all of it sitting in his mind, unproven and unforgotten.

He had cast out everything he owned above a sand that had killed Primevals, with the suspicion filed and waiting, and he had done it anyway, because the door needed opening and he was the one who could open it, and because a man who has just generated his own light from nothing is a very different of a man than the one who entered.
So now he stood in the black sands, bleeding gray, transformed and transforming, and watched a stolen friend’s hand close the last inches toward a Remnant Existential Treasure.
And his eyes showed no surprise at all!
"Why are you in such a hurry," Noah asked, "when your prize is right before you?
Can you tell me why?"
Across the sands, the hand stopped inches from the gold.
Anaximander’s body did not turn.
The cold ancient light in his eyes stayed fixed on the collar, and the voice that came out of him was almost conversational!
|Because I could not possibly give such a thing to another.|
|Do you understand what this is?
What it can do?
With this in hand, I could save every Superpowered Lifeform in this Dimension without needing anyone.
Without waiting on candidates, without lowering standards, without begging strangers to be worthy.
Every descendant I have watched die in rows in front of stones, and I could end all of it myself, at last, after ages of watching.|
|And with this body, it is possible.
Anaximander, containing my remnants, and all the others who failed before me.
He can hold what none of us could hold alone.|
The glazed eyes tilted slightly, as though appraising the flesh they occupied.
|He is almost like you, you know.
He just seems a bit different.
I have not yet determined where the difference lives.|
Noah listened in silence.
His transformation had not stopped for any of it.

The gray filth still ran from him in thinning rivulets, the hum of the singularity still worked down through his atoms, and he stood in the middle of his own remaking and asked his next question as calmly as the first.
"How did you get into Anaximander, though?"
|Carefully.|
The word came cold.
|A being like him cannot be taken.
I did not cheat, whatever you may be preparing to think of me.
His body cannot be harmed by others.
His identity makes existence conform around it.
Every art of possession ever devised breaks against a nature like his, and I knew it, and so I did the only thing that works on the truly unique and the truly powerful.|

He agreed to carry the pieces of every failure across every age, freely, with his eyes open, because he is kind, and kindness is a door that beings like him never think to lock.
What entered him, entered invited.What lies atop his consciousness now, he accepted the weight of.
I broke no law of his existence.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5568: Four Numbers! I
paragraphs: The hand trembled.

It stopped, fingers spread, a breath from the collar, and it shook there in the air as though caught between two winds, and the face of Anaximander contorted through astonishment into shock and then into rage as the thing inside him hauled at the arm with everything it had absorbed across every age, and the arm did not move!
HUUM!
|Impossible.|
The Voice tore out of the borrowed mouth.

|I accounted for everything. EVERYTHING. The wills of multiple Primevals lie atop his consciousness. Mine, and my friend’s, and every candidate of every age, all of it pressing down on whatever remains of him, he cannot simply...! I....!|
But he could!
Oh, Anaximander could!
Because not too long ago ago, a scholar had said the same thing to the only two friends he had ever made in different times.
Whenever you need me, call. Say, Anaximander, Come!

He had said it as law, a condition and regulation imposed upon his own existence, written into the same nature that let him go where he pleased and made existence conform around him, and no will in existence had standing to countermand a rule that Anaximander had set for Anaximander!
The body at the obelisk buckled.

It went down to its knees in the black sand with both hands grasping its head, and the cold ancient light in the eyes guttered and flared and guttered, and a sound came out of it that was two voices at once and then, by degrees, only one, a raw human cry of pain as the real Anaximander surfaced through everything lying on top of him and came, because he had been called, and coming when called was what he was!
The ancientness drained out of the figure.

The pressure of ages went out of the air around it. What knelt in the sand released no aura at all, carried no weight of epochs, read to every sense as a tousled man in white robes breathing hard with his hands in his hair, and when he finally raised his head, his face was his own!

And it was... profoundly sad as be breathed out. He was...disappointed, in the deep quiet way of a man who had extended trust as a matter of principle to something ancient and beloved by an entire people, something that had watched over every Superpowered Lifeform across every age, and had found, underneath all that long guardianship, this.
He looked at Noah with that sad face, and rose slowly to his feet.
"Thank you,"he said. "And sorry about that."
He glanced back once at the collar, and then away.
"I thought things would be different. I knew the burdens would be heavy. I weighed that before I said yes, and I was prepared for the weight."His voice caught slightly.

"I did not anticipate greed to be such a profound condition. That it could encompass even something like him. A guardian. A being that spent its dying light saving its own people while it did this..."
Anaximander seemed lost.
Noah remained where he was, and his expression softened.
"Greed spares no one..." His voice came quiet and certain across the sands.

"Not the small, not the ancient, not the dying, not the good. It is the one appetite that grows best in the largest existences, because they have lived long enough to want one thing across ages. Greed...is a critical factor of existence..."
WAA!
And then Noah’s body released a deep, resonant pulse.

The last of the gray filth stopped at his pores and did not come again. The transformation completed itself in a single settling wave, and what stood in the black sands afterward was a man whose fair skin was clear and unblemished from crown to heel, whose hair had gone pure dark, deeper than it had ever been, and whose stillness was the stillness of a thing with nothing left in it that did not belong.
His eyes opened fully.
The pupils in them were obsidian singularities, small and absolute, and they looked unfathomably old, the way the first idea anything ever had is old!
And they looked new!
Oh, so new!
Noah breathed in.

The air of the final domain came into lungs that had been remade at the level of cells, and it carried nothing to him. No ambient essence. No drifting weavings. Nothing his body reached for, because his body no longer reached outward for anything at all!
He did not absorb!
The hollow where an ocean of power once sat now held a single blue singularity, blinding within and silent without, humming its ancient hum through the whole of him.

He was himself! He had cast out the Primordial Source and Infinity and eighteen Causes and the Intent and a Scale of his own design, and after all of that, he still felt like Noah Osmont. More like Noah Osmont than he had ever felt in his life!
He opened his eyes, looked toward the distant obelisk where Anaximander knelt beneath the hanging gold of THE Aurate Collar, and took a step.
And...
BOOM!
The domain shook!

The obsidian sand beneath his foot did not scatter. It curved. It bent downward in a wide, smooth bowl for miles in every direction, sinking the way ground sinks when it is asked to hold something unfathomably dense, and the dark grains ground against each other with a sound like a mountain settling!
Heavy winds erupted from that single point of contact!

They tore outward across the flats in expanding rings, ripping the stillness of ages off the face of the domain, and far ahead even Anaximander had to raise one hand against the gale to remain steady, his white robes cracking around him like banners!
The golden obelisk light flickered. The distant landmass hanging in the sky groaned. All of it, from one step.
Noah stood in the center of the bowl his own weight had pressed into existence, and he frowned.
It was very hard to describe how he felt right now.

He felt normal. His arm rose when he asked it to rise. His breath came when he called it. There was no surging tide inside him, no roaring reserves, no pressure begging for release. By every internal measure he was a man standing on sand.

And yet every move he made exerted terrifying pressure on everything around him, the way a thing exerts pressure when it is far too dense for the space holding it, and existence itself in these surroundings was straining and creaking simply to contain him.
The cause of all of it was himself.

His Provenance was newly budding. It generated from him constantly, his own essence, his own authority, unique to him alone, and he did not yet know how to properly hold it in. It was new. He was new!

chapters.title: Chapter 5569: Four Numbers! II
paragraphs: Across the shaking flats, Anaximander looked over at him through the heavy winds. There was no fear in the scholar’s face. There was something quieter and heavier, sitting beside the fresh sadness already there.
"What is happening to you?" he asked somberly.
Noah raised his hands and looked at them.
CREAK!
Space distorted around his fingers as he lifted them, thin lines of strain webbing out through the air and sealing themselves shut again, the domain flinching away from ten ordinary fingers!
"I am expressing myself,"Noah said. "Fully. Who I am, all of it, all at once."
He turned his hands over slowly, watching the air bend."I don’t have control over it yet."
He lowered his hands.
"But the solution should be easy."
He breathed out and closed his eyes again.

As much as some part of him wanted to, he could not go back to his old system. The Scales were familiar. The grades, the ranks, the ladders, the tallies, every rung of it was familiar. He had even kept all of it, saved inside THE Infiniverse, because in the end he could not entirely let it go.
But he had begun to be unfathomably true. He had generated something of his own, out of nothing but himself, and a being who had done that could not keep measuring himself with borrowed rulers.
He would have to look at himself differently now.
So at this moment, standing in the bowl of bent sand with the winds still circling him, Noah turned his attention inward and focused on the singularity.
His light.

He did not command it. Commanding was for external things, and this was not external. He communicated with it instead, the way a man communicates with his own heartbeat when he finally sits still long enough to listen, and the singularity answered by simply being understood.
Its hum ran through him, ancient and grand and his.
Every moment of listening taught him something, because every moment of listening was self-knowledge. This was Provenance Essence!

This was what he generated. It was not a store of power to be spent. It was an ongoing statement of what he was, and the pressure wrecking the domain was only that statement spoken too loudly, without shape.
Shape could be learned. He was already learning it. His mind filled with possibilities, one after another, each opening onto ten more.
And then...
Noah smiled.
And at this time, he called out.
"Oh, Ruination."
HUUM!
Light gathered beside him and became a figure!
Her illusory form took shape in strands of crimson and blue, the familiar silhouette he had carried on through wars beyond counting, and she...was crying.

She appeared already wiping at her face with both hands, over and over, quick and precise the way she did everything, as if she wanted the tears to stop and could not make them stop, and they kept coming anyway, bright drops sliding down through her translucent light!
Because Noah had cast out many things.

She had felt every one of them arrive. The Source. The Causes. Infinity. The Heart. The entire contents of his existence, delivered into THE Infiniverse, one treasure after another set down and pushed away, and from the far side of a silent channel it had felt like watching someone give away everything he was as even she...felt disconnected! When he had been so close!
Noah’s heart pained when he saw her like this.
He crossed the sand to her, and the domain shuddered under every step, and he did not care, and he took her into his arms.
"I’m sorry," he said quietly. "I had to put many things aside."
She shook against him without a sound.
"But you are never something that came from others."His hand rested on the back of her head. "Most of what you are came from our journey together. And it will always continue. Okay?"
Ruination looked up at him.
Then she stepped back, wiped her eyes one last time, and waved her hands. Between them, light condensed into a circlet of deep blue, slender and clean, turning slowly in the air.
THE Circlet of the Quintessential Ruin, offered back to him.
Noah smiled and took it, and set it on his head.
Ruination watched him do it, and her hands came together in front of her, and her voice came out small.
"Always together?"
"Always together," Noah said.
He let the words sit for a moment. Then he continued.
"Now. I want you to be the one to display the prompts of my new existence. Though this time, from here on out, I will be generating the knowledge." He tapped his own chest once.
"It comes from me now. You can make it simpler for us to look at and analyze. Okay?"
Ruination nodded.

Her figure dissolved into a glimmer of crimson blue light that flowed upward and into the circlet, and it settled loosely above his head, riding there the way a crown rides on a king who has stopped needing one and wears it anyway.
The last of the change moved through him then.

The adornments on his body, robes and wrappings that had carried him across Dimensions, were riddled through with the black filth his transformation had expelled, and now they burned away entirely, ash scattering on the wind. In their place, pristine white pants took form, plain and heavy, burning with a sense of ancientness that no forge in existence had put there!
Above the waist he was laid bare, and his muscular upper body stood clean under the obelisk light, every line of it pristine, a physique with nothing borrowed in it anywhere.
Dark hair. Obsidian singularities for pupils. A crown of blue light!
Noah closed his eyes.
And he heard Ruination’s voice once more.
|An unfathomable change has occurred to your existence.|

|What is being identified as Provenance Essence has bloomed within you in the form of a singularity. Your existence has communicated with itself to better allow you to grasp your power, and it has generated a System of Power and Measurement unique to you, applicable to your power alone.|
|When you gaze upon others, their weavings will also appear and be translated into this same System of Measurement.|
|Your existence has been broken down into the following:|
|VERITAS: how true you are to yourself.|
|PROVENANCE: how much of you is your own generation.|
|POTENTIA: what you could still become.|
|PONDUS: the weight you can carry without breaking.|
Noah looked at these prompts with a smile.

This was what his existence wanted to simplify things down to. Four measures. Not grades handed down from trees older than his species, not Scales built in answer to another being’s framework. Four questions a man could ask himself, made into numbers!
He went a step further.
"Show me my current Status Panel."
WAA!
|STATUS PANEL: NOAH OSMONT|
|VERITAS: 10|
|PROVENANCE: 1(???)|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 5|
|THE OSMONTIAN TONGUE: I AM · OSMONT · QUINTESSENTIAL · HUMAN · PROTAGONIST|
|THE NINE FOUNDATIONS: S-RANK EBAD|

|THE Unkneeling Crown · THE Tide That Owes Nothing · THE Mirror That Keeps · THE Hunger That Refines · THE Unmoved Verdict · THE Pure Trajectory · THE All-Drawing Stillness · THE Remembered Truth · THE Sovereign Existence|
|All Foundations stemmed from your own making. They have been naturally elevated through your transformation.|

Ruination looked up at him.
Then she stepped back, wiped her eyes one last time, and waved her hands.
Between them, light condensed into a circlet of deep blue, slender and clean, turning slowly in the air.
THE Circlet of the Quintessential Ruin, offered back to him.
Noah smiled and took it, and set it on his head.
Ruination watched him do it, and her hands came together in front of her, and her voice came out small.
"Always together?"
"Always together," Noah said.
He let the words sit for a moment.
Then he continued.
"Now.
I want you to be the one to display the prompts of my new existence.
Though this time, from here on out, I will be generating the knowledge." He tapped his own chest once.
"It comes from me now.
You can make it simpler for us to look at and analyze.
Okay?"
Ruination nodded.

Her figure dissolved into a glimmer of crimson blue light that flowed upward and into the circlet, and it settled loosely above his head, riding there the way a crown rides on a king who has stopped needing one and wears it anyway.
The last of the change moved through him then.

The adornments on his body, robes and wrappings that had carried him across Dimensions, were riddled through with the black filth his transformation had expelled, and now they burned away entirely, ash scattering on the wind.
In their place, pristine white pants took form, plain and heavy, burning with a sense of ancientness that no forge in existence had put there!
Above the waist he was laid bare, and his muscular upper body stood clean under the obelisk light, every line of it pristine, a physique with nothing borrowed in it anywhere.
Dark hair.
Obsidian singularities for pupils.
A crown of blue light!
Noah closed his eyes.
And he heard Ruination’s voice once more.
|An unfathomable change has occurred to your existence.|
|What is being identified as Provenance Essence has bloomed within you in the form of a singularity.
Your existence has communicated with itself to better allow you to grasp your power, and it has generated a System of Power and Measurement unique to you, applicable to your power alone.|
|When you gaze upon others, their weavings will also appear and be translated into this same System of Measurement.|
|Your existence has been broken down into the following:|
|VERITAS: how true you are to yourself.|
|PROVENANCE: how much of you is your own generation.|
|POTENTIA: what you could still become.|
|PONDUS: the weight you can carry without breaking.|
Noah looked at these prompts with a smile.
This was what his existence wanted to simplify things down to.
Four measures.
Not grades handed down from trees older than his species, not Scales built in answer to another being’s framework.
Four questions a man could ask himself, made into numbers!
He went a step further.
"Show me my current Status Panel."
WAA!
|STATUS PANEL: NOAH OSMONT|
|VERITAS: 10|
|PROVENANCE: 1(???)|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 5|
|THE OSMONTIAN TONGUE: I AM · OSMONT · QUINTESSENTIAL · HUMAN · PROTAGONIST|
|THE NINE FOUNDATIONS: S-RANK EBAD|

|THE Unkneeling Crown · THE Tide That Owes Nothing · THE Mirror That Keeps · THE Hunger That Refines · THE Unmoved Verdict · THE Pure Trajectory · THE All-Drawing Stillness · THE Remembered Truth · THE Sovereign Existence|
|All Foundations stemmed from your own making.
They have been naturally elevated through your transformation.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5570: Four Numbers! III
paragraphs: Noah stood in the settling winds with the Status Panel still hanging in his sight, and he read it again.
|VERITAS: 10|
|PROVENANCE: 1(???)|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 5|
Four numbers. His whole existence, broken down by his own existence, into four numbers!
He wanted to understand them properly before he moved another step. So he raised his eyes across the dark sand, and he gazed at Anaximander.
HUUM!

The moment his attention truly settled on the scholar, his new sight went to work. The weavings of Anaximander’s existence rose into view, dense and strange and layered with things that should not have been there, and his obsidian singularity pupils drank them in as Ruination translated everything into the one System of Measurement that belonged to Noah alone!
|STATUS PANEL: ANAXIMANDER|
|VERITAS: 3|
|PROVENANCE: 0|
|POTENTIA: UNDEFINED|
|PONDUS: 1|
Noah went still, and his analysis began.
VERITAS 3!

This was Anaximander. The man whose identity made existence conform! Noah almost wanted to say this number may be low, but he had just advanced himself as he didnt know how high he was compared to more...normal lifeforms.

But Noah remembered what was inside Anaximander now. The Ancestral Voice, suppressed but present. Failed candidates, the remnants of collapsed existences, all of them packed into one body and held down by one will.

The panel was not measuring Anaximander the man. It was measuring everything currently answering to that name, and most of what answered to that name right now was not him. A muddy mixing of many selves, weighed as one. Of course the number came out low when Anaximander was so unique!

Which meant VERITAS as a measure...could fall.It could be diluted by what a being carried. And if it could fall, then it could climb, and Noah did not for one moment assume that his own 10 sat at any ceiling!
The numbers would go higher. He could feel it in the hum! A 10 today was a floor he happened to be standing on, nothing more.
He then thought about Anaximander’s Provenance.
That one required no theory at all!
Anaximander generated nothing of his own. Neither did anyone else Noah had ever met. As for the Undefined potential of Anaximander...this continued to be his own mystery!
Noah turned his sight inward, and laid his own four numbers beside his conclusions.
VERITAS was how true he was to himself, and it could climb without limit.
PROVENANCE was how much of himself he generated, and only he could generate it.
POTENTIA was what he could still become, and his read INFINITE.
PONDUS was what he could bear without breaking, and bearing more was a matter of becoming more!
And every one of them pointed the same direction. Not outward, toward treasures and grades and the frameworks of ancient beings. Inward, toward how he lived.
His eyes opened fully, and he his voice boomed out because he felt like it!

"If I live gloriously, tyrannically, Quintessentially... I will advance, as I will be living truly as myself. My VERITAS increases... so will my PROVENANCE, and PONDUS, and everything else follows. Based on my actions, I will generate more Provenance. I will be more true, and my immensity will increase as external authority... won’t do anything to me! External treasures won’t do anything to me! Only that which I generate myself, from my own existence!"
HUUM!
The singularity in his chest hummed grandly at the declaration, and the obsidian sand for miles trembled once and went still!
That which he generated from his own existence.
His mind went automatically to THE Tide That Owes Nothing.

It sat among his Nine Foundations, and the Nine Foundations had survived the casting out because they were fusions nobody had conceived before him, carved from his own thinking. And the Tide’s whole nature was generation through his actions.

If anything else in what remained of him could be considered truly from him, could generate returns that fed VERITAS and PROVENANCE both, it may be the Tide. One more engine to further accelerate his progression, waiting to be tested against his new existence!
But then his eyes flickered.
Because he thought about Mana.
He thought about Infinity!

Both of them gone from him now, resting in THE Infiniverse with everything else he had set down, and their absence raised the question his existence had already answered and not explained. His POTENTIA was INFINITE. But how could he use his potential?

He felt the hum of Provenance inside him, steady and vast, and the answer it gave was not words. It was certainty. He would not be limited when it came to expressing his power. The concepts he had cast out were external things, and external things had external limits, but Provenance generated. Whatever he needed, he would not borrow it back.
He would learn to express and generate his own type of mana!

His, from nothing but himself, shaped by no one’s framework. The thought opened outward into a hundred others, arts and expressions and possibilities stacking up behind his eyes, and he breathed once and set them all aside.
He would be able to understand many things about himself. There would be time for all of it!
But for now, he had to grasp that unique treasure lying in the open for him before anymore accidents occured.
Noah breathed in.
He took another step.
And existence no longer creaked around him.
The sand held flat under his foot. The air stood calm. His weight moved with him instead of ahead of him, and Noah smiled and nodded to himself.
Then, in an instant, he was in front of the obelisk.

The golden pillar rose above him with its wrapping of obsidian gold light peeled away, and THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity hung there in the open, rows of tubular gold beads and a teardrop fringe and a front plate that no eyes in THE Ymnaros had ever read, holding the thing upon it that only his transformed sight could see. The treasure that had eluded many across the ages, with nothing left standing between it and his hand!
Anaximander stood close by, steadier than before, though the cold ancient light was gone from his eyes and the sadness was not.
Noah looked at him first.
"Are you feeling okay?"
Anaximander smiled wryly.

"I have to digest a number of old things, and get myself back to my baseline. I should be okay."He tipped his head toward the hanging gold. "Go ahead, and see what this whole thing has been about. The thing that even ancient lifeforms became so greedy about."
Noah nodded.
And he reached out!

chapters.title: Chapter 5571: Remnant!
paragraphs: There are beings who reach for the treasures of the ages with trembling reverence, and there are beings who reach for them the way a man reaches for his coat. Noah belonged to the second kind!
His fingers closed around THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity as he breathed out.
"I have felt young all this time...." His thumb moved slowly along the gold. "And today, for the first time, I can almost say I feel old. As if I have passed a significant milestone."
He turned the collar slightly in his grip.
"And just as I get that feeling. Just as I settle into it, start to enjoy it, maybe. I come across something so ridiculously old that I almost feel young again."
He gave a small, unhurried smile.
"That is what this Collar is."
Anaximander listened closely, and as the words settled, his expression gradually normalized, as his curiosity won out.

Noah said all of this because of what he had felt at the first instant of contact. His Provenance Essence, that single singularity seated in his existence, had released a heavy, droning hum the moment his hands came against the gold, and through that hum he affirmed something the legends of THE Ymnaros had never once suspected.
The collar was made of bones.
HUUM!
Then the collar asked its question!

An invisible wavelength erupted from it, soundless and total, and Noah’s hand trembled against the gold, almost as if the item were asking him, plainly and without malice, whether he could even hold it!
And his Provenance Essence answered tyrannically.
It pulsed within him, once, and roared through the whole of his being with an answer that required no thought at all.
Fuck I can!
BOOM!
A fiendish, silent aura unfurled across the whole area, pressing outward through the dark sands in a wave that made the domain itself sit very still, and the trembling in his hand stopped!
Beside him, Anaximander, a man who had spent his entire long life loving nothing so much as exploring and understanding and grasping new things, leaned in.
"What is it, exactly?"
Noah closed his eyes.
And for the first time, truly, he began utilizing Provenance Essence.

The blue glow within him pulsed, and pulsed again, finding a rhythm, and the rhythm resonated with the collar in his hands. His own essence, generated from nothing but himself, reached into a thing older than every framework in existence and asked it what it was, and information began to feed back into his existence, direct and wordless, his to understand because he was the one generating the understanding.
Even he was astonished at what came back.
He confirmed it twice before he spoke.

"Existence is unfathomably old, and unfathomably vast,"Noah said, eyes still closed. "Older than any Scales. Older than the Dimensions the Scales were built to measure. Older than every Tongue and Law and Source that beings like us spend our short, ambitious lives collecting. And at the very beginning of all that vastness, before any of it had names, there lived THE First Lifeforms. THE Provenance Lifeforms."
His voice slowed, giving each piece its full weight.

"They lived grandly. They lived with unfathomable power, the kind that was never granted and never borrowed, because there was nothing yet to borrow from. And this collar...." His hands tightened slightly on the gold.

"This collar stems from the chest bones of a Provenance Lifeform. It has been deemed a Remnant Existential Treasure. But... It is, and it isn’t. It is simply the cluster of bones of an extremely terrifying lifeform, put together. And that alone is enough to make it a treasure. And also, somehow, not."

Noah sighed as he finished, and Anaximander came closer to look at the thing, his eyes moving across the tubular beads and the teardrop fringe as though rereading a book that had just changed languages.
Then the scholar shook his head.
"All my life, I ask the question of where things come from. Where things began. I want to understand."He gestured at the collar, at the obelisk, at the hanging landmass above them, at everything.
"But it is like existence does not want to be understood. It is frustrating." A pause, and the smallest wry lift at the corner of his mouth.
"Even though I will never stop asking."
Noah smiled at these words.

Then he turned his focus back to the terrifying tool in his hands, because he knew, as of this moment, that he had only grasped an initial understanding of it. The bones of a Provenance Lifeform were too unique to be read in one resonance. And there was something heavy within the collar, something he could almost sense at the edge of the feedback, close enough to know it was there and far enough to have no shape. He needed to spend just a bit more time with it, and...
HUUM!
At such a time.
The domain began to shake and tumble.
Above them, the skies tore open as if they were pages, ripped crudely along seams no sky should have, and the color of blood permeated everything, drowning the obelisk light in red!
What came through the torn skies was horrific.
Rivers of corpses gushed out of the wounds in the sky.

Rivers. Of corpses! Superpowered Lifeforms, the exemplifying kind, the kind that carried the weight of Observable Existences in their bare bodies, now tangled dead in their thousands and pouring downward in thick red torrents, limbs and faces surfacing and sinking in the flow, and the sound of it arriving was a wet, rolling thunder that this domain, which had held silence since before the Scales, had never once been asked to hold.
And riding on these rivers of corpses came Infinite Lifeforms.

Dozens of them, gliding down the dead as though the dead were a road, and all of them followed behind one figure at the forefront. A red robed entity whose gaze was extremely old and extremely callous, the gaze of something that had been looking at things like this, and arranging things like this, for longer than most Dimensions had existed.
Noah and Anaximander raised their heads to see all of it.
The river of corpses smashed into the sands!
BOOM!
Red sprayed across obsidian. The dead settled in heaps and drifts. And the old lifeform at the very forefront came to a leisurely stop in the air, and looked, first, at the object in Noah’s hands.
Then at Noah himself.
He blinked, incredulously.
And then he laughed.
"You cannot possibly be serious."The laugh rolled out over the corpses, genuinely entertained. "Really? How could you have possibly arrived here, and gotten swept up in this?"
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5572: MY MANA! I
paragraphs: A horrific aura erupted from the old lifeform, crashing down across the domain, and the drifts of dead flattened under it!
But Noah was not listening to the aura.

He was looking into this being’s eyes. And even though the body was another body, a stranger’s face wearing a stranger’s age, the instant their gazes met, he recognized what looked out from behind it.
It was the visage of THE Sealed One!

Noah’s gaze went cold and imperious. And behind that gaze, many things clicked quietly into place, one after another, regarding the Dimensionlapses, and the Infinite Lifeforms, and the shape of certain long games!
Without further ado, and without so much as a word, Noah casually raised THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity and put it on.
The sands beneath his feet twisted!
Existence cried out around him, a thin, straining sound from every direction at once, the sound of a domain realizing what it now contained, and Noah took a step without offering a conversation!
In an instant, he appeared in front of THE Sealed One!

And in that instant, hanging in the red air with the gold at his throat, he did not look like a man who had knelt as a normal Human beneath a falling sky mere hours ago. Bare-bodied and pristine, white pants burning with ancientness, dark hair unmoving in the corpse-wind, obsidian singularity pupils fixed on his enemy, the collar of a First Lifeform resting on his chest bones above the singularity that was his and no one else’s....
He looked like something out of the first age of existence. A primal, ancient being, arrived very late, and very calm!
He punched out!
HUUM!

Existence shattered like mirrors before his fist, whole panes of it breaking and falling away, and the cracks did not stop at THE Sealed One, they extended outward, racing through the red air toward the Infinite Lifeforms and all the others behind!
BOOM!
Truly, there had been no technique in it.

Noah had instinctively moved and struck out in the most natural manner possible. He had tugged on the power of that single singularity within his existence, that Provenance Essence, and simply punched.
And the result was something even he could not have imagined.
Existence cracked!

It felt like it, and then it proved to be exactly so, as spiderweb cracks echoed outward through the air opposite him, pane after pane of reality splitting along lines that had no business existing, and the cracks did not heal and did not fade. They remained, hanging in the red sky like the aftermath of a stone through glass, frozen mid-shatter!
And the army riding the rivers of corpses had been standing in the way.

Cenozoic Scale Infinite True Lifeforms. Mesozoic Scale Infinite True Lifeforms. Beings who had climbed ladders for entire ages to stand where they stood, and every one of them caught in the spread of those cracks had their bodies split alongside existence itself!
They looked down at themselves, horrified.
Because it was not only their bodies. Their Intents cracked. Their Pantheons cracked!

Their Infinity, the silent compounding core of everything they were, took structural damage and fractured alongside their physical vessels, lines running through flesh and framework alike as though the punch had made no distinction between the two. It had not, of course. To that fist, there was no distinction worth making!
Then the leaking began.

Their Infinity seeped out through the cracks in slow ribbons of light. Their Trueness followed it, thinning into the air. Everything they had gathered across their long, acquisitive lives began escaping through fractures that would not close, and they wailed, and they screamed, and they could do nothing else!
HUUM!
They were dying! They were hit by something so unfathomably true they couldn’t help but die!
Noah took all of this in with shining eyes, and yet he could not take those eyes off one singular figure.
THE Sealed One!
The red robed vessel had cracked with all the rest. Fractures ran through its borrowed body from crown to heel, the same lines that were bleeding an army dry.
And it was stitching itself back together.

The cracks along its frame drew closed, seam by seam, unhurried, the way an old tailor mends a coat he has mended a hundred times before. Not one thread of its Trueness leaked. Not a wisp of its Intent escaped the fractured vessel!

Everything that should have poured out of a body broken that badly simply stayed, held in place by something that had clearly done this before, in more bodies than anyone would ever be permitted to count.
It was an eerie thing to watch. All around him his followers were coming apart at their seams, and the old monster quietly reassembled his own.

When he was whole, THE Sealed One drifted down and sat himself on one of the hanging cracks in existence, settling onto the broken edge of reality as though it were a garden bench. He looked at Noah with an extremely somber gaze, and his eyes moved, briefly, to the collar Noah now wore.
"Now you are becoming even more of a pain than a vessel," he said."I want you more. And yet here you are, actually ruining plans now?"
His voice was calm. Pleasant, even! And underneath the calm, one could feel the heavy anger.
Noah gazed coldly at him and clenched his fists.
He did not care what tricks the old monster had brought today. He was thinking about one thing only: how to wipe out this body of THE Sealed One, here, before it stepped back behind its curtains.
So first, he truly gazed at this being.
HUUM!

|VERITAS: 10|
|PROVENANCE: 0|
|POTENTIA: NULL|
|PONDUS: 3|

The Trueness, the VERITAS of the vessel of THE Sealed One, was exactly the same as his. Ten. So high!
Was this why its Trueness had not leaked even while cleaved?
Everything else in those cracks had bled out because everything else was borrowed, and borrowed things escape. But a being true to itself at that depth held together by definition!
The immensity, PONDUS, was lower than his at 3. And the potential displayed NULL, which was not the UNDEFINED that Anaximander’s panel had shown, and was not zero as it was hard to interpret!
THE Sealed One truly was an old monster.

As Noah looked at this being, he knew one more thing with complete certainty. THE Sealed One loved to scheme and fuck around. Every extra moment gifted to him was a moment he would spend arranging something. So Noah wanted to finish things quickly!
Which meant he had to ask himself a simple question.
How could he express his power most effectively?

He had just wiped out everything from his body. All he had was Provenance Essence. A single unit of it. A single singularity. It felt anchored into him, and he could throw its force out through his limbs, but was that it? Could he only brutely punch out to express his power?
Surely THE Provenance Lifeforms had their own ways of fighting. They generated everything themselves!

So what could he do? He wanted his Mana. He wanted his Causes. But those were old systems that others had made, and they were external, and he had cast them out for exactly that reason.So...how could he make his own?

chapters.title: Chapter 5573: MY MANA! II
paragraphs: What could he generate that would be filled with his power? That he could use to unleash his power, and have it be his? What could he replace his Mana with?
It had to be infinite. And he had to generate it!
Provenance Essence itself was too unfathomable. He could not endlessly generate more singularities. What else could...
Oh.
Oh...
BOOM!
His body shook as a pulse boomed out of him that caused the surrounding space to quiver!
He had thought of something!
And it made him feel so supremely stupid.
Something he generated. Something carrying his power. A resource he could consider Infinite!

It had been circulating through him this entire time, through every trial and every transformation, so close and so constant that he had looked straight past it while interrogating the whole of existence for an answer.
Toward the seemingly calm Sealed One bubbling with anger, Noah raised his hand.
He looked at his fingertip as the skin split open, and a crimson gold drop of blood flowed out!
HUUM!
The moment it did, a heavy and terrifying hum erupted.

Far ahead, every one of the dying Infinite Lifeforms trembled at that hum, their fractured bodies seizing all at once, as though something ancient had just exposed itself to the air for the first time in an age and their existences recognized it before their minds could!
In the next instant, their bodies exploded into puddles of blood.
An army that had ridden into this domain on rivers of the dead, reduced in one heartbeat to red stains among the red!
And THE Sealed One, seated on his crack in existence, opened his eyes wide with shock as his very existence began to buzz!
Meanwhile, Noah felt like he was in an extremely unique state.
His Blood. His Mana!
Mana was external. An ambient resource, absorbed, refined, spent. A thing one gathered from the generosity of existence and returned to it when the spell was done. But his Blood!
Oh, his blood!

He had even cast out his Marrow. Nothing borrowed remained anywhere in his veins. The blood within him now was the blood of a Provenance Lifeform, produced by remade cells that answered to nothing external, bathed from its first drop in the singular light of a Provenance Essence.
The drop at his fingertip hung there, immense crimson gold, and through its depths shone a stellar blue hue, his light, his singularity, alive inside his blood the way the sun lives inside a sea.
Noah looked at it, and he called out.
"My Blood... my Mana... Sanguine Mana... My..."
He let the last words fall silent, because some names were not for the air, and certainly not for the old monster listening from his perch.
’My Provenance Blood! My First Blood!’
HUUUM!

The moment he named it, the hum deepened, and he felt an overabundance of control flood through him, command so total it bordered on the absurd. One drop, and it answered him like a limb. He told his single drop of Sanguine Mana one thing.
Show him.
Show him its capability!
And the drop of blood popped.
Ahead of him, everything turned crimson gold!

The phenomenon that erupted was akin to countless event horizons blooming at once, an unfathomable twisting force of infinite density unfolding across the space where an army had died, dragging light and air and the hanging cracks of existence into its turning!

Crimson gold light and stellar blue swallowed everything, blindingly, wall to wall across the domain, and through it all rang a single sustained hum so vast and so ancient that even Anaximander, far behind, pressed his hands over his ears!
And by the time the light cleared...
The fractured existence ahead of Noah was covered in his blood.

It coated the frozen cracks. It sheeted across the broken air. It lay over the obsidian sands in a thin crimson gold film that shimmered with stellar blue, and Noah felt absolutely everything within it, every inch, every surface, as though the entire painted expanse were an extension of his own body and he could control everything his blood had touched.
And in the center of it stood the vessel of THE Sealed One.

Ragged and heavily injured. Its red robes torn to strips, its reassembled seams torn open again, and this time its Trueness was actually spilling out, flaking away from the wounds as red ash that drifted and dissolved. It breathed haggardly, each breath dragging, and it looked toward Noah with cold eyes as its existence visibly decayed!
Noah looked out over the crimson gold expanse where an army used to be, and he gave the thing he had just done its name.
"Sanguine Blood Drop."
HUUM!
The hum of his singularity rose to meet the naming, and Ruination’s voice bloomed into his senses, translating what his existence was declaring into clean lines he could look at and analyze.
|Your existence has made a declaration.|
|Blood has been officially designated as your Infinite Generated Resource: SANGUINE MANA.|
|SANGUINE MANA: blood generated by your remade cells, bathed in the light of your Provenance Essence. Production is generation. Generation is you. Reserves: INFINITE.|

|Properties confirmed: Sanguine Mana carries your power in full. Its potency reflects the concentration of your Provenance Essence, VERITAS and PONDUS and will rise as they rise. It answers no external authority. It cannot be adulterated, seized, or turned against you. Where it rests, you feel. Where it spreads, you command.|
|The first Provenance Art has formed.|
|PROVENANCE ART: SANGUINE BLOOD DROP.|

|A single drop of Sanguine Mana, released and detonated at your will. Capabilities: the detonation expresses twisting force of infinite density, akin to blooming event horizons, across a region you define. All things within the region caught in the detonation are subject to your power without distinction between body, framework, or authority. Residual Sanguine Mana coats the region. Coated regions become extensions of your control: you may sense all things within them, deny movement within them, and detonate them again. Drops may be scaled: one drop, many drops, or a continuous flow.Cost: nothing you will miss. You generate more with every heartbeat.|
|Note: this Art was not taught, granted, or inherited. You made it. Designation is permanent.|
Noah read the lines once, and permitted himself a single moment of satisfaction. His first Art!
Named by him, built from him!
Then he floated forward, across his own blood, toward the dying vessel of THE Sealed One.
The vessel stood in the center of the crimson gold film, decaying by the breath, its Trueness flaking off as red ash. It did not retreat. Beings like this never retreated!
