chapters.title: Chapter 5574: A Glorious Direction!
paragraphs: Noah came to a stop before it and looked at it coldly.

"I never had any issues with you," he said. "Think about that. All this time. Then you took our Lower Observable Existence, you played your long games from behind your curtains and now you’ve made me an enemy. Can you imagine? Whatever plans you had for eons, however many boards you’ve arranged, however many vessels you have folded and pressed and hung in whatever closet you keep them in. They may all just crumble. Because you happened to target the wrong guy."
HUUM!
The vessel’s ragged mouth curved. Even decaying, the voice that came out was calm, unhurried, almost warm, and the heavy anger beneath it had been pressed flatter still.

"A young thing like you can also be a unique thing, and a special thing," THE Sealed One said. "And there are many such things across existence. I have collected a few. I have discarded more. So let us not make this larger than it is. Tell you what. How about we call it quits? I will not pursue you as a vessel. I will even bear the unbearable pain of handing off that collar I planned so very many years for, the one you are wearing right now, the one you stole. Consider it a gift between professionals. I have too many things going on to designate this much focus to something like you."
The offer hung in the red air, reasonable and generous and rotten all the way through.
Noah smiled slightly.

"Now see, a me from days ago may have taken that deal," he said. "Truly. Walk away, and don’t worry about an old monster. A younger man closes that deal and sleeps well." His eyes did not warm at all as he spoke.

"But now? Ah, I’ve grown up. For me to be true, and Quintessentially me, I wouldn’t take such a deal. You do not get to reach into my life, take what is mine, hunt my people, and then buy your way back to neutral the moment the weaving turns on you. Our choices, our consequences, big boy."
He drifted closer, and the crimson gold film below them stirred like a tide sensing its moon.

"This is the first of your vessels I kill. There will be more. However many you have, wherever you have hidden them, in whatever ages you have seeded them. I will find them, and I will make each one cheaper than the last."His voice dropped, cold and even. "O ancient thing. I want you to feel afraid. I am coming for you."
"Sanguine Blood Drop."
BOOM!
Another drop of blood bloomed before Noah, crimson gold around stellar blue, and it exploded like a wave!

The detonation rolled over the vessel of THE Sealed One and eradicated it completely, body and robes and pressed-flat anger and all, scattering it into red ash that thinned and dissolved into nothing!
And this time, nothing stitched.

The wave passed on across the ruined expanse, sweeping the puddles and the stains and every last remnant of the army that had ridden in on rivers of the dead, and when it settled, the domain was clean of all of them. Nothing survived.

Slowly, the spiderweb cracks hanging in existence began to heal, panes of fractured reality drawing themselves closed seam by seam, the way a wound closes when what caused it has finally been removed. The torn pages of the sky sealed. The red light drained away.

The final domain returned, by degrees, to its ancient stillness, minus one army, one vessel, and a considerable quantity of borrowed power that had leaked out of its owners and gone wherever such things go.
Noah stood in the center of the quiet, and felt his Provenance Essence buzzing.
HUUM!
|Your Provenance Essence has increased slightly in concentration.|
|Your PONDUS has increased by +2. PONDUS: 7.|
|You were Quintessentially true to your existence. Your VERITAS elevated tremendously, but has not been able to climb past the value of 10.|
Oh?
Noah’s existence pulsed as he thought about that information.

He did not need to devour anything externally. He had just confirmed this. No corpses harvested, no essence absorbed, no boons collected from the ash. He had simply acted, truly and faithfully as who he was, and his power had increased. So long as he conducted himself as himself, the numbers would climb. That was the entire system. That had always been the entire system, and existence had needed to crush him under a falling sky before he saw it.

He just had not thought elevating the values of his four attributes would be so arduous. A slaughtered army, an eradicated vessel, an Art created from nothing, and the yield was a plus two, and a VERITAS that strained against its own value of 10 and could not pass it. Small numbers, grudgingly given!
But having numbers that were small yet meaningful was something he also liked.
After all, he had played with numbers that reached Trillions and Decillions before. The new system his existence was slowly enacting seemed much more meaningful!
Noah turned.
Anaximander had seated himself near the base of the obelisk at some point during the eradication of an army, arms resting on his knees, and he was shaking his head at his friend!
Noah took a step and appeared beside him.
"You are one ridiculous existence, you know that, right?"Anaximander said.
"I am just a human trying to grasp the wonders of existence. Just like you." Noah settled his gaze on him. "But how is the situation elsewhere? I ask because you took the Ancestral Voice within you."
Anaximander nodded slowly, and his eyes unfocused, looking at something that was not in front of him.

"It is a unique sensation. I am still grasping it. It is as if I have an eye overseeing vast stretches of THE Ymnaros, and the eye never closes, and it was never mine, and yet it reports to me now."He exhaled.

"What it reports is not good. Armies of Infinite Lifeforms are still rushing into the different domains of the Superpowered Lifeforms and waging war. The Superpowered Lifeforms are strong, but they defend homes while the invaders spend bodies. And in the largest domain of THE Ymnaros, in THE Golden Expanse, the largest army of them all has gathered. Killing the vessel of THE Sealed One does not seem to have deterred them."A pause.
"Or they simply do not know yet."
His eyes refocused, and found Noah.
"Hvitrmarr and Damodred and Ryaenara still move. Though the White Steed seems distraught." He tilted his head. "Your transformation here affected a few things?"

Noah thought about this for a moment. The bond, the mixture of Causes, the cry through it as eighteen seats emptied without a word of warning. A feeling her other half vanish out of her own existence.
"A few things that I will correct," he said. "But when it comes to dealing with the armies of Infinite Lifeforms..."
He let the sentence rest there, and pondered.

His new power. His new self! The possibilities of what he could do were, in the most literal reading his Status Panel offered, limitless. His potential was limitless. All that was left was his imagination.

He had already reclaimed Mana as his own, something he generated, and it was now his blood. In time, he would think about how Causes could also be his own, something he generated rather than seated. That was a project for a quieter hour.
But first, he had to design something grand of his own to address the immediate problem. One body, however true, could not stand in every burning domain at once.
His hand rose and touched the Collar on his chest.

It was silently resonating, humming along with his Provenance Essence in a low harmony, and through the contact he could feel the slow work underway: the unique thing was being refined by him, layer by patient layer, his essence working into bones older than every framework in existence. When his Provenance Essence actually got through to it, he would grasp its secrets. For now, it was a grand necklace on his chest, and he was entirely at peace with owning the single most coveted piece of jewelry in THE Ymnaros.
He allowed his existence to continue refining it, and turned his mind to generation.
Ideas were already buzzing. Many of them!
He selected one, opened his palm, and let the skin split.
A drop of incandescent blood rose out of his palm, crimson gold around stellar blue, and he gathered it onto the tip of his finger.
Then he began to write.

His fingertip moved through the air, and the blood followed it, laying down lines that stayed where he drew them. A runic symbol took shape stroke by stroke, and it was like no script in any catalog of existence, because it came from no catalog!

Curved lines nested inside curved lines. Rows of dots marched along the arcs in deliberate rhythms. Spirals turned inward at the joints, and every stroke was placed the way old rituals place things. He was not remembering it.He was generating it, and his hand simply knew, because the knowledge was being made in the same instant as the ink.
HUUM!
The finished rune hung in the air, humming, drinking the light.
Then it transformed.
The lines swelled and flowed outward, blood multiplying upon blood, and the rune unfolded into a figure that rose and rose until it stood titanic against the obelisk light!
It looked like Noah.
And it did not.

The face was his face, calm and cold. But the body stood far taller, broad and ancient, skin the deep crimson gold of his Sanguine Mana with ritual markings scored across it in stellar blue: spiral upon spiral down the arms, dot-lines crossing the chest in measured rows, patterns that read as ceremony older than language. Charms of pale bone hung in layered strands from its neck and wrists, and curved horn framed its shoulders beneath a great mantle that fell like a chieftain’s burden.
In its right hand it held a bloody staff, taller than itself, wet and dark with blood and crowned with a knot of the same nested spirals!

Above its head floated a crown made entirely of blood, turning slowly, never dripping. And around its whole titanic frame, streams of blood swirled in endless infinity symbols, crossing and recrossing, the oldest shape Noah owned, drawn now in the resource he would never exhaust.
|The second Provenance Art has formed.|
|PROVENANCE ART: SANGUINE SHAMANIC RUNE.|

|A rune written in Sanguine Mana that unfolds into a PROVENANCE SANGUINE CLONE. Each Clone portrays half of your power in full expression: your force, your Sanguine Mana arts, your control. Clones draw their blood from you. Your reserves are INFINITE; the cost is a formality.|

|Termination clause: if a Clone is ever destroyed, its blood does not die. It stains. The stain corrupts a region up to the measure of an Observable Existence, and within the stained region, all enemies you have designated will leak their Trueness out through their own blood. Allies are untouched. The stain does not expire.|
|Note: destroying your Clone is the least advisable way to defeat it.|
Anaximander rose to his feet and looked up at the bloody crimson gold version of his friend in its ancient adornments, and for a while he said nothing at all!
Noah spoke first.

"I will make more of these. For now, can you do what the Ancestral Voice did, and transport this one, and the others I will make, to different locations across THE Ymnaros?"His voice was even, almost administrative, as though he were arranging deliveries!
"I will finish this quickly, and see about extending my human rule here fully..."
Anaximander’s eyes pulsed as he turned to look at his friend.
He saw that it was still Noah.

And yet, looking at him now, Anaximander truly felt it. Something ancient, and far. As though his friend stood beside him and also somewhere very early, in an age before ages, and the distance between those two places was growing quietly wider every hour.
Anaximander shook his head with a wry smile, and closed his eyes.
"Understood."
An instant later, the ancient looking clone of Noah disappeared, sent somewhere across THE Ymnaros between one breath and the next.
And Noah himself stood by the obelisk with blood flowing freely from him, palms and fingertips running crimson gold, as he began to draw more bloody runes!

sentences.text: Noah came to a stop before it and looked at it coldly.
"I never had any issues with you," he said.
"Think about that.
All this time.
Then you took our Lower Observable Existence, you played your long games from behind your curtains and now you’ve made me an enemy.
Can you imagine?
Whatever plans you had for eons, however many boards you’ve arranged, however many vessels you have folded and pressed and hung in whatever closet you keep them in.
They may all just crumble.
Because you happened to target the wrong guy."
HUUM!
The vessel’s ragged mouth curved.
Even decaying, the voice that came out was calm, unhurried, almost warm, and the heavy anger beneath it had been pressed flatter still.
"A young thing like you can also be a unique thing, and a special thing," THE Sealed One said.
"And there are many such things across existence.
I have collected a few.
I have discarded more.
So let us not make this larger than it is.
Tell you what.
How about we call it quits?
I will not pursue you as a vessel.
I will even bear the unbearable pain of handing off that collar I planned so very many years for, the one you are wearing right now, the one you stole.
Consider it a gift between professionals.
I have too many things going on to designate this much focus to something like you."
The offer hung in the red air, reasonable and generous and rotten all the way through.
Noah smiled slightly.
"Now see, a me from days ago may have taken that deal," he said.
"Truly.
Walk away, and don’t worry about an old monster.
A younger man closes that deal and sleeps well." His eyes did not warm at all as he spoke.
"But now?
Ah, I’ve grown up.
For me to be true, and Quintessentially me, I wouldn’t take such a deal.
You do not get to reach into my life, take what is mine, hunt my people, and then buy your way back to neutral the moment the weaving turns on you.
Our choices, our consequences, big boy."
He drifted closer, and the crimson gold film below them stirred like a tide sensing its moon.
"This is the first of your vessels I kill.
There will be more.
However many you have, wherever you have hidden them, in whatever ages you have seeded them.
I will find them, and I will make each one cheaper than the last."His voice dropped, cold and even.
"O ancient thing.
I want you to feel afraid.
I am coming for you."
"Sanguine Blood Drop."
BOOM!
Another drop of blood bloomed before Noah, crimson gold around stellar blue, and it exploded like a wave!

The detonation rolled over the vessel of THE Sealed One and eradicated it completely, body and robes and pressed-flat anger and all, scattering it into red ash that thinned and dissolved into nothing!
And this time, nothing stitched.

The wave passed on across the ruined expanse, sweeping the puddles and the stains and every last remnant of the army that had ridden in on rivers of the dead, and when it settled, the domain was clean of all of them.
Nothing survived.

Slowly, the spiderweb cracks hanging in existence began to heal, panes of fractured reality drawing themselves closed seam by seam, the way a wound closes when what caused it has finally been removed.
The torn pages of the sky sealed.
The red light drained away.

The final domain returned, by degrees, to its ancient stillness, minus one army, one vessel, and a considerable quantity of borrowed power that had leaked out of its owners and gone wherever such things go.
Noah stood in the center of the quiet, and felt his Provenance Essence buzzing.
HUUM!
|Your Provenance Essence has increased slightly in concentration.|
|Your PONDUS has increased by +2.
PONDUS: 7.|
|You were Quintessentially true to your existence.
Your VERITAS elevated tremendously, but has not been able to climb past the value of 10.|
Oh?
Noah’s existence pulsed as he thought about that information.
He did not need to devour anything externally.
He had just confirmed this.
No corpses harvested, no essence absorbed, no boons collected from the ash.
He had simply acted, truly and faithfully as who he was, and his power had increased.
So long as he conducted himself as himself, the numbers would climb.
That was the entire system.
That had always been the entire system, and existence had needed to crush him under a falling sky before he saw it.
He just had not thought elevating the values of his four attributes would be so arduous.
A slaughtered army, an eradicated vessel, an Art created from nothing, and the yield was a plus two, and a VERITAS that strained against its own value of 10 and could not pass it.
Small numbers, grudgingly given!
But having numbers that were small yet meaningful was something he also liked.
After all, he had played with numbers that reached Trillions and Decillions before.
The new system his existence was slowly enacting seemed much more meaningful!
Noah turned.
Anaximander had seated himself near the base of the obelisk at some point during the eradication of an army, arms resting on his knees, and he was shaking his head at his friend!
Noah took a step and appeared beside him.
"You are one ridiculous existence, you know that, right?"Anaximander said.
"I am just a human trying to grasp the wonders of existence.
Just like you." Noah settled his gaze on him.
"But how is the situation elsewhere?
I ask because you took the Ancestral Voice within you."
Anaximander nodded slowly, and his eyes unfocused, looking at something that was not in front of him.
"It is a unique sensation.
I am still grasping it.
It is as if I have an eye overseeing vast stretches of THE Ymnaros, and the eye never closes, and it was never mine, and yet it reports to me now."He exhaled.
"What it reports is not good.
Armies of Infinite Lifeforms are still rushing into the different domains of the Superpowered Lifeforms and waging war.
The Superpowered Lifeforms are strong, but they defend homes while the invaders spend bodies.
And in the largest domain of THE Ymnaros, in THE Golden Expanse, the largest army of them all has gathered.
Killing the vessel of THE Sealed One does not seem to have deterred them."A pause.

chapters.title: Chapter 5575: We Follow!
paragraphs: <Ianthe Kallias>
Ianthe Kallias had carried the weight of an Observable Existence in her body since she was young, and until this war, she had believed that meant something.

The sky of THE Golden Expanse had been gold all her life. Now it ran blue and wrong, rivers of Infinity pouring through it in torrents, and beneath those torrents the invaders’ Pantheons stood unleashed across the plains, palaces and coils and hungry geometries pressing their laws down onto ground that had never obeyed anyone!
Their Intents came ahead of them like weather. Hundreds of her people held the line with their bare bodies and their exemplified weight, and the line was moving the wrong way.
She drove her fist through an Infinite Lifeform’s descending claw and felt the claw’s law try to write itself onto her bones before her weight crushed it out!
CRACK!

Beside her, old Peleus staggered, three Intents grinding against his shoulders at once. Past him, the twins fought back to back in a shrinking circle. Everywhere she looked, her people were giving ground, one stubborn step at a time, and Ianthe felt the fear she had been swallowing all day rise up her throat. Not fear for herself. Fear for all of them!
The invaders spent bodies the way rivers spend water, and her people had only the bodies they were born in.
Then... the hum arrived. A heavy and unfathomable hum!
It was simply there, underneath everything, a single sustained note so old that her body recognized it before her ears did, and her body’s opinion was terror!
Across the battlefront, thousands of beings looked up at once.
High above the breaking line, where nothing had been a heartbeat ago, something now floated.

It was titanic. It was shaped like a man, and it was the color of deep crimson gold, marked across its skin with spirals and dot-lines of burning stellar blue, hung with strands of pale bone, mantled and horned, and above its head a crown made of slowly turning blood floated without dripping!
Around its whole frame, streams of blood swirled in endless crossing loops, the same shape over and over, a symbol she would never afterward forget.
She could not have said what it was. Nobody on that field could. Understanding was not offered!

Its aura pressed down, and Ianthe’s knees nearly went. This thing had come to their side of the war, she could feel that much in the way its weight fell only forward, onto the invaders, and still her hands shook.
It was the dread of standing near something out of the first age of existence, ancient beyond the weavings of ages, and the dread did not ease when she told herself it was rescue!
The Infinite Lifeforms received it truly.

Their formations had already stopped. Rivers of Infinity faltered mid-pour. Beings who had spent the day as executioners now hung motionless in the silver air, and Ianthe watched creatures wearing Cenozoic weight begin, visibly, to shake.
The floating figure raised its staff.
At the staff’s crowned tip, a single drop of blood formed. Crimson gold, with a stellar blue light living in its depths. One drop, above a battlefront that stretched past the horizon’s patience!
The drop popped.
HUUM!
The battlefront ahead of her ceased to be a place.

Everything the invaders held turned crimson gold at once, event horizons blooming across the plains in their uncounted numbers, twisting light and law and Pantheon-palaces into themselves with a force that made Ianthe’s exemplified body feel like a leaf pressed in a book!

The hum became a roar and became a pressure that bent the world’s edges inward, and through it she saw the Infinite Lifeforms crack like vessels, their hoarded Infinity leaking out in ribbons, their bodies coming apart into red!
BOOM!

When the light thinned, the plains were painted. A film of crimson gold lay across the ruined ground where the invading army’s forward strength had stood, shimmering with blue, and nothing that had ridden in on those rivers moved anywhere upon it. The rivers themselves were gone. The unleashed Pantheons were gone!
The pressure of a hundred foreign Intents was gone, and its absence rang louder than any of it.
The war in THE Golden Expanse was not over. Ianthe could feel the rest of the invasion out beyond the horizon, vast and undeterred, still arriving.
But the field before her was finished.

And the being that had finished it did not chase, and did not speak, and did not land. It simply floated there above its own blood, grand and unhurried, arms loose at its sides, the crown turning over its head and the endless loops of blood crossing and recrossing around it, letting itself be seen at full length by every survivor of both sides, as though being witnessed were itself part of the work.
Then, slowly, it turned toward the horizon, where the rest of the war was waiting!
Ianthe rose from her knees, and she watched.

There was nothing else to be done with what was happening in the sky. The titanic crimson gold being drifted out from the cleared battlefront, unhurried, the crown of blood turning above its head, and where it went, the war simply ended.
She saw it stop above the burning reaches east of the plains, where the blue rivers had been pouring. It raised its staff!
One drop of blood formed at the tip, crimson gold around a heart of stellar blue, and Ianthe braced herself this time, and the bracing did nothing at all.
BOOM!

The east turned crimson gold from earth to sky, event horizons blooming through the invaders’ ranks, and every single Infinite Lifeform within that region cracked, leaked, and collapsed into red. Not most of them. Every one!
Then the being drifted on, south, to the shattered terraces where the twins’ home had stood, and did it again. One drop!
Just one drop of blood!

Then the high passes. One drop. Then the coast of the golden sea, where the largest mass of the invasion had gathered its Pantheons into a fortress of stacked laws, and Ianthe thought, surely, here it will need more!
And yet still...
One drop was all it required.
BOOM!
She did not know what this lifeform was. No one on the field knew what it was!

But her people were already speaking of it in low voices between the drops, and a name was forming out of nothing, because beings must call a thing something or go mad looking at it. The crown gave them the word. By the fourth region, Ianthe heard old Peleus murmur it, and realized she had been thinking it for some time.
The Blood-Crowned One.
It was not a grand name. It was simply true!

Region by region, drop by drop, the Blood-Crowned One unmade the invasion of THE Golden Expanse. There was no battle in any of it. A single ridiculous thing happened: every Infinite Lifeform, cleared out and completely collapsed, until the rivers ran nowhere in any sky she could see, and the last foreign Intent guttered out of the air like a lamp pinched between fingers!
And then THE Golden Expanse was entirely cleared.
A heavy silence fell upon it.
It was the first true silence in longer than Ianthe could count. No rivers pouring. No Pantheons grinding their laws against the ground. No screaming, hers or theirs.
Just the wind moving over ruined gold plains slicked in crimson, and hundreds upon hundreds of Superpowered Lifeforms standing in the wreckage of everything, slowly raising their heads.
Every single one of them looked up.
The Blood-Crowned One floated at the center of the sky, staff loose in its grip, the loops of blood turning endlessly around its frame.
Then it spoke.
"I will lead you."
BOOM!
The voice was ancient and booming and everywhere at once, arriving in the chest before the ears, and Ianthe flinched, and could not look away.
It did not even seem like a request!
There was no question mark living anywhere inside those words. The being was not offering. It was telling them what it would do, the way the sky tells the ground it will rain!

"For ages, you have been defending against an onslaught of enemies,"the voice rolled on, slow and vast. "Age after age, they have come for your homes, and age after age, you have held your lines with your bare bodies, and buried your dead, again, and again, and again. No more."
The staff turned, once, unhurried.
"I, THE True Human Emperor, will lead you."
A pause came, in which the whole of THE Golden Expanse seemed to hang from a thread.
"Will you follow?"
HUUM!

The hum swelled beneath the words, ancient and enormous, and the oppressive silence that followed was the heaviest thing Ianthe had ever stood under, heavier than the Observable Existence she carried in her body, because this weight asked something of her!
Her emotions would not settle into any single shape.
His words about her people resonated in her bones. Dying age after age. Burying the dead again and again!
That was her mother, and her mother’s line, and old Peleus’s four sons, and every golden field she had ever seen churned to mud and red!
He was right!

And at the same time, she was afraid of him. Deeply. He had asked nothing of them before saving them. He had wiped out the very enemies that were butchering them, armies of Infinite Lifeforms, whole invasions, with single drops of blood, and power like that did not need their consent for anything, and yet here it floated, waiting for their answer.
But beneath the fear, and beneath the awe, there was something else. And it was actually fairly simple.
She was tired. She was so tired of the cycles of death.
And this fearsome being that none of them could understand had protected them. If he could continue to do so...

Ianthe Kallias stepped forward over the ruined ground, the first body to move up in all of THE Golden Expanse. She put her hand on her chest, over the weight she had carried since she was young, and she raised her voice to the sky.
"We follow!"
HUUM!
She was a single lone voice in a silence the size of a domain!
But she was the first. And how she thought was how many just like her thought!

Old Peleus rose from beside his dead, put his hand on his chest, and said it. The twins rose together, hands on their chests. Then the line she had fought beside all day, then the survivors of the terraces, then voices from the passes and the coast, Superpowered Lifeforms rising one after another out of the wreckage across the whole golden breadth of the domain, hands over hearts.
"We follow!"
"We follow!"
It became a phenomenon!

All those within THE Golden Expanse looked up as they said it. Some of them said it holding the corpses of their families in their arms. Some said it kneeling, too injured to stand, pain written across their faces as they looked around at the devastation of everything they had built, and then looked up, past all of it, toward the fearsome being promising to lead them.
Their voices rose and joined and rose again, hundreds becoming a single sound rolling across the cleared plains, grief and exhaustion and hope all speaking the same two words!
"WE FOLLOW!"
The Blood-Crowned One looked down upon all of it, the crown turning slowly above its head.
And it gave them its last words.
"I will lead you towards an age of humanity, and empowerment. Towards an age where those who butchered you... will fear even standing before your shadows."
The words burned through Ianthe and many others!

Her blood boiled. There was no gentler way to name it. Because what better emotion was there to rouse up, if not revenge? They had been prey for so long that she had forgotten there was another way to stand!
Those who butchered them, afraid of their shadows!

Ianthe threw her head back and roared, and around her, THE Golden Expanse roared with her, hundreds of voices tearing loose at once with a fervor that shook the crimson from the ruined ground, louder than the war had ever been!
"WE FOLLOW!"
HUUM!

And the being that had finished it did not chase, and did not speak, and did not land.

It simply floated there above its own blood, grand and unhurried, arms loose at its sides, the crown turning over its head and the endless loops of blood crossing and recrossing around it, letting itself be seen at full length by every survivor of both sides, as though being witnessed were itself part of the work.
Then, slowly, it turned toward the horizon, where the rest of the war was waiting!
Ianthe rose from her knees, and she watched.
There was nothing else to be done with what was happening in the sky.
The titanic crimson gold being drifted out from the cleared battlefront, unhurried, the crown of blood turning above its head, and where it went, the war simply ended.
She saw it stop above the burning reaches east of the plains, where the blue rivers had been pouring.
It raised its staff!
One drop of blood formed at the tip, crimson gold around a heart of stellar blue, and Ianthe braced herself this time, and the bracing did nothing at all.
BOOM!
The east turned crimson gold from earth to sky, event horizons blooming through the invaders’ ranks, and every single Infinite Lifeform within that region cracked, leaked, and collapsed into red.
Not most of them.
Every one!
Then the being drifted on, south, to the shattered terraces where the twins’ home had stood, and did it again.
One drop!
Just one drop of blood!
Then the high passes.
One drop.
Then the coast of the golden sea, where the largest mass of the invasion had gathered its Pantheons into a fortress of stacked laws, and Ianthe thought, surely, here it will need more!
And yet still...
One drop was all it required.
BOOM!
She did not know what this lifeform was.
No one on the field knew what it was!
But her people were already speaking of it in low voices between the drops, and a name was forming out of nothing, because beings must call a thing something or go mad looking at it.
The crown gave them the word.
By the fourth region, Ianthe heard old Peleus murmur it, and realized she had been thinking it for some time.
The Blood-Crowned One.
It was not a grand name.
It was simply true!
Region by region, drop by drop, the Blood-Crowned One unmade the invasion of THE Golden Expanse.
There was no battle in any of it.

A single ridiculous thing happened: every Infinite Lifeform, cleared out and completely collapsed, until the rivers ran nowhere in any sky she could see, and the last foreign Intent guttered out of the air like a lamp pinched between fingers!
And then THE Golden Expanse was entirely cleared.
A heavy silence fell upon it.
It was the first true silence in longer than Ianthe could count.
No rivers pouring.
No Pantheons grinding their laws against the ground.
No screaming, hers or theirs.
Just the wind moving over ruined gold plains slicked in crimson, and hundreds upon hundreds of Superpowered Lifeforms standing in the wreckage of everything, slowly raising their heads.
Every single one of them looked up.
The Blood-Crowned One floated at the center of the sky, staff loose in its grip, the loops of blood turning endlessly around its frame.
Then it spoke.
"I will lead you."
BOOM!
The voice was ancient and booming and everywhere at once, arriving in the chest before the ears, and Ianthe flinched, and could not look away.
It did not even seem like a request!
There was no question mark living anywhere inside those words.
The being was not offering.
It was telling them what it would do, the way the sky tells the ground it will rain!
"For ages, you have been defending against an onslaught of enemies,"the voice rolled on, slow and vast.
"Age after age, they have come for your homes, and age after age, you have held your lines with your bare bodies, and buried your dead, again, and again, and again.
No more."
The staff turned, once, unhurried.
"I, THE True Human Emperor, will lead you."
A pause came, in which the whole of THE Golden Expanse seemed to hang from a thread.
"Will you follow?"
HUUM!

The hum swelled beneath the words, ancient and enormous, and the oppressive silence that followed was the heaviest thing Ianthe had ever stood under, heavier than the Observable Existence she carried in her body, because this weight asked something of her!
Her emotions would not settle into any single shape.
His words about her people resonated in her bones.
Dying age after age.
Burying the dead again and again!
That was her mother, and her mother’s line, and old Peleus’s four sons, and every golden field she had ever seen churned to mud and red!
He was right!
And at the same time, she was afraid of him.
Deeply.
He had asked nothing of them before saving them.

He had wiped out the very enemies that were butchering them, armies of Infinite Lifeforms, whole invasions, with single drops of blood, and power like that did not need their consent for anything, and yet here it floated, waiting for their answer.
But beneath the fear, and beneath the awe, there was something else.
And it was actually fairly simple.
She was tired.
She was so tired of the cycles of death.
And this fearsome being that none of them could understand had protected them.
If he could continue to do so...
Ianthe Kallias stepped forward over the ruined ground, the first body to move up in all of THE Golden Expanse.
She put her hand on her chest, over the weight she had carried since she was young, and she raised her voice to the sky.
"We follow!"
HUUM!
She was a single lone voice in a silence the size of a domain!
But she was the first.
And how she thought was how many just like her thought!
Old Peleus rose from beside his dead, put his hand on his chest, and said it.
The twins rose together, hands on their chests.

Then the line she had fought beside all day, then the survivors of the terraces, then voices from the passes and the coast, Superpowered Lifeforms rising one after another out of the wreckage across the whole golden breadth of the domain, hands over hearts.
"We follow!"
"We follow!"
It became a phenomenon!
All those within THE Golden Expanse looked up as they said it.
Some of them said it holding the corpses of their families in their arms.

Some said it kneeling, too injured to stand, pain written across their faces as they looked around at the devastation of everything they had built, and then looked up, past all of it, toward the fearsome being promising to lead them.
Their voices rose and joined and rose again, hundreds becoming a single sound rolling across the cleared plains, grief and exhaustion and hope all speaking the same two words!
"WE FOLLOW!"
The Blood-Crowned One looked down upon all of it, the crown turning slowly above its head.
And it gave them its last words.
"I will lead you towards an age of humanity, and empowerment.
Towards an age where those who butchered you... will fear even standing before your shadows."
The words burned through Ianthe and many others!
Her blood boiled.
There was no gentler way to name it.
Because what better emotion was there to rouse up, if not revenge?
They had been prey for so long that she had forgotten there was another way to stand!
Those who butchered them, afraid of their shadows!

Ianthe threw her head back and roared, and around her, THE Golden Expanse roared with her, hundreds of voices tearing loose at once with a fervor that shook the crimson from the ruined ground, louder than the war had ever been!
"WE FOLLOW!"
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5576: Stability!
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
Noah stood by the obelisk with his eyes closed, and he was also standing in a dozen other places.

His senses ran through every Provenance Sanguine Clone at once, shared fully, a single awareness wearing many titanic bodies across the breadth of THE Ymnaros, and what that awareness observed was the same short story with different scenery!
No Infinite True Lifeform stood against even a single Sanguine Blood Drop.

Not the Cenozoic ones anchoring invasion spearheads. Not the patient ones hanging back behind their stacked Pantheons. Not the desperate ones who saw the crimson gold figure arrive and threw everything they had hoarded across their long lives at it before the staff could rise!
One drop formed. One drop popped. And rivers of Infinity went silent in one region after another, armies collapsing into red, until whole stretches of THE Ymnaros held no invaders at all!
And in THE Golden Expanse, the grandest of them, his clone had done something else besides.

Through its eyes he had looked out over the cleared plains at thousands of Superpowered Lifeforms rising from their ruins. And past them, sheltered in the heart of the domain, he had seen the grand sprawling citadel that the Superpowered Lifeforms had been defending all this time, tier upon golden tier of it, and the millions of humans within its walls pressed onto every balcony and rampart to see the sky!
His clone had told all of them that he would lead them!
And as they looked up, one after another after another, and pledged themselves to him...
HUUM!
|You have increased the stability of a small localized portion of Existence. Your Provenance Essence has increased significantly in concentration.|
|Your PONDUS has increased by +.5. PONDUS: 7.5|

|You were Quintessentially true to your existence and have increased the stability of a small localized portion of Existence. Your VERITAS elevated tremendously,but has not been able to climb past the value of 10.|
He had received similar prompts not long before, and he visibly felt his power increase as these ones settled, the hum in his depths thickening by a degree that his whole body registered.
But the most important thing was not the numbers. The most important thing was what his existence had communicated to him about the cause.
He had increased the stability of a localized portion of Existence!
And he could feel his existence was fortifying, and deep within him his singularity of Provenance Essence was growing larger and larger in concentration, denser and brighter.
And the growth was his to generate, but due to his actions bringing about the stability of existence itself!
Such a thing interested him greatly.
How were THE First Lifeforms connected to the stability of existence itself?

Everywhere he had ever traveled, existence ran on boundless chaos. Entropy only increased over time. Lifeforms always fought, wars churned realms into dust, and every framework ever built was a temporary argument against a disorder that always, eventually, won the argument.
And yet it seemed the earliest lifeforms, or truly the first lifeforms, became stronger by cutting against that disorder. Their power grew from their own existence generating more of themselves!
He sighed and opened his eyes, and turned to Anaximander beside him.
The scholar nodded to him.
"Everything around THE Ymnaros is stable. We can have a moment to breathe, somewhat."
Noah nodded back, and looked down at the collar on his chest.
He wanted to use his own moment of breathing to take a proper look at this ridiculous cluster of bones of a First Lifeform.

How did it come about? Why would an existence so supremely powerful carve out its own bones and make them into a necklace? Beings hoarded power. Beings defended their bodies above all things. And this one had reached into its own chest and shaped what it found there into an ornament, and left the ornament behind for the ages to kill each other over.

And the more he thought about it, the more special the Superpowered Lifeforms became. Their power, their exemplification, the whole strange lineage of authority-less might that filled this Dimension, traced its origins back to the Panaceas. And the Panaceas actually stemmed from this very necklace, its runoff, its residue, pooling in wells across THE Ymnaros for others to drink.
THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity!
The First Purity now made sense in its name. He simply had to figure out the rest!
And while he did that, there was also his own newly changed existence to attend to. He needed to generate his own system of power, piece by piece, because he had cast out far too many things.
There were weavings he would have to alter as well. The Causes of the First Steed. Potentially the Laestrygonian too, Damodred, bound to him by structures that no longer had anything to bind to.
He would continue to experiment, and see exactly what path he would forge. A path that would be genuinely his, and nobody else’s, from here on out!
One of the bigger puzzles for him to solve remained the Causes.
THE Infiniverse was filled with them, thousands of realms turning on them.

Even one of Those Who Remain, THE Sleepless Fiend, was playing around with Causes in an entire Dimension. Well, really, in multiple Dimensions, if the Laestrygonians were included in the counting. Causes sat beneath everything he had ever climbed, and everything he intended to rule.
He had to generate something of his own that took the place of Causes.
And as he thought of this...
WAA!
Space folded open on the dark sands of what used to be the domain of the final trial, and three figures stepped through, delivered by the scholar’s quiet courtesy at Noah’s earlier request.
Hvitrmarr. Damodred. Ryaenara!

The White Steed came in her humanoid form, white-haired and gold-eyed, the ring pupils fixed on Noah the moment the fold released her. Damodred stood at her flank, and Ryaenara a step apart, and all three of them looked toward Noah with complex gazes, each carrying their own thoughts across the sand.
Hvitrmarr, who had felt her newly established bond dissipate out of her existence.
Damodred, who was bound to Noah, and who now sensed no Causes on him at all!
And Ryaenara.
Noah looked at this woman, vibrant and grand, and a silent thought arose within him.
He may actually be able to cure her little brother.

chapters.title: Chapter 5577: NOBLESSE! I
paragraphs: With a bit of breathing room, many things could be done without rushing!
Noah crossed the sand to Hvitrmarr first, and caught her shoulder before her knee could touch the ground.

"None of that,"he said quietly. "The bond you felt leave was one more borrowed thing I had to set down. It was never you I set down. I told you I would be your Rider, and I will continue to be your Rider. Soon, something better than what we had will bloom, okay?"
The White Steed’s gold eyes searched his face. She straightened, and the distress she had carried finally loosened its grip on her frame, and she stayed close to him!
He then looked at Damodred.

"With the power I have now, I should have something grander than Causes soon enough," Noah said."I will see if I can easily find the genetic markers of Laestrygonians, and bring more of your brethren back."
The Laestrygonian went very still! His people, eradicated by THE Sleepless Fiend, existing now as one survivor bound to one man!
Damodred bowed his head deeply.
"I follow The Master completely,"he said, "and await your continued glory."
Noah then turned to Ryaenara.
He chose his words carefully.
"I don’t want to make any promises. But... we can try to see if curing your Brother is a possibility right now."
BOOM!
The words landed on her like a detonation! Her body trembled, her composure cracking as her eyes shone with unfathomable hope as she surged a step forward!
"Can we... can we go right now? He is in my Dimension, as we ca... GAH!"
Even before she finished her words, she spat crimson blood.
It was not ordinary blood! It came out shining with her Trueness, threads of her very existence leaving with it, and then, shockingly, her chest split open, and out of the wound erupted faces!
Hateful, roaring faces, pressing up out of her flesh in a snarling cluster, screaming without sound!
OOOOH!
Noah frowned and was instantly at her side, his hands grasping her shoulders, his senses driving down into her existence, and he quickly understood what was happening.
HUUM!
|Analysis of the existence: RYAENARA.|

|A bond of following was established between this existence and THE Sealed One in ages past. However much of a double agent this existence believed herself to be, serving and not serving, the initial bond she formed was filled with weavings even she could not understand, layered beneath her perception at the moment of its making.|

|Through those hidden weavings, THE Sealed One has grasped the Lifeline of her existence and cursed it with deterioration. Her Trueness and her Intent are already infected. Her Lifeline is bound over to collapse.|
|Designation of the curse: THE Hollowing Chorus of the Forfeited Lifeline.|
|She is marked for death.|
Noah looked at the prompts with heavy eyes.

The old monster still could not be underestimated. Killed in one body an hour ago, and reaching out as he must have perceived something regarding Ryaenara! After all, she was in THE Ymnaros where THE Sealed One just faced a catastrophic loss of THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity!
But for someone to be marked for death?
Noah’s voice tyrannically boomed out!
"I won’t allow it."
BOOM!
He moved with immensity. Ryaenara was still convulsing in his grip, vomiting blood and Trueness in gouts now, and she was crying, and even dying she spent her words on someone else.
"Ulf, please save Ulf! Enter my Dimension before it collap... GAAH!"

She spat out more blood, and her teeth fell out with it, scattering white against the dark sand, and her body began sagging toward the ground as the roaring faces on her chest howled their silent howl!
Noah focused.
Time seemingly slowed before his perception, thinning and thinning until it was no longer even moving, the domain caught in a single stretched instant with her blood hanging mid-air between them.
A blood drop appeared on his fingertip.

He thought for a moment, whole architectures of reasoning assembling and collapsing and reassembling. The curse held her Lifeline, and her Lifeline sat threaded through the frameworks of existence, and anything threaded through frameworks could be gripped by things older and crueler than her.
He would continue to lean on his Infinite Sanguine Mana as the solution!
And right now, he was making another Art.

His fingertip began to carve, and this rune was unlike the shamanic rune, deeper and slower, waves and strings coming together within his blood as he drew, strand weaving into strand. The Letters of THE Osmontian Tongue flowed into its construction, I AM and OSMONT and HUMAN pressed into the turning lines, and beneath the Letters something even more ancient moved through the strokes, a texture that belonged to the age his blood now remembered, and the finished rune hung in the stopped air like a seal from before the first framework was ever raised!
Time resumed.
The rune flowed into Ryaenara.
HUUM!
|The third Provenance Art has formed.|
|PROVENANCE ART: THE PROVENANCE BLOOD MARK.|
|A mark carved of Sanguine Mana, THE Osmontian Tongue, and that which came before frameworks. It is placed upon a select few chosen existence, and it is irreversible.|

|The marked existence has its Lifeline and its entire Existence fully bound to you. Their fate is lost from all Scales and all frameworks: no instrument of existence may weigh them, no authority of existence may grip them, and no thread of theirs remains for any hand but yours. They follow you, fully, from the moment of marking onward.|
|In exchange, their Potential is elevated grandly.The marked become NOBLESSE BLOOD APOSTLES.|

|NOBLESSE BLOOD APOSTLES manifest in five tiers of rarity, determined by the potential of the one marked.From the least to the rarest: BLOOD KNIGHT, BLOOD BARON, BLOOD DUKE, BLOOD MONARCH, BLOOD SOVEREIGN.The rarer the Apostle, the grander the attributes their existence may carry.|
The effects on Ryaenara were immediate!

She started trembling even harder, gushes of dark blood erupting from her, old blood, wrong blood, everything the curse had touched being driven out of her at once, and the hateful faces on her chest reared and cried out as the mark’s authority closed over them!
And yet, her Trueness stopped leaking.
The shining threads that had been escaping with every cough drew back into her, held fast, and then she transformed.

The dark blood burned away off her skin. Her hair poured down glossy obsidian, blacker and deeper than it had ever been, catching the obelisk light like still water at night. Her eyes opened, and the pupils within them burned bloody red, and behind the red turned a quiet light of infinity, depth without end!
Red gold robes wrapped around her out of nothing, layered and regal, settling onto her shoulders with the weight of a station rather than a garment.
The roaring faces gave one last soundless howl, and dissolved.
|The curse THE Hollowing Chorus of the Forfeited Lifeline has been destroyed.|

|Cause of destruction: the curse was anchored through the frameworks of existence, gripping a Lifeline threaded within them. The marked existence of RYAENARA no longer resides within any Scale or framework. There is nothing remaining for the curse to hold. Her Lifeline answers to one authority alone, and that authority cannot be weighed or touched by the instruments of THE Sealed One.|
|As of this moment, her existence is without any Scales or framework.|
|RYAENARA has become a Noblesse Blood Apostle of the fourth tier: BLOOD BARON.|
WAA!
Ryaenara stood whole in her red gold robes, and her crimson eyes burned with nobility and wonder as she looked at Noah.
Then she instantly knelt before him.

It was nothing like the kneel of a defeated thing. Her back was straight, her head lifted, her reverent eyes raised to him as if she were looking at a distant and grand lifeform across an impossible span, and her voice came out grandly, formal in a way Ryaenara had never once been formal in all the time he had known her!
"Thank you for the generosity, Master. Command me, and I will move existence for you!"
HUUM!
Noah looked at her oddly.
He had not expected such a heavy change!
Did his blood have such a heavy effect when he did this?
"Are you... still you?"
"I am Ryaenara, your Apostle, from this point on in existence."
"What... do you want?"
"If Master can grant my Brother the same favor as me, I would be grateful."Her crimson eyes did not waver.
"He would also be of much more use to you, with his gaze being capable of reaching into the future."
She was still her. The first thing she wanted was still Ulf, before power, before anything. But different!
Noah affirmed this as he looked at her deeply, his gaze reaching into her remade existence.
|STATUS PANEL: RYAENARA- NOBLESSE BLOOD APOSTLE, BLOOD BARON|
|VERITAS: 1|
|PROVENANCE: 0|
|POTENTIA: 5|
|PONDUS: 2|
He took the panel in, and nodded.
He had changed her into a grand lifeform, unmoored from every Scale and framework in existence, her potential elevated to a value that stood beside numbers he had bled for!
And it seemed she would only be the first.
Because nearby, Hvitrmarr and Damodred had both kneeled down onto the dark sand, heads bowed, as if they were waiting for the same thing!

After all, she was in THE Ymnaros where THE Sealed One just faced a catastrophic loss of THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity!
But for someone to be marked for death?
Noah’s voice tyrannically boomed out!
"I won’t allow it."
BOOM!
He moved with immensity.
Ryaenara was still convulsing in his grip, vomiting blood and Trueness in gouts now, and she was crying, and even dying she spent her words on someone else.
"Ulf, please save Ulf!
Enter my Dimension before it collap...
GAAH!"

She spat out more blood, and her teeth fell out with it, scattering white against the dark sand, and her body began sagging toward the ground as the roaring faces on her chest howled their silent howl!
Noah focused.
Time seemingly slowed before his perception, thinning and thinning until it was no longer even moving, the domain caught in a single stretched instant with her blood hanging mid-air between them.
A blood drop appeared on his fingertip.
He thought for a moment, whole architectures of reasoning assembling and collapsing and reassembling.
The curse held her Lifeline, and her Lifeline sat threaded through the frameworks of existence, and anything threaded through frameworks could be gripped by things older and crueler than her.
He would continue to lean on his Infinite Sanguine Mana as the solution!
And right now, he was making another Art.
His fingertip began to carve, and this rune was unlike the shamanic rune, deeper and slower, waves and strings coming together within his blood as he drew, strand weaving into strand.

The Letters of THE Osmontian Tongue flowed into its construction, I AM and OSMONT and HUMAN pressed into the turning lines, and beneath the Letters something even more ancient moved through the strokes, a texture that belonged to the age his blood now remembered, and the finished rune hung in the stopped air like a seal from before the first framework was ever raised!
Time resumed.
The rune flowed into Ryaenara.
HUUM!
|The third Provenance Art has formed.|
|PROVENANCE ART: THE PROVENANCE BLOOD MARK.|
|A mark carved of Sanguine Mana, THE Osmontian Tongue, and that which came before frameworks.
It is placed upon a select few chosen existence, and it is irreversible.|
|The marked existence has its Lifeline and its entire Existence fully bound to you.
Their fate is lost from all Scales and all frameworks: no instrument of existence may weigh them, no authority of existence may grip them, and no thread of theirs remains for any hand but yours.
They follow you, fully, from the moment of marking onward.|
|In exchange, their Potential is elevated grandly.The marked become NOBLESSE BLOOD APOSTLES.|

|NOBLESSE BLOOD APOSTLES manifest in five tiers of rarity, determined by the potential of the one marked.From the least to the rarest: BLOOD KNIGHT, BLOOD BARON, BLOOD DUKE, BLOOD MONARCH, BLOOD SOVEREIGN.The rarer the Apostle, the grander the attributes their existence may carry.|
The effects on Ryaenara were immediate!

She started trembling even harder, gushes of dark blood erupting from her, old blood, wrong blood, everything the curse had touched being driven out of her at once, and the hateful faces on her chest reared and cried out as the mark’s authority closed over them!
And yet, her Trueness stopped leaking.
The shining threads that had been escaping with every cough drew back into her, held fast, and then she transformed.
The dark blood burned away off her skin.
Her hair poured down glossy obsidian, blacker and deeper than it had ever been, catching the obelisk light like still water at night.
Her eyes opened, and the pupils within them burned bloody red, and behind the red turned a quiet light of infinity, depth without end!
Red gold robes wrapped around her out of nothing, layered and regal, settling onto her shoulders with the weight of a station rather than a garment.
The roaring faces gave one last soundless howl, and dissolved.
|The curse THE Hollowing Chorus of the Forfeited Lifeline has been destroyed.|
|Cause of destruction: the curse was anchored through the frameworks of existence, gripping a Lifeline threaded within them.
The marked existence of RYAENARA no longer resides within any Scale or framework.
There is nothing remaining for the curse to hold.
Her Lifeline answers to one authority alone, and that authority cannot be weighed or touched by the instruments of THE Sealed One.|
|As of this moment, her existence is without any Scales or framework.|
|RYAENARA has become a Noblesse Blood Apostle of the fourth tier: BLOOD BARON.|
WAA!
Ryaenara stood whole in her red gold robes, and her crimson eyes burned with nobility and wonder as she looked at Noah.
Then she instantly knelt before him.
It was nothing like the kneel of a defeated thing.

Her back was straight, her head lifted, her reverent eyes raised to him as if she were looking at a distant and grand lifeform across an impossible span, and her voice came out grandly, formal in a way Ryaenara had never once been formal in all the time he had known her!
"Thank you for the generosity, Master.
Command me, and I will move existence for you!"
HUUM!
Noah looked at her oddly.
He had not expected such a heavy change!
Did his blood have such a heavy effect when he did this?
"Are you... still you?"
"I am Ryaenara, your Apostle, from this point on in existence."
"What... do you want?"
"If Master can grant my Brother the same favor as me, I would be grateful."Her crimson eyes did not waver.
"He would also be of much more use to you, with his gaze being capable of reaching into the future."
She was still her.
The first thing she wanted was still Ulf, before power, before anything.
But different!
Noah affirmed this as he looked at her deeply, his gaze reaching into her remade existence.
|STATUS PANEL: RYAENARA- NOBLESSE BLOOD APOSTLE, BLOOD BARON|
|VERITAS: 1|
|PROVENANCE: 0|
|POTENTIA: 5|
|PONDUS: 2|
He took the panel in, and nodded.
He had changed her into a grand lifeform, unmoored from every Scale and framework in existence, her potential elevated to a value that stood beside numbers he had bled for!
And it seemed she would only be the first.
Because nearby, Hvitrmarr and Damodred had both kneeled down onto the dark sand, heads bowed, as if they were waiting for the same thing!

chapters.title: Chapter 5578: NOBLESSE! II
paragraphs: "What the hell did you just do? And how?"
Anaximander had come up behind Noah, and he was staring at Ryaenara with open marvel!
He could sense the complete change of her existence, and it was not a change of degree. Her weavings did not read as elevated, or healed, or empowered. They read as absent!
A being stood before him, undeniably present, radiating quiet crimson nobility, and every instrument of perception he owned reported that she did not display much immenisty at all.
Noah was already walking toward Hvitrmarr, a fresh drop of blood rising to his fingertip.
"My existence has begun living truly as myself,"he said, beginning to draw. The rune took form stroke by patient stroke, waves and strings gathering in the blood.

"Everything I do now comes from that. I am using my blood as a resource to alter existence itself, because my blood carries everything I am, and I am no longer something existence gets a say in. This time in particular, it is the alteration of one’s Lifeline."
WAA!
The rune turned slowly in the air before the kneeling White Steed, and he began a second one beside it, for the Laestrygonian, speaking as he carved.

"I’ve begun thinking of a Lifeline as a thread. Spun for you at your beginning and woven into frameworks you never chose, by hands you will never see. Every Scale that measures you holds that thread. Every authority that curses you grips it. Every framework that promises you power is also a loom that owns your weave. Beings spend their whole existences climbing ladders with this preset notion..."His fingertip finished a spiral of joined strands.
"My Mark cuts the thread free of every framework. Your Lifeline leaves the frameworks entirely, and binds to me instead. Simple enough."
Simple enough! Oh, so simple!
He looked between the two kneeling figures.
"This does change you bindings to fully be...behind me."
Neither of them moved from their knees.
Noah nodded once, and released the runes.
HUUM!
The two marks flowed into them, and the transformations began.

Hvitrmarr rose off the sand as her humanoid form dissolved outward into her true one, the colossal white dragon unfurling against the obelisk light, and then the Mark’s authority moved through her from Lifeline to scale-tips!

Her pearl white body deepened and glossed, alabaster taking on an undertone of living crimson, as though her whiteness now ran above a tide of blood. Her wing membranes thinned and cleared into sheets of red gold, light passing through them the way it passes through stained glass in an old hall. Her twin spiral ivory horns banded themselves in rings of red gold, her mane of white flame threaded through with ribbons of crimson fire, and along her jaw the elegant line of her fangs lengthened, refined, predatory, the mouth of something that drinks its conquests rather than merely winning them!
When her eyes opened, the gold ring pupils burned with a new center: bloody red, and behind the red, a quiet turning light of infinity.
She was still the White Steed. She was now also, unmistakably, something more magisterial!
And Damodred!

The Laestrygonian...his proportions loosened at their edges, joints suggesting themselves in numbers the eye declined to count, his silhouette gaining a margin of half-present limbs that existed mainly in the corner of one’s perception and withdrew when looked at directly.

The ancient blindfold of hands across his face changed first and most: every hand of it turned bloody crimson gold, fingers lengthening, and then the whole lattice of them opened outward from the center like a terrible flower.
And at the very center, revealed, a single cyclops eye burned.

Its iris was vast and dark. Its pupil was red, and the red was not a shape but a congregation: countless minute hands, joining and rejoining, clasped into the form of a pupil that flexed when it moved. The eye swept the domain once, and the domain felt swept!
|The marked existence of HVITRMARR presents a unique transformation.|

|While all that you carried was cast out, her Causes were never carried. They are part of her existence itself, seated within her organs, born into her flesh by the hands of Those Who Remain. They cannot be removed from her, and so they are transforming WITH her.|

|Her nine Causes are becoming her own: unthreaded from the frameworks that seated them, remaking themselves within her organs under your authority. The process is ongoing. Their transformation may provide weavings of what your own Causes could be.|
|HVITRMARR has become a Noblesse Blood Apostle of the third tier: BLOOD DUKE.|
|DAMODRED has become a Noblesse Blood Apostle of the third tier: BLOOD DUKE.|
Noah read the prompt about her organs twice, and set it carefully into the front of his mind, beside the Cause-replacement puzzle it had just illuminated!
The two finished beings bowed to him, dragon and Laestrygonian, and he checked their status panels as they did.
|STATUS PANEL: HVITRMARR- NOBLESSE BLOOD APOSTLE, BLOOD DUKE|
|VERITAS: 3|
|PROVENANCE: 0|
|POTENTIA: 9|
|PONDUS: 3|
|STATUS PANEL: DAMODRED- NOBLESSE BLOOD APOSTLE, BLOOD DUKE|
|VERITAS: 3|
|PROVENANCE: 0|
|POTENTIA: 10|
|PONDUS: 3|
Noah nodded at their power and their advancements.

"As of now, I basically have a backbone of my own power and forces," he said. "This Dimension still has another Dimension fusing into it, and armies of Infinite Lifeforms remain scattered through both. I think you two would be able to take care of them, yes?"
He looked at Hvitrmarr and Damodred, and both of them nodded with immensity, the dragon’s great head dipping and the cyclops eye closing once in assent.
Then Noah’s voice went grand, and cold.

"Any who fight, kill them. Those simply living within the Dimension, and however things will be once these Dimensions finish fusing, will know that they are under a new rule. THE Ymnaros, for now, will be a base of operations. The first Dimension I will have under my rule, and protect." A pause the length of a decree being sealed. "For now, go stabilize it."
He gave the command to Hvitrmarr and Damodred, and nodded to Anaximander, who smiled wryly at having been reduced, in the span of one afternoon to a courier service. He waved his hands.
WAP!
The two of them disappeared.
Noah then turned to Ryaenara. She was already looking at him, her crimson eyes carrying utmost conviction, her hands folded before her red gold robes.
He nodded.
"Let us see about Ulf."

Times of peace were rare. Even as he moved to cover many things at once, his Provenance Essence continued its patient refining of THE Aurate Collar of the First Purity against his chest, working into bones older than frameworks, and beneath all of it his mind kept turning, constantly, on what more he could design for his own grand new system of existence.
There was so much to be done!

chapters.title: Chapter 5579: Existence Does Not Collapse!
paragraphs: <THE Creature>
The number, at this moment, stood at nine hundred and ninety nine.

THE Creature walked through the deep places of THE Ghor-Vazhal, and the deep places were veins. Tunnels of pulsing obsidian ran down and down, their walls contracting in a slow rhythm, warm underfoot, wet along their seams, and through their channels rivers of blood flowed thick and unhurried, all of it moving in one direction. He followed the direction as he knew who it would lead to!
Behind him, only corpses remained as a fiendish aura wrapped around his entire figure.
Ten minutes of the hour remained to him, and he did not hurry either.
The blood was not his. Very little of the last hour’s blood had been his!

He had walked through rivers of it. True Lifeforms of the Cultivation Farms, in their hundreds, bred and stacked and set against him in the trial’s counting, and he had borne their attacks and THE MAW had eaten what was worth eating, and the rest had gone into the rivers now keeping him company on his walk. Nine hundred and ninety nine lives lifted, and set down. One remained.
The statue spoke as he walked.
It had been silent for most of the hour. And yet now, its voice arrived the way it always arrived, from no direction.
|The coming battle will be extremely taxing and almost impossible for you. You can be given a boost to guarantee your victory... for another condition.|
THE Creature did not slow down.
"And what condition would that be?"

|Your friend. Osmont. He is also a perfect candidate to bear weight, just like you. We are interested if you steer him towards Existence as well. Only the willing may walk this path, so they can remain unfathomably true. Make the introduction. That is the only condition.|
THE Creature’s gaze went heavy.
He walked on through the pulsing vein-tunnel, blood parting around his tread, and he thought for a moment before deciding.
Then he shook his head.

"Everyone has their own weight to bear," he said. "My introduction would be me imposing that weight upon him. That is not an introduction. That is a debt, dressed as a door. If he is meant to bear the weight of Existence, he will bear it, regardless of my introduction or not."His voice did not rise. It never rose.
"Existence is vast, and existence is grand, and there are countless paths through it. Even you. Even Those Who Remain behind you. You are only grains of sand in the vastness of existence."
BOOM!
Existence shook as he said it.
The vein-tunnels seized around him, the rivers of blood jumping in their channels, the whole deep structure of THE Ghor-Vazhal trembling once!
And THE Creature could see the statue with whatever sense a bearer has for what he bears. The seated colossus, faceless and gray and worn, and across the blank stone where a face would be...smiled!
A brutal smile, wide and slow and satisfied, the smile of something that had asked its question mostly to hear this exact answer.
Then it turned silent.

THE Creature walked on, silently, and the tunnels widened as the rivers deepened, and the pulse of the walls grew slower and heavier, the rhythm of a larger heart. At the end of the last vein stood a door.

It was a door of blood and gore. Sheets of dried crimson layered over meat, arteries braided into hinges, the whole of it seamed together with the patience of something that had been building itself out of its victims for ages. Behind it, he could sense the power.
He walked through it while speaking.
"I always felt my fingers trembling, whenever I was about to face a truly fearsome enemy,"THE Creature said, to the statue, or to the door, or to no one really.

"Every time. In the early ages, when I was small, and everything above me was a weight I had not yet learned to lift. I would look at my hands, and they would tremble, and I would close them, and go forward anyway. Always...just step by step. One foot at a time. Keep moving forward."
The gore of the door parted around him, unwilling and yet obeying!
"But after so many years, they never tremble anymore. Do you know why?"
A pause, in the place where he carried the statue as its voice boomed out...
"Now," THE Creature said, "Existence itself trembles."
HUUM!
And everything began to tremble.

The door shuddered apart around his shoulders. The vein-tunnels behind him convulsed down their whole length. The domain he stepped into rippled from its floor to its distant ceiling, blood standing up in the rivers, gore shaking loose from the walls, all of it trembling at his passage the way his fingers had once trembled at everything, the debt of ages inverted and repaid in a single direction.
The domain was vast, and it was made of slaughter.

Lakes of blood spread across its floor between islands of mounded remains. Arteries thick as towers rose from the lakes and climbed through the dark air toward the far end of the domain, converging, feeding. And at the place where they all connected, fed by every vein in this deep Domain, stood the final weight.

A massive humanoid titan, mountainous in the gloom, its flesh crawling and seething where countless Gu Lifeforms had been fused into it, bodies within bodies, a colony wearing the shape of a colossus. A Primeval One!
Its murky obsidian eyes opened, and looked at THE Creature coldly, with the flat assessment of something that had ended ages and expected to end another. It opened its mouth to speak.
THE Creature shot ahead!
Existence shook all around him as he came, the lakes of blood parting in walls, the tower-arteries snapping taut, and his voice arrived ahead of his fists gloriously!
"A vile thing like you does not even deserve to converse. Fight. Either you or I will collapse here today."The distance closed to nothing!
"And...Existence does not collapse."
